Amazing massage! Very good therapists - cubicles. Work every muscle and attentive to what you ask to focus on.

I see Dr. Lingappan for my regular checkups and Dr. Patel for retinal problems. Both are very kind and caring. If you have an issue that needs immediate attention, you will get an appointment. Sometimes you have to wait because the doctor is caring for someone they had to squeeze in due to an emergency.  You will receive quality care at this practice.
Amazing pizza, the best I have ever had. However the staff is rude and the place is a mess. Order over the phone and send someone else to pick it up and you will be good.

It's ok. The men's department seems kinda small (so is the whole store) but they do have decent sales now and then. The selection of designer items is not as great here as at some of the "flagship" stores like King of Prussia or Center City Philadelphia.
I've only been once recently, but i highly enjoyed there hot braised chicken, fried rice, crab Rangoon. I will definitely go back. one of the better ones of tried in this area.

I absolutely love brunch, especially eggs, and ever since moving to Philadelphia, I've always wanted to try Green Eggs Cafe. Although my friends and I waited for 40 minutes in order to get a table (we didn't realize that it was going to be that busy), it was definitely worth the wait. I got the egg white omelette, simple but entirely delicious. The roasted vegetables and potatoes on the side were cooked and seasoned perfectly, yet I had wished they buttered the toast for me. I tried my friend's The Cure, and the mac-and-cheese really melts on your tongue.

The portions at Green Eggs are huge and definitely worth the price. My friends and I made two meals out of it (super helpful for college students kinda on a budget). The servers were incredibly nice too -- super upbeat and accommodating. Would definitely go back again!

HELPFUL TIP: They only take cash, but there's an ATM inside. I hadn't known that there was an ATM, so actually unnecessarily walked 0.5 miles to my bank's nearest ATM oops.

Attended catered party here and the food was delicious. The jalapeño poppers and cauliflower appetizers were standouts. I barely had room for the dinner tacos. Our family loved the chocolate chip (plus more additions) cookies that we gobbled as part of dessert. Beautiful setting too.
Fast, cheap, and friendly!! Theyre pretty consistent, too!

Me and 4 girlfriends were in town for a girls weekend and decided to give this place a try for a quick breakfast before the beach. The staff was amazing and so accommodating! The breakfast croissant was delicious, and they even had gluten free muffin options for one of our friends. The coffee was great with so many flavors and not too sweet. They even had matcha, which is my favorite. Highly recommend this place to anyone in the area!

This is my first yelp review because I was so disappointed that I had to comment. Went in today to get a gel manicure and pedicure. They had me sit for my manicure first which proceeded to be all of 20 minutes of the manicurist watching tv and butchering my nails. She made three of my cuticles bleed but just kept going as if nothing happened- as she's telling me to put my hand under the light, there was blood running down my nail, then would try to wipe it up with alcohol wipes. I ended up leaving without my pedicure- she never even apologized. Will not be returning.

They call this a Signature gym and charge more. For what? They get 12 channels when they are all working. Its dirty and the workers are worthless and uniformed. I have never seen a group of people care less about their jobs. Before you get a membership check around at Crunch, etc.

I've been to copper monkey several times and it seems that's it's been going downhill the post few times. I was there last night and my bartender, Marisa, seemed more concerned with smoking than providing a good customer experience. She made my Long Island incorrectly and rolled her eyes when I asked her to correct it and told her that it does not in fact include bourbon. Our food came out wrong and when I got the bill and asked why the Long Island was $11, she said it had always been that way and other bartenders must have been giving me a break. All in all a horrible experience. I'm a bartender and I would never treat a customer that way.

First of all, MOD has gluten free pizza crust, which is a huge bonus in my book. The set price for as many toppings as you want is also a huge selling point. They have a large selection of toppings and the pizza comes out quickly and is piping hot. My only complaint is that they shout at you when you walk in the door, shout when pizzas are ready, and shout just to hear themselves talk. Honestly it gave me a headache. As someone that is very sensitive to stimulation (loud music, shouting, etc), I found this aspect extremely distracting, uncomfortable, and will make me rethink coming here again in the future. It's ridiculously too much shouting and entirely unnecessary.
The only way to watch a movie, pitcher of cold beer, popcorn and food served to your table!

Finally decided to stop in for dinner.First impression, love the decor and the music is pretty cool.  The menu is very small. Chicken sandwich( ordered but didn't eat it)bone/boneless wings(boneless wings look like they are made with thigh meat)deff not chicken breast. Fries, not the crinkle fries like pictured from other reviews. Few flavors for the sauces. I had the honey garlic. It was good! Everyone at the table seemed to enjoy the different flavors so that's a plus. Chicken is CRISPY

The food was completely flavorless. I was really disappointed.

The staff gets 3.5 stars. They were kind, professional and neat.

I STRONGLY suggest a "floor monitor".  UNSUPERVISED children constantly pouring out and refilling their drink cups.

I highly doubt I would return. 

Good Luck Norristown Popeye's.

I used to use Winner parking but a few years back they had a driver who ran my BMW up on a curb when picking me up so since then I have been weary.
I liked the idea of them meeting me at the airport but the few times I tried this I would be there waiting for them while getting dirty looks from the airport personnel because I am taking us space. I get that but Winner would take a bit to find me and then for picking me up it was stressful flagging them down and finding me. Plus I would have to wait outside. 

I took a chance on this Pre Flight and LOVED it. I parked outside to be picked up instead of the garage and boom, there was a shuttle in no time. They were nice and loaded my luggage. 
Then for my pick up I walked out my terminal door and boom again there was the shuttle which was great cause it was freezing out. This will definitely be my new parking facility to use.
IT WAS AWESOME!!!!

Came here for a group lunch on a busy Thursday. Placed was packed and had a typical fast lunch atmosphere. Quickly seated and there were many good options. Started with guacamole and salsa and those were good and come with pita chips. I ordered the mixta fajitas with shrimp and steak and those were okay. Some burritos and tacos were ordered and looked great. They didn't have Diet Coke today but other subs were available. Horchata was delish!

Tacos 5/5
Burrito 5/5
Enchilada 5/5
Chips and salsa 5/5
Fajitas 2.5/5 steak was shredded and a little flavorless and shrimp wasn't at par for me.

Service quick and attentive 5/5

I'm a Chicago boy. So pizza is an important staple in my history. TennFold's pizza was fantastic! I mean fantastic. Subtle, scrumptious and inventive. It's not often I find a pizza worthy of praise. TennFold lives to the top of their game. Can't wait to go back.

Disappointing. Our group ate from all corners of the menu and everyone was underwhelmed. Everything in here is cramped and crammed together making the experience a bit of a drag. Lots of other great options nearby.
Ordered take out salads (Cobb and Mediterranean). Both were fresh and very tasty. The staff is very nice and attentive.

Service was fantastic and very knowledgeable. I and the wagyu steak and it was probably top 3 steaks I've ever had in my life. My wife had the chicken and she said it was good but nothing extraordinary.

I have been looking for some good, and affordable, gluten free pizza for quite some time so when I came here and found out that I could get a fairly large, gluten free pie for $9.95, I was floored!

The pizza did not disappoint either. The wait was only about 10 minutes, and my 8 year old niece, who is not gluten free, enjoyed it so much, that she said she wants to go back for it!

On top of that, they offer amazing truffle ice cream desserts for $5.00. At first I thought the cost for this bite sized treat was high, but I went for it anyway and the price was worth it.

The interior of the restaurant is newly renovated, and nicely done. Everything is clean, and new, and the staff is friendly and kind.

I think I found my new go to pizza place! :)
Atmosphere was warm, food was great. Salads and small plates are the targets for this menu!

My toes and fingers are so happy after the service they've received at this nail salon. My husband and I went there today to get our pedicures and I wanted my finger nails painted too. Beautiful space! We both got their "Deluxe pedicure" ($35 each). It was so nice and relaxing. Our nail techs were a hoot! It was so nice talking to them both. Complimentary mimosas were fantastic. I love that they use organic products. The whole experience was top notch. I will most definitely recommend this place to all of my friends.

The pros: the food is great and consistently good. They have a unique selection and the brunch is always good. The cons: the seating arrangement is stressful due to how crammed it can get and the chairs are really uncomfortable and awkward.
In town for a wedding. The staff was super friendly room was comfortable and clean and it was easy to find. All kinds of eateries very close. Hotel is located on the main road through town.

Worst Taco Bell I have ever visited.  Waited 10 min in drive thru just to place a small order.  Then waited another 10 min in line to get the order.  Avoid this place if at all possible.  Horrible situation!  Rating should be 0 !!!! Not good

So, I own a family restaurant in the Philadelphia area, so maybe this is going to sound harsher than it should, but as someone in the industry I guess I'm just trying to hold the rest of the locations up to the standard that we try to live up to. I ordered a to go order from grub burger bar and I got there early in order to be there as soon as the order was ready so that I could take it home and eat it hot, because I understand that to go orders for burgers can be a little tricky. I entered the location, gave my name to the staff, paid, and was told to wait and that I would be called.  No one called, and I guess maybe I should have been on top of the staff, but my back was kind of to them and I just took them at their word that they would call me once the one and only to go order in the place was ready. At any rate, I turn around some 15 minutes later to see a to go bag with my name on it. "How long has this been sitting here," I ask. No one knows.  Forgot to call me I guess. Anyway, I'm out the door and home soon after. But a lukewarm burger is not my the only problem.  I may have to come and show you the staff what Medium means in terms of cooking a burger.  I had to take my burger off the bun and give it a quick turn on the stove top, it was so red in the middle.  Barely rare.  Bad experience. All in all, next time I'll opt for a non chain burger spot with some organization and management that takes pride in their work.

This place is fantastic! Live bands, great jukebox, and awesome food! The whole place was recently renovated including the upstairs which is the perfect place to host a party. I recently attended a party in the upstairs and had an amazing time. The food catered by the bar was a taco buffet including homemade salsas and amazing carne asada that rivals the best on Cherokee street! The location is super convenient when going to Cardinals games, Blues games and any other downtown event. They even have a shuttle for blues games now too!

Had the day off, mid week and was looking for a quick bite while running errands. I've had Trios before, at a friends' house but had never been inside the joint. It's clean, attractive and encourages you to sit and scarf down your pizza (sometimes those slice places make you want to take your food and run!).  It's a great addition to Girard Ave which needs some love.

I go here for breakfast a bunch. They open at 9am and there are always people in there. its a nice way to start your day... watching the news, eating some delicious Pho. I love the location too because I can do my grocery shopping also since its in the same strip mall as the market. 
The staff is crazy fast and super nice! Very affordable and filling.

Jacek does make some wonderful chocolates, and it's certainly worth a visit to check it out. They have seasonal features, which you can also buy at Credo next door, and they also do fun things for holidays. 

I've grown to love their chocolate bars, my favourites being the Cocoa (milk chocolate topped with white chocolate) and the Jackie (caramelized milk chocolate with fleur de sel). 

The individual chocolates are really works of art. Jacek has some of the most unique flavour combinations I've come access at a Chocolatier, and there are new flavours for every season.

If you are looking for a unique gift, or to just satisfy an expensive sweet tooth, then definitely check out Jacek!

We've been here a lot. It's our go to bar at home (outside of Philadelphia). The food is always really good. The drinks are good for the price. I myself like beer more than mixed drinks because I find it's a better deal than mixed drinks anywhere, so this is a great place for me. 

They always have pretty good beer. They always have the mainstream cheap beers (Coors Light, Miller Light, Blue Moon, etc.) on tap with a rotating selection of craft beers (my favorite). Although recently they've had quite a lot of Ballast Point, which I'm less fond of. It's all good, though. They're more fair with their higher abv drafts, offering 12oz pours instead of 10oz like in the city (it makes a difference). I'm pretty sure Dogfish Head Olde School, a more expensive 15%, was only 10oz, though, but the 12oz Ballast Point was 12%.

The food's always excellent for the suburbs, but very good compared to bars in the city. I've had burgers, crab cakes, French Onion Soup, and probably more if I'm forgetting. 

So far I think these are the best burgers in the area. The French onion soup is my favorite dish from here. Its even comparable to some Philly restaurants I've been to. The crab cakes are better than area chain sports bars who specialize in crabs (if you know what I mean), but I'm not gonna go ahead and say it's the best I've ever had.

The only bone to pick I have is for their $5 burger night. They make the burgers a lot smaller and don't include fries. Do they know the point of specials like this is to bring in customers and not make more money? If you're going to make smaller patties, at least include fries!

Just had the most unfortunate experience at a favorite family place we've been enjoying for over 15 years. The manager was incredibly rude just because we asked for a different table to practice social distancing. He berated the nice people sitting down already for agreeing with us, and offered to sit us outside. He was obnoxious, disrespectful and downright mean. After that kind of treatment we decided to walk out instead. We'll miss Italian Affair. They have lost a life long customer. I feel very bad for the family he yelled at too. Very unfortunate. We had 3:30 reservations on Dec 19th.

I live out of the area, but whenever I am in town to visit family, this is one of my go-tos. The food is amazing, and the cocktails are great. It's a little on the pricier side, but the food is never disappointing. 

Some of my favorite things here:
-The Flamestone 21 cocktail is a fantastic, smoky (literally!) take on the bourbon old fashioned. I've seen the gimmick of capturing smoke in a glass and preparing it tableside elsewhere, but this was the first place I experienced it years ago.

-Flamestone Salad (with your choice of meat, I prefer rare steak) is a delectable mix of greens with sweet cranberries and walnuts and that kick of Bleu cheese. You can't go wrong with this one. It all just plays so well together.

Guacamole prepared tableside. This ensures freshness, a key ingredient for guac. What makes this one slightly different from most places is that they use jalapenos instead of cumin. Different, but delicious.

All together, the food and ambience is great. It's a classy, upscale casual joint.
They have the best blueberry cheesecake ice cream! Oh, their other flavors are really good too!

This place is soooooo dangerous!!!

How can you pass up a buy 1 get 2 free deal?  At the very least you have to take a look.  I walked out with $400 worth of boots for $200.

These aren't cheesy boots either.  Sure they have the gaudy boots, but they also have regular boots as well.  They also have all of the name brands.  You are just at the mercy of what they have.  

The first time I was here, I picked up a pair for me, my sister, and a friend of mine.  The pair for my friend dosen't fit her, but with the Exchange Only policy I won't have a problem fixing the issue.  As long as it's the same model boot they have no issues switching them out.  

Now that I'm back here in Nashville, I need to ensure that I stay away or I'll end up going home with 3 pairs of boots I don't really need, but want.
Very responsible manager. Solve problems for you, even during weekends. Willing to cater to individual needs of the tenants. Responsive in replying emails. Highly recommended!!

I would save your money! Not sure if different therapist very in their procedure but I enede up with more of a physical therapy session ie. Stretching my limbs rather that a massage.  The actual massage part was on one body part and lasted about 10min of an hour deep tissue massage! Also there was a buzzing noise going on the entire time of my massage! My expectations were a little higher I guess.

Sam Levitz gave me and my family the worst exsperience ever from a furniture store We will never return and make sure every one knows what liars they are .My husband and I spent 3 hours there trying to pick out furniture we both could agree on and a tv stand well our salesman "David" who was just worried about the commission he would make off of us told us these items were in stock because I wanted in stock items only! We went through quite a few couches and TV stands to find in-stock items that would be delivered in 2 days, well delivery  day comes no one has called to give us an approximate time they would be coming so my husband calls and say they cant find our order. Then they get "David"on the phone who ends up hanging up on my husband so I end up calling to talk to a manger they give me "Ian" who says he is sorry but could really care less and says there is  no TV stand or couches coming because there on back order for a few weeks! At this point I'm furious I had already got ride of my old couches  and have no furniture in my home I decide Im going down there, when I get there Ian and David are outside looking like they are trying to leave after I said Im going down there right away well "Ian" try to fix it by giving me $50.00 off my order that was over $1500.00 so at this time iI was beyond insulted he told me he had nothing to give me and that was the best he could do, David admitted the items he told us were in stock were actually not but thought they would come in by delivery time which is so unacceptable he flat out lied to us to get his commission while my kids have nothing at home to sit on and my Tv is on the floor .To top it off I want my money back and the girl at the desk is so rude like its her $1500.00 Im asking for. I ended up calling the main manger a few days later which he was very nice and seemed to make things right his offer was $50 off the TV stand free delivery which was about $40 and $50 off the couches I was still not happy with the offer and decided to go else where and got what I wanted and ended up saving about $600 so I just wanted to share my disgusting experience and hope I help some one choose another store thats not owned by sam levitz. I was very unsatisfied with the customer service so much that I left the store in tears.

The selection was huge, well-organized, and high quality. Everything was a bargain, and I got a 3.5 yard remnant for $11. I re-covered my kitchen chairs and know this fabric will withstand messy eaters and active cats. 

The staff was friendly and helpful; I'll definitely be back the next time I need fabric!
I love this place ! It's my new nail shop. My nails are absolutely perfect. Best experience ever. The workers are also super nice !

They were understanding and quick to respond on the offer for my car. They offered a couple grand more than any dealership and we're very eager to get my vehicle and check in hand. I highly recommend them!

Quality pizza and food. The restaurant is very casual. If you are looking for a more intimate restaurant recommend going to Vetri. This was perfect for dinner (or lunch) after a day of shopping and wandering the city. The wait staff is extremely friendly and helpful. The service is quick and they do a great job clearing the tables. For three people, we got the Caesar salad to start. The Caesar is excellent and classic. The dressing is homemade and lettuce was fresh. 

We then shared two pizzas, the fig and prosciutto (seasonal) and the sausage. Recommend the both though i really liked the figs. 

Great place to stop by for a quick bite. The bar menu is also excellent and have a good happy hour special!

If you are in NOLA and need a place to watch sports, this is your jam.  On a Sunday during football with three different fan bases in six people, we needed somewhere that would have all three games on.  We were staying down the block so this was an obvious choice.  The hostess was amazing.  She got all six of us in at a table within 20 minutes and the place was packed.  They literally had every football game on as well.  Crystal was our server and she was really good and super friendly.  We had already eaten but got a few snacks.  The fried pickles had a good texture but they were bread and butter pickles as opposed to dill.  I thought they could use some tang and were a bit too sweet.  The bayou chips were just eh.  Nothing was really integrated so you didn't get all the tasty items in most bites.  Not that I expected it, but they don't have good wine.  The drinks were pretty average; I thought the hurricane was too sweet and couldn't finish it.  Overall a great place to watch a game but the food and drinks were a bit lacking.

Maybe I'm spoiled by NYC restaurants, maybe it was an off night, or maybe it just isn't THAT good. Sorry, I just wasn't that impressed by Bern's Steakhouse (I'm talking the actual restaurant, not the Dessert Room, which I will get to later).

First of all, upon arrival we discovered that valet parking is mandatory. There was a huge sign that specifically said it costs $5 NOT including tip (so tacky). We were annoyed that despite the inevitability that we would be spending a ton of money on our meal, we would have to tack on an additional $5 for something that should be complimentary. It's Tampa, not NYC. I'm sure parking isn't that difficult.

Inside is really cool. Definitely unlike other steakhouses. Red lights and antique feel. I felt like I was in another era. We were seated in the almost-empty Florentine Room. Our waitress introduced herself and the menu. The menu is like a novel. When I go out to eat, I want to be attended to. I don't want to think. I want to relax. Too many options from sizes, to thickness of cuts, to temperature...it was just all unnecessary.

We started with a bread basket and Tuna Tartare (Sushi quality tuna, hand-diced and dressed with Asian spices, soy wasabi dashi, wasabi tobiko, wonton crisps). This was VERY fresh, but lacked flavor.

The sorta good thing is that every dish comes with a house salad with choice of dressing, a small portion of French onion soup, onion rings, baked potatoes with chives and bacon, and 2 vegetables (changes daily). The salad and soup came first then the steak (Chateau Briand cut) and vegetables. The French Onion Soup was really good and I was actually appreciative of the smaller portion as it would be way too filling as a regular size. The steak and sides then came out. The steak was cooked well but did not have any special flavor. The sides were so dull looking and tasting-spinach and carrots.

We then asked for the tour and a table in the Harry Waugh Dessert Room.

We were escorted to the kitchen where our tour started and continued through the epic wine cellar. Our guide was very enthusiastic, much more so than our waiter was. It was interesting to hear about the history and contents of the Steakhouse. I almost wish we had done the tour before dinner, we saw a lot of dishes being made that we would have liked to try.

Then the Dessert Room. It is upstairs but has a separate reservation desk. We were seated in an old-school booth with a retro phone and mini juke box. You could play live music or pick something else. The menu was vast as well but somehow less annoying than downstairs. 

We had:
Chocolate-Chocolate-Chocolate, Classic (Layers of our chocolate cheese pie, chocolate cheesecake, and milk chocolate mousse on a dense chocolate crust. Served with fresh whipped cream and milk chocolate shavings)
Trio of Liquid Center Cakes (Mini dark chocolate cake, dulce de leche center with banana caramel ice cream. Mini chocolate cake, 
praline hazelnut center with Caramélia crunch ice cream. Mini chocolate cake, white chocolate center paired with vanilla bean ice cream).

Both were unbelievable. Rich, decadent, and absolutely scrumptious. Just what we needed after a lackluster dinner.

So, this is getting an average of 4 stars...3 for the steakhouse and 5 for the Dessert Room. Next time I'm in town, I would skip dinner there all together and go straight for dessert.

Nothing special.  They have had pretty much the same menu for 20 years. You know what you are going to get. Got their lunch house low mien.   (Noodles. A piece of chicken, a price of beef and a few shrimps). This time asked for it spicy. Enjoyed it. Cannot beat the price and value. Comes with tea. Soup.

I wish I could give this company ZERO stars.  I purchased a deal for 2 hour house cleaning over Living Social.  I called the company, and left a voicemail informing them I would like to redeem my coupon.  They NEVER called me back.  So I called again.  And left ANOTHER voicemail.  Again, they NEVER called me back.  What's the definition of insanity?  Trying something 3 times and expecting a different outcome?  I won't even bother calling them again because they probably will never call back.  Don't waste your time or money with this unreliable company.

Mandarin Hide used to be DTSP's best kept secret.  An unmarked wooden door on Central Ave. near the Detroit marked a new destination for the city and slowly people caught on...and kept catching on...and now it's the most popular bar in DTSP. 

Unfortunately, it's small so the experience is not quite as enjoyable as it used to be, but the drinks are very solid and it is a fun place to be.  I like to hang out on the back porch, where there is a smaller bar with less people and you can hear the music at Jannus if someone is there that night.  

If you are in the mood for a classy night out and want to start or finish here, this is a great bet.

I have used chiropractors for over a decade. I've been treated by about 5 or 6 over that time.

During my visit, Dr. M pinpointed my issue within 20 seconds of me hitting the table. And minutes later, she had my L4 back to where it should be. I am walking upright again. Thanks. 

Also, the location is nice and clean and well organized. I really like that they are open on the weekends so I can get some relief if I need an adjustment that day.

Fantastic tour!!! We went on the "Pirates and Booty" tour with Christie and it was a phenomenal experience. The guide knew exactly where to take us and we got to explore some great hidden gems. Christie was charismatic and accommodated our requests. We paid $25 each and visited... 5 bars? Maybe six. They were all different types of establishments and came with great stories! We had the opportunity to purchase drinks everywhere we went (including absinthe) but were never pressured to do so. Christie knew where free water was served too, so we all stayed hydrated. We would definitely recommend this tour for couples looking for a fun night in New Orleans! 

**This tour does mostly take place in and around Bourbon Street at night, so if that's not your thing then you might want to look for a more family-friendly tour.

Wouldn't stay here again. Great service which is very important but the rooms are so dated. It's like stepping foot into a 80's Miami Beach hotel. As a gold member, who always chooses Hilton properties, this has been my least favorite. This place needs a huge makeover. But I have to say PJ who works with maintenance was super cool and very helpful. We had an event at their meeting room and everyone was very helpful but the meeting room is in dire need of a makeover. Walmart is about 5 minutes away. Beach is about 5 miles. Plenty of food places within 5-10 minute drive.

Creme brûlée is out of this world! The torching is so easy to mess up but the one here has a perfectly thin, hard crust with a soft rest of the dessert. It also didn't taste like pudding/custard (which is good!) Great service too and my friends loved their actual food. I had dental surgery that day and the waitstaff recommended the creme brûlée which I'm glad I had- will have to try the other dishes at this cute French place!

This branch is two blocks off of City Avenue and Conshohocken State Road (corner of the two "battling Sunocos", lol). Although, according to demographics, I have a post office within my own zip code...I go out of my way to visit this location. I used to love it because there were these cute older white male clerks there. They were so friendly and would get you taken care of quickly...especially the one with the ponytail :)

I suppose they've retired because I haven't seen them in a while. However, the new clerks are very friendly and efficient as well. They have a self-service center, P.O. Boxes, greeting cards, as well as all of the other standard postal services. Going here on a repeated basis tends to make me feel that the government is not as convoluted as it often seems....ok maybe not....and let's face it, nobody really enjoys going to a post office. It's a kind of necessary evil, but there's definitely nothing evil about this place.
Fun spot! You have to wait for a spot at the carousel but it's totally worth it. We had Cucumber Collins which were great but a bit sweet. Fun for a quirky drink while in the French quarter!

Huge disappointment.  Went in Saturday night at about 8:00 p.m. There were more staff than customers - only four customers, counting ourselves.  The atmosphere is kinda dank and the decor is dingy and cluttered.  Our waitress was super friendly and very attentive.  

Our sides were just OK, nothing special.  The BBQ sauce itself was *very* good.  We both got pork steaks, and they were very overdone - dry and tough, and hard to cut.  They should have been fork-tender.  No smoke flavor, either.  When we paid, and were asked "how was it?" I was honest and said I was disappointed, and told them about the dry, tasteless, tough pork steaks.  The young man's reply?  "Really?  That's all I've been selling all night, and no one's complained."  Not even a feeble "sorry 'bout that."  

When the customer doesn't like what they've shelled out their hard-earned money for, money that could have been better spent elsewhere, you don't dispute their opinion - you offer a heartfelt apology and maybe, just maybe, you consider that your food could have been better.  I think the owners should consider that there's a problem with their food, as evidenced by the sparsity of customers on a summer Saturday evening.  

Although I live just a few blocks away, and have been several times (but not in a couple of years), I won't be back.  There are better places with better food where I can spend my money.

Overly hyped, over-priced and disorganized.

First off...I agree with others who have said their mac 'n cheese is bland, runny and the macaroni was texture-less and overcooked. We even waited for a fresh batch...but we'll discuss that later.

We went on a Saturday rush on an opening day of an "annual" auto show and Delilah and her staff were not prepared for the rush.  We were waiting in line for their mac 'n cheese but they were out. They told a few of us to wait to the side and that it would be an additional 20 mins.  When there was a fresh batch, they began serving the incoming line.  The side line (which they created for those waiting for the mac 'n cheese) began to complain and in the confusion they just consolidated the line and asked the side line to go back in line in the back so we had to wait again.  We got the combo platter which was over priced for $13 for a side of mac n cheese, collard greens and a thigh-leg fried chicken...plus they were out of corn bread. 

I hate to say it but I've had better mac 'n cheese from a food truck.  Their collard greens were ok but nothing impressive to make it stand out.  Their fried chicken was lightly battered and juicy and it was their saving grace  of the combo imo. 

I'd like to hope this was an isolated incident...but on a Saturday rush and a trade show that comes annually, I'd hoped they would have expected the high volume.  I would go back to see if this experience is the norm or the exception.

I'm super excited for this new, cozy (and healthy) spot to join the Indy neighborhood! The inside is gorgeous, the staff were incredibly friendly and helpful (they anticipated every single need - it was impressive!) and I'm excited to come back soon. 

I visited during lunch and got a big plate of butternut squash and a chicken gyro in pita with brussels around it. I love how you can choose your meal, exactly how you want it. The menu works by you choosing how many sides you want to make up your meal. There are also some full entree meals you can choose from if you don't want to get crafty in choosing your own combos. You order at the counter and can visually see all the options (which I promise will make your mouth water). You then pay and they bring the food out to you.

The seating area is large and I love the design. There are supercool lighting fixtures and I loved the patterned benches. The benches were super cozy and I can picture coming back for brunch or to study with some great tea/coffee. 

This place can be a bit pricey if you come for an entire meal ($15+) for lunch, but the food you're receiving is very high quality and I also got a decent portion size that I had leftovers. The coffee is also fairly priced so definitely a good spot to come with friends. 

Excited to have another Public Greens!

Came in today for the first time for lunch with my family. We ordered a variety of entrees, including pasta, pizza & paninis.  We then got a chocolate chip cookie for dessert. Everything was delicious & our server Katherine was fantastic! We will definitely be back!

Food was good, portions were good, price was a little high. Overall I found it good enough to add this place to my Saturday lunch rotation. Then a note on the door said temporarily closed because they were out of Fish. Then the next week the sign said the owner had gout. Then the next sign said FOR LEASE. Sorry to say they didn't make it. Now permanently closed.

Indeed, as the other reviewers have described, the ambiance here is incredible. Great music, fantastic wines, wafting scent of jasmine and citrus from the trees surrounding the dining area, and fire pits on the tables. And while the food is fantastic (although do prepare yourself for mucho garlic) and the wait staff friendly and professional, it's the dining under the stars in a completely romantic outdoor setting that takes the proverbial cake. Oh, and it doesn't hurt to share the experience with a lovely friend, either.

I purchased the beginners blacksmith class for my husband as a Christmas gift. Working with Robert through email and phone was great! He provided thorough information to make sure I was making the correct purchase for my husband and was pleasant to speak with. 

My husband had nothing but great things to say about his experience. He loved the one on one teaching and the fact that was able to forge/create his own " Crocodile Dundee style knife ". 

Thanks for the wonderful memories!

Overall, very disappointed. Expected more from such a high Yelp rating with many reviews. The crawfish cake appetizers were fantastic and so flavorful. I wish it had been an entire entree because it was heads above our entrees.
Seafood pasta mix- typical seafood mix with a tomato sauce. Not much flavor.
Shrimp n Grits- very plain and bland. I've made better shrimp n grits at home. Very disappointing.

Let my start off by saying I'm allergic to all kinds of fish. I know what you're thinking. "Why are you reviewing a sushi place?" Well, my friend convinced me to go here and get something fish free. 

I got the dumplings which were GREAT and I would definitely get again. I also got there lunch orange chicken bento box. Not a huge fan of tempura vegetables personally, and the chicken wasn't the best - meat wasn't fresh and it was drenched in sauce. I'd probably just order something else next time.

My friend got a lot of food that looked really good and she seemed to enjoy. Overall, decent for some cheap and edible food.

Great place with great potential. Best part was the service. Our server was fast and polite. Maybe because we were the only ones in the place but either way - he rocked. Food was average. Nothing special. Nothing unique. Only one side for entrees - 2 seems normal. 

We went because of the games - cornhole, darts, shuffle board. Great set up but missed the mark with the little things. No chalk for scorekeeping darts and one of dart boards was loose. Cornhole bags were missing one of the colors and also missing another whole set. Only one board could be used with makeshift bags. 

This could be a 5 star place. Maybe they don't have people play games but we made the most of it and had fun.

I went to Jasmine Rice on Wednesday for restaurant week. The restaurant was packed but we were seated right away. There was only one server working that night so it took a bit to get our food HOWEVER that did not detract from our experience. The staff offered us a complimentary dish to apologize for the wait which was really nice. I will definitely be back when restaurant week is over!

Primo Bacio is located in a giant apartment complex known as The Towers At Wyncote.  I'm not sure if there is good signage to point the way within the complex, because as a passenger I wasn't paying attention, but I imagine it is a little hard to find if you don't know where you are going.

Although Primo is not a great restaurant, is it a very good value for the price, at least at lunch.  You get nice decor, waiters, tablecloths and a decent lunch for about $8.  The fare is generic, including pasta, burgers, sandwiches and salads.  I went with a group from work and I think it was a good choice for that type of situation - everyone will be able to find something they'll be happy with.  Beyond that, the place is nothing special, and I probably wouldn't choose it for going out with my wife or friends.

I came to this place today,  and honestly really wasn't all that! I mean food was ok tasting but really didn't quite do it for me....food was warm not hot! Place looked dirty, seats and tables were old seats at the booth were ripped. My omelette was really grease! Service was ok but a long wait to get your food!

Okay, so I would have been happy to give this mall four stars for their otherwise great selection of stores. However, their staff and some of their policies are not conducive to happy shopping. And, when I say staff, I really mean the security bouncer guys.

I have continued to come here because it's convenient, but other than that, it isn't a place I would.  Theirs shops are absolutely great stores and the workers at the stores are extremely helpful.  I had people help me pick out suits, presents for my family, and the frequently remember their shoppers and honestly go out of the way to help their customers.

The one part of this mall that drives me crazy is are the bouncer's at almost every entrance. I frequently feel like I'm an underaged high schooler trying to sneak into a club instead of coming here to shop. I absolutely hate their policy on carding "younger" looking shoppers. The official policy is that shoppers under 17 cannot shop without a guardian over 21. Yes, it gets so ridiculous that they will card twenty something year olds and harass you until they know you're old enough to shop. Isn't this a little ridiculous for a mall?  I wouldn't have as much of a problem if they only did this during school hours, but they only do this on nights and weekends.  If the mall is already crowded and if "kids" aren't supposed to be in school, why slow people down and card everyone who shows up under 30? Also, if this were an just a once-a-visit kind of thing, I wouldn't have as much of a problem.  If frequently have been carded three or four times in the middle of a mall trip.  And, yes, it's so crazy that they will make you put down all your bags and fumble around for an ID. Other than that, I really do like this mall. I just really wish they didn't make it such a pain to shop here.

Everything about Amis was perfect. We didn't have a reservation and the hosts got us seats at the chefs bar looking in at the kitchen-which turned out to be the absolute best place to sit. The service was fantastic from start to finish. The meatballs were the best I've ever had. We got the lamb and the wheat pasta with brisket ragu which were both delicious. The carrot cake was heaven and the lemon cookies melted in your mouth. This was our first time in Philly, but we will be back, if not only for Amis.

What an awesome way to spend a few hours in Nashville. This was by far the coolest thing we did for my friend's Bachelorette Bash in Nash last weekend. We had thirteen girls and thought a pedal tour would be a super cool way to explore the downtown area of Nashville led by someone who knows the area well. Rain or shine they said. Well, they weren't kidding. Sunday morning we woke up and it was a torrential downpour. To be honest, couldn't imagine us doing a pedal tour in the rain and thought for sure we would be told it was canceled once we showed up, but we did it and holy heck it was a freakin' blast.

Quick note: We start at the Nashville Pedal Tavern home base, which is  a store kind of because they sell Nashville Pedal Tavern apparel, hats, koozies, ponchos, etc. The stuff they sell is pretty great, the girls were super cool, long sleeve, short sleeve, tanks, tees and they were super soft. They sold some really cool hats in various colors (black, red, white, gray) that said NASH on them and so us gals bought a bunch, maybe 8 of us purchased $34 caps. Additionally we all bought ponchos, a few of us bought koozies, oh and we were also about to embark on our pedal tour meaning we were all paying for the experience as well. Point of me saying this is after the group of 13 dropped $300 plus on souvenirs and then hundreds more on the tour itself, the girl behind the counter left a real bad taste in my mouth. They had sample hats out for people to try on, the hats were loaded with face makeup, bent in weird ways, hence why they were the sample hats. Each of the girls who got their hat received a new one from the back. However, when I went to buy my hat, the girl took the tag off the sample one, which had other peoples' makeup in it. I asked her for a fresh one (like everyone else got) and she actually gave me a hard time for it. Literally couldn't believe how she handled the situation after how much money we all just dropped. Not cool. Also, when I showed the Yelp check in get a free koozie, a different girl was hesitant about giving me a cheap $2.50. Again, not cool.

Enough about that though, our tour guide Dan was DA bomb. He knew how to make us completely forget we were being poured on. He was upbeat, funny, loud, theatrical. An entertainer if you will. He grabbed us new drinks from our cooler whenever we were running low. He kept our drinks on ice while we were inside the bar to make sure they stayed cold. He let us play Celine Dion music and let us sing at the top of our lungs in unison. This was the best part of our trip and he made the experience quite memorable for us all. He went over all of the rules of the bike to ensure our safety and we appreciated that. We did red light socials and waved to people on the streets as they took our photo. We pulled over right on the river to take photos. We stopped at four different bars and he gave us thorough explanations about what each bar served in terms of their specialty drink or shot. Even though we were soaking wet, we had the time of our lives. The music was loud, the drinks were flowing and I can't remember laughing so hard. We stopped at Swinging Doors Saloon, Doc Holidays, Headquarters Beercade, that may have been it, so maybe 3 bars. At Swinging Doors Saloon they had beer specials and vodka specials, Doc Holidays had an orange juice shot and Headquarters Beercade had the most unbelievably sinfully delicious peanut butter and jelly shot. We were dropped off near Broadway wishing we had more time on the pedal tour. One thing to say, you actually have to pedal. I was definitely breaking a sweat, no joke. Highly recommend this to anyone traveling to Nashville, would totally do this with strangers too, it's so much fun and request Dan!!

They must have been on happy pills when I first visited. When I returned they (vets) acted like I was a diva for asking questions and being concerned about my beloved. Don't really want to go back but don't want to start over somewhere new either.
Authentic Italian food and amazing service.  I feel like I'm in Venice again.  Will definitely be back again.

Franks pizza is the best in the area. We first tried it after another local pizza place changed their recipe and haven't stopped ordering from here since! It's not fancy gourmet but definitely delicious and reasonably priced. Their milkshakes are thick and taste like they are from the ice cream shop too!

Had jury duty. A day of waiting around. The one bright spot was lunch.  Wandered down the road and found this place. Go with the lunch specials... 2 slices of cheese and a drink for $5 or $6.  The cheese slice was greasy but good. Definitely have to fold this slice or it's going to spill onto your shirt. I made the mistake of having the lasagne pizza.  It looked great, but it was just bland. The garlic knot was definitely good.  And they read my mind, was wanting an ice cream and they had a great peanut butter cup gelato.  The pizza was much better than Paci's but not as good as Grimaldi's.

Everything here was really yummy! I'm glad I came in during happy hour! Their Johnny Sanchez Margarita was custom made since I cannot do tequila. For starters their chips and salsa was Delicious with  their warm tortilla and plantain chips. Their crispy Brussels sprouts  for starters had butternut squash, cotija, and jalapeño vinaigrette is very filling! For the main course they recommended the soft shell crab torta that has coleslaw, avocado and a vinaigrette served on a lightly toasted bun.   The staff was great! Everything was delicious!

This theater has vegan options for dinner, and the movie popcorn and even the "butter" are vegan too. The dinner options were really small and over-priced but it's worth it for the movie date night experience. You can order stuff on a little tablet thing and they'll bring it out to you during the film. Pretty cool!

Portions were big!  Price was very affordable!  It was very tasty - I usually order one without cheese so I can taste the meat better.  Tried it a couple of times and both times were consistent.  Minor complaint was that the bread was a bit soggy, even after making the second order toasted. Next one, I'll request it "less soggy" hehehe.

The food was exceptional.  Portions are on the smaller side, but it is definitely a case of quality over quantity.  The garden and the different interior areas are very different from each other, but all very nice and enjoyable.

Very frustrating experience.   Went into dealership with email quote for both new car (USAA TrueCar) and trade-in (Trade-in Valet) from the dealership and when we arrived we were told the Trade-in Valet email was in error and they could not honor.  Price offered was less than lowest range of trade-in quote ($14K - range quoted was $15.1K-$17.6K which was quoted  "This is a guaranteed offer").  We left, went to another dealership down the street and they offered us a check on the spot for the trade-in which was reasonable (and ironically was within Wolfe's Trade-In Valet trade-in range - $15.5K).  Great!   Went back to the dealership a few days later and said, ok, trade-in is now out of the picture lets move forward with the True-Car discount (note I said discount as any additional options can increase price) .   Salesman, Daniel,  went off for a while and came back with a discount not matching that of the email on an exactly comparable car (i.e. same options).  Now he said the email True-Car discount received from FJ (works for Wolfe) also was in error and they would not honor - difference of about $1500 on a $49K Highlander Limited Platinum.  It was even more frustrating that we let Daniel know as soon as we walked in we wanted the TrueCar DISCOUNT quoted from FJ and he let us wait almost an hour while he searched for a car, checked options and quoted us a delivery date before letting us know they would not honor the previously quoted discount.  We left frustrated we wasted  our time and gave the dealership a second chance.  Very bad experience.  We really wanted to do business as they were our local Toyota dealership.  How can we?
Cool place! The staff seem willing to help both pros and novices alike, which is a great thing.

On a business trip in Carmel, really wanted a salad bar, I don't like prepared salads. The hotel recommended Jason's Deli. Spot on! I made my salad from the salad bar and ordered half a turkey sandwich. It was yummy. Great menu selection. Great service, I got there around 8pm tonight and the place was empty. The young lady Alanna was very helpful and sweet. I am probably going back tomorrow evening. Yup I went back for more of the salad bar.

Work party review!

When I first heard that my branch of Whole Fooods was gearing up to throw its annual store party at the Yards Brewing Company I was popping and locking like Carlton (http://youtu.be/zS1cLOIxsQ8). Especially when I factored in things like the special open bar rate and free brewery tours that it would offer. And n the end I got an awesome package from the spot that provided my first ever real taste of Philly beer (despite it separating from its brotherhood of PBC in a Twix Factory moment).

Yards gave our group the flexibility to do things like bring our own food spread and post up special raffle prizes for team members to win. And the open bar package that they offered gave whomever wanted to opportunity to enjoyed as many brews from their signature offerings, Ales of the Revolution series, and what limited batches they had on tap for just $27. So when I wasn't savoring the smoothness of the Bourbon Spruce and infinite power of the Grand Cru, I was kicking it with Poor Richard and a Brawler.

Despite our tour guide being a wee bit tipsy for the circumstances, and out of practice in giving tours by a couple months; he managed to offer an informative and interesting tour of the brewery vicinity. It was especially interesting to hear that the warehouse used to maintain an old indoor skate park while checking the remnants of the street art within.

The tour and brew left enough whimsy to merit another visit, possibly even during a UYE. Especially when their tasting room features a menu of  offerings made with ingredients from farmers that they exchange their leftover grains with like buffalo chili and fresh baked goods.
It was our first time here today. The food was delicious - they have the best pancakes!! The service was fast and friendly. We felt very welcome! Can't wait to come back.

Very impressed with this place. It's a relaxing atmosphere and they take their time to get things done right the first time. Prices are reasonable as well! Call ahead to make an appointment they're usually pretty busy.

Food was cold when it arrived, my friends order was not even correct, when mentioned , server brought wrong dish, upon mentioning again he brought side dish, which was total bummer. The restaurant was cold the heat was not working, too uncomfortable to sit there and eat in 30 degrees. In end we decided to order gulab jamun, we asked for the plates to eat, instead of bringing extra plates , he brought one more gulab jamun dish , horrible customer service.

Stowers used to be known for wonderful caring staff, but not anymore. They pushed me to sign up for meetings with staff, with no reason given at the time.  These meetings turned out to be a sales pitch to but funeral services. Also the manager on staff that day was rude by insinuating I might not come back to pick up my father's ashes, because he'd seen a lot of that lately. He made me say it twice that I would come and pick up the ashes. Also..they charge twice as much for basic cremation than other nearby funeral homes.

I have been doing yoga off and on for close to 40 years and more frequently since my recent retirement. I have been to many wonderful and not so wonderful studios throughout the country.  Yoga Garden is truly exceptional in terms of the teachers, environment, spirit and community. Mark and Nikki are extremely knowledgeable about yoga and physiology and bring great skill and every day wisdom to their classes. All of the teachers are trained, prepared, and committed to teaching and growing their practice. I have gone to many gentle and all levels classes and have enjoyed many different teachers and have never been disappointed. I love the full schedule of classes that presents numerous opportunities to find a class. Finally, I'm am continually impressed how the Yoga Garden welcomes students of all ages and abilities. They are able to effectively support folks regardless of whether it is their first class or their daily routine, whether they are an an athlete and/or dealing with injuries or physical challenges. I am grateful to have found this yoga home.

We came here for my birthday lunch!  Woohoo!  It was a Saturday around noon and there were just a handful of patrons, so in my mind that's a plus.  It's a counter order, like most good BBQ spots in St. Louis, with a modern design and friendly. helpful staff.  I like that it has its own parking lot - unexpected in the Grove.

I had the pulled pork and wagyu brisket.  These were both highlighted on an article I read that mentioned the high quality of the meat.  My assessment:  I have to agree the quality was high and pretty special.   The wagyu didn't quite have as much flavor as I mght have hoped, but it was very tender.   I wasn't such a big fan of it being served with a tortilla instead of some kind of bun.  Original, but just not my favorite.  

I really loved the texas and "very hot" sauces that were available.   For sides I had bacon mac and chees and baked beans.  The mac was really cheesy, but not a very bold flavor.  The beans were excellent. 

This place should be on your list if you are a BBQ lover.
It's a bit on the expensive side, and the killer is that they charge extra if you want ice in your bar beverage.

This is the best mall.  I moved away from the area for a few years and missed the great shopping terribly.  It gets crowded, especially around the holidays, and if you haven't been there before check the maps - it's big.

If you're in the STL area, at least one of your meals needs to be from a local Italian joint in my opinion. Tony's on Main was the perfect spot for us as we stayed at a hotel on Main Street, and walked in with a few minutes to spare before closing. 

Their toasted ravilolis were tasty, although only available in a meat option for all you vegetarians out there. The Italian Salad was flavorful and worth ordering every time in. 

What stole the show though was their pizzas. I know it's semi-fashionable to hate on STL style pizza outside this area, but hey I'm an honest guy and I freaking love it. It's thin crust, loaded with creamy cheese and toppings. It's 10x better than Chicago style pizza if you're asking me. 

Hungry from riding, I ate as much as I could possibly stomach and was sad when I started getting full, it was that good. 

Aside from the food, our server was helpful and fast, and even though they were about to close, they weren't rude at all and we made a point to get out to let them do their thing.

One of the best Mexican restaurants in Philadelphia. The food speaks to your heart. Having eaten in local hotels Mexico I can safely say the food is very close to being authentic. And the drinks are simple with a kick too. Especially the michilladas. The setting is very cozy and the service was very warm. Pesos well spent here.

This isn't like a froyo shop where there is a bunch of variety. There are a limited number of items but they are yummy! I've had the salty pimp before and it lives up to the hype. This time I tried the mermaid and it tastes just like key lime pie but with ice cream! I'm confident that most of the ice cream selections are great depending on what you are craving.

Ok, maybe it's the attitude of the staff or the fact that it's all self-serve or the fact that all of their cups leak; coupled with the high cost and horrible roasts...  But I'm not a fan!  I tried and tried and tried to be, but it's not good.  The food isn't even that great.  Save your money and go to Starbucks!

If it had an option for no star, I would. Me and my friend waited for 10 minutes to be seated. No one was helping us, the waitresses kept walking past us. I finally had to ask someone to be helped. When we both were finally seated, we were not being served in for a while so we got up and left. Their breakfast menu sucked! Not appealing.
Don't care how much u have changed the place..will never go back there again..this place has screwed me over 1 time to many

Everything was delicious here! My husband and I ordered some variation of a cáprese salad, grilled octopus, olives, and the paella with chicken and chorizo and it was all amazing. Also, I felt their portion sizes were very generous. Sometimes you go to a tapas place and leave hungry, but not here. 
Additionally, the ambience of Loquita really transports you to Spain. We sat on their patio and the decor is beautiful with fire pits, Spanish textiles and beautiful bougainvilleas. On top of that, we had an excellent server (wish I could remember his name...Matt maybe??) and there wine comes in half carafe in this cool looking decanter. Go there! You won't be disappointed :)

I try to stop in a Filipino restaurant whenever I get a chance because they're few and far between and The food reminds me of growing up. The food was actually pretty good. They serve the food cafeteria style. I got the Pork Sinigang and Chicken Adobo combo served with rice. The restaurant is attached to a small Filipino store. The restaurant needs some interior improvement, but I'll be back.
Deluxe is great if you have time! Love the pebble stones. Definitely will be headed back

I thought I would try this salon that I knew several people had gone to in the past. 
The shop was clean and I really liked the idea of using plastic pedicure bowl liners. I picked a slightly higher price pedicure, a treat for me. The pedicure was not the best. I said I wanted the standard manicure, $14.00. When I checked out my total bill was $ 71.00 dollars. I don't get manicures often, I asked why and it was gel polished he used. I didn't ask for gel. Now it's chipping, I got the manicure three days ago. 
Lesson learn I will get a written cost up front. 
I will ask for the manager to talk with me and repair the curled polish. 

Buyer beware.

Strolled in to my normal brunch spot (north 3rd) as if it was any other Saturday. I Was browsing and saw there was mofongo on the menu. As a bodega and lechonera frequenter I found this interesting and I  knew I needed to have. I kid you not, this is by far, undoubtably, THE BEST mofongo I've ever had in my life. Called my father this shit so good. Chef comes out to shake my hand this shit so good. The chef said it's First time he's ever cooked plantains. Never thought whiteboys could whip up plantains like this, but yet again don't  sleep  on  n3rd

I haven't had Indonesian food for quiet some time and this place got the taste perfect! It definitely reminded me a bit of home and the customer service was amazing. I ordered the chicken satay which was cooked perfectly and paired it with their homemade peanut sauce and it tasted amazing! I'm a big fan of salty fish fried rice and the taste of the dish was great too! I definitely am coming back here sometime soon and would highly recommend this place to others!

Not sure why the overall score is so low. 
I guess some people have really high expectations, typical Santa Barbara.
In reality, don't expect Panera to spoon feed you bites of amazing food. Panera is a bakery first, café second. 

Let's start with the food: 
Sure, their food may not be cooked to order as you would get from a specialty location, but if you're going to Panera, you are going there for the bread, not the salads, soups, and sandwiches. If you look closely, *half* of their front counter contains an assortment of baked goods (cookies, bagels, and other pastries). Did you miss it on your way in? So stop complaining about the sandwiches because the lettuce wasn't grown with unicorn fertilizer. Every time I visit I get the mac and cheese or bbq chicken salad with a baguette and a PASTRY (yes! bread!). And the bread is like the best part! Free refills on your fountain drinks and coffee. 

Service: 
You order over the counter, they serve to you at your table within minutes, you don't feel obligated to tip as you would in a sit down restaurant. How can you complain on the service? If you sit there long enough after your meal they will even take your plates away. 

Cleanliness: 
It's a brand new location, it's sparkling clean. The seating always looks comfortable. And they even have an outdoor seating area. Restaurants usually forget there is an outdoor at their respective locations, but this location keeps the outside very clean.

Overall: 
When it comes down to it, Panera is a relaxed place to eat (on your lunch hour, after some downtown shopping, in the morning when you're body is begging for coffee). I will admit that I wish the prices could be lowered on a few items, especially the non specialty items.

We couldn't wait to try Merchants and it surpassed our expectations!!!! Everything from our cocktails, appetizers and dinner were perfect!!! Super fast service and our waitress was the sweetest ever!! If you're in Nashville you have to stop in!

This is my 3rd and final bad experience with this restaurant. I went by this evening at 8:04 to grab a bite to eat and as usual this generation of young people know nothing about quality customer service. I ordered from the drive thru only to have the young lady be sarcastic with me while placing my order. When I arrived at the window, paid for and received my order I then asked for condiments. The look that I was given would've made you think that I asked for her social security number. She rolled her eyes, shut the window and took her sweet time just to grab condiments. And if wasn't enough, one of her co-workers said "I hate when they ask for stupid s**t to make you work harder." I'm just blown away by the level of unprofessional behavior that is allowed in today's businesses in our communities. This company will never get my business again after this evening. I've contacted their corporate headquarters in Ohio each time I've been treated this way and absolutely NOTHING was done about it, not even a phone call from the store to at least offer an apology. If anyone else has had any negative experience with this store location please drop me a message and let me know, I'm very curious.

It was a Saturday night and our last night in New Orleans.  The girlfriend and I wanted to culminate a great weekend in a great city with a great meal.  Following the advice of savvy locals, we decided to go to Cochon.  As an aside, I've been told by a friend (Jenn H, this means you) that I slaughter the pronunciation of the word "cochon".  Well, I may not know how to speak French, but I do know good food and Cochon, no matter how you say it, has damn good food!

It was prime time and we didn't have reservations.  We were willing to sit at the bar, which had a couple of open seats and were seated immediately.  We started off with a couple of their house original cocktails.  I had the Yellowjacket, a satisfying whiskey-based cocktail.  I wish I remembered everything that was in it, but it was a winner!  The GF had the Orange Whiskey, another solid offering.  

For our food choices, we started with the Fried Boudin with pickled peppers and the Fried Alligator with chili garlic aioli appetizers.  The boudin was wonderful, a perfectly fried pork ball.  Savory, meaty, yet surprisingly light.  A great start!  Unfortunately, the fried alligator was a slight misstep.  While nicely fried, leaving the meat tender, I thought it was over-breaded resulting in it falling off of the gator meat onto the plate instead of making it intact into my mouth.  I also felt the gator was over-sauced with the aioli.  Still a tasty offering, but not executed as well as the boudin.  However, our entrees both hit the ball out of the park!  The Louisiana Cochon with turnips, cabbage and cracklins was a pork tour de force.  Imagine a pan-fried (?) crab cake, but make it with a tender, spicy, and flavorful pulled-pork, and you have the Louisiana Cochon.  The turnips, cabbage, and cracklins were pleasing accompaniments to the meat.  The girlfriend's Oyster & Bacon Sandwich was so simple in concept and presentation, yet beautiful in its simplicity and flavor.  

We perused the dessert menu, saw several promising selections, but we were full after our pig feast.  Tyler persuaded us to give the Catdaddy moonshine (yeah, MOONSHINE) a try as an after dinner digestif.  Truth be told, I was skeptical, but this corn liquor had a subtle sweetness and possessed vanilla, cinnamon, and nutmeg notes.  It was a real surprise and a great finale to an enjoyable meal. 

In summation, service was 5-stars...food and drink was 4.5-stars, rounding up to 5-stars! Cochon is a must for anyone who loves good food and pig!

Terrible. Everything from the hostess, the waitresses and whomever the African American "manager" is could care less about the very serious complaints brought to her attention. She did nothing to even attempt to resolve the issue. I won't ever be going back. Save your money and go to chilis off Manhattan!

Etch has really changed the game in Nashville.  Deb is an amazing chef, she mixes spices and sauces together that make you think 'wow what is that? ' I love this restaurant!  Anytime clients are in town or family I show off Nashvilles food scene by going to Etch... and according to swarm I have eaten here over 30 times since it opened!

The service here was def above and beyond. I showed up at the time of my reservation and our table wasnt ready. The manager introduced himself and offered a drink on the house for my guest and I because of the table wait. The thing was there was only at most a 3 minute wait for our table to be ready!! Service was as excellent as we were dining and made for a great experience. We were there for restaurant week so i can imagine how hectic things were but service was not compromised. The food was really good as well! I did NYE at the same Ritz 2 years ago and it was the same excellent serivce and attention to detail. Def recommending to friends and coming back!

One complaint: This hotel needs to open up the doors from the locker room/gym that lead outside to the pool.  It is very uncomfortable to walk all the way through the cold tiled casino past other guests in a bathing suit when going from the pool to the gym.  There are doors all over the place, but they won't let you use them.  Very bad for guests who are there to enjoy the pool and locker room facilities.

Although I read all the bad reviews.  I still went here after i checked out of Harrah's.   Just wanted to get some brunch and drive 4hrs back...

Was not intending to go crazy on buffett like I usually do.  I wanted to get some protein.  Leftover prime rib.  Not bad.   Sample some other leftovers. The grilled chicken. Not so good...   Went for a bowl of noodles.  Freshly made, egg noodle with Chinese BBQ pork.  Not bad.  Not as fancy or nice as the buffett I've had in all the china and Taiwan hotel breakfast buffet.  

Well, total was 20 with tax..  not a local so didn't get the 50% discount.  Didn't feel like going down to the casino to get a card to save $2.  Probably will never come back to this buffet.  

Overall, I got what I wanted out of the meal. Prime rib and a bowl of noodles with some dessert and cup of coffee.   That's about right....  had to drive and didn't want to be too full.

Essentially, the brunch looks like it's all leftovers...  They did have a omelette station.  Definitely a deal for locals. But, I rather go elsewhere and have some fresh made to order food if I have the time.

The Tin Box is a bright and fun household and gift store.  It is full of trinkets and items for the home, often with a unique slant.  One of the things that led me to the store was the huge selection of Sigg aluminum water bottles and accessories.  Another was the Lunastix juggling sticks -- very hard to find on the shelves anywhere.  I usually have to special order my juggling sticks, but here they were.  

The Tin Box also has some handcrafted jewellery, home accents (lamps, mirrors, blinds), and other high-end toys.  It's a great place to head if you have to buy a gift for the proverbial "person who has everything."  It's also a great place to pick up something unique for yourself or your home.

Cristy our waitress was amazing! I ordered a martini she told me to try this Asian vodka it was so smooth and so worth it. She was always checking up on us. That atmosphere of the restaurant was great such a good date location. The music was great the fish was fresh! Can't go wrong with this location

Dinner tonight was not even mediocre at best.  The fish (snapper) was tough and way over cooked as was the vegetable medley mix.  In fact, the mushy consistency and lack of vegetable content left one wondering how do they stay in business and get away with charging what they do. Do yourself a favor and skip this one.  With the variety and choices in the area there is no reason to stop into such a poor tasting and for that matter quite dirty of a restaurant.  Well maybe, to pickup dessert, now that is where my two stars come into play.  But only if you get it to go.
i am 50 effing  years old thesee guys wouldnt  let me in!! lame as shit! i wont be back. dumber than a box of rocks!!!

Had dinner with my wife for a special occasion. Service was excellent. Both servers were awesome. We don't get to true "Steak House" steaks often but have been to a couple and this one ranked right up there. If you have a little extra cash and can spoil someone, take them here.
Great new spot for BBQ. Don't skip on the Lou sandwich and the Texas Twinkies. Will definitely be back.

A consistently inventive menu, a good selection of cheeses and other foods, and a friendly, inviting owner and ambiance have made this place one of my favorites. New dishes appear regularly; the quality of the food is consistently high and prices reasonable. The place is warm, unpretentious and inventive--an ideal neighborhood spot.

The pizza rates a 4 and is one of the best in the area.  This can't be said for the entrees we just had at their new location a couple of doors up from the old one - coming in at best at a 2.

Have you heard the phrase - It wasn't good but there was plenty of it - well that describes the 2 very poor chicken dishes we were served.  The better of the two was the Chicken Marsala that had no flavor of Marsala at all.  And speaking of flavor, or lack of, I'm afraid that perfectly describes the Chicken Abbruzzio which brought pieces of chicken breast covered with mounds of way over-cooked asparagus, broccoli and spinach with canned (?) black olives floating in a tasteless broth.

Stick with the pizza !

The haircuts and staff are just fine.  The problem is you never know when someone is going to be there.  When I attempt to get a haircut there is consistently no one there.  The store hours say 8am to 8pm 7 days a week.  If they actually honored the posted hours this would be a positive review.  I personally witnessed 5 customers attempting to patronize this establishment but were unable to because there was no one on site.

This is the first restaurant I visited since the lock downs started in March. Granted, I've been to Sampan many times over the past 5 years for happy hour and dinner since moving back home but revisiting any familiar place during COVID, with all the changes and restrictions, makes the experience strange and new. 

A close friend who I also had not seen since March made a reservation (no just walking up and claiming a table) so we could have an after work happy hour. We both arrived, masked, just a few minutes before 3 while the masked hostess outdoors was setting up her station with paper menus and hand sanitizer. She showed us to a table for 2 set up against the outside wall of Sampan. Tables were all 6 feet apart and a portion of the street in front of the restaurant was also cordoned off and made into a dining area. Again, tables were correctly distanced. 

Our table was on a distinct tilt; not bad enough so that eating implements and food rolled off but significant enough that we were not 100% comfortable. On the other hand, it was preferable to sitting in the street as regular, Friday Philly traffic rolled noisily and closely by.  

All tables were bare for easy cleaning between patrons. Our server, masked and gloved, took our order and chatted happily with us about being very glad to be back to work again. We told her we were utterly sick of our own cooking and, in Nick's case, delivered food. The atmosphere here was noisy (sirens, motorbikes, raised voices, horns honking) but festive. Not everyone (other than Sampan staff) we saw was wearing a mask. Of course, those seated and enjoying their food and drink were sans mask, but that was to be expected. 

Nick and I ordered what we usually would have had in pre-COVID days-the house special cocktail (a cranberry/vodka spritzer on this day-very weak), happy hour priced edamame dumplings, crab rangoon, beef skewers, kim chee fried rice, roasted brussels sprouts and roasted shisito peppers. By now, we had several masked servers attending our table, thus the food was coming out rather quickly, crowding our small, tilty table top. 

Happy hour prices have not changed and you'll still get a solid meal if the happy hour bites are going to be your dinner. No shame in that at all. The fried rice was not quite as we remembered; still a very plentiful serving but seeming a bit underseasoned, lackluster and very light on the kim chee. Like what I find at almost every restaurant that offers shisito peppers, these were more soggy than fried/lightly charred; as well, they were served in an oddish way-a big bowl heaped with peppers (making them MORE soggy as they sat and steamed together) with the 'dipping' sauce smeared on one side of the bowl in a thin swathe. This made the peppers hard to 'dip' so we wound up using first a knife, then our fingers, (since it was just the 2 of us) to retrieve some sauce for our peppers. That finger thing isn't something I'd do if I were to eat with a group, though. Regular plates and utensils were used for serving, but chopsticks and napkins were disposable. 

We ate, had several drinks, caught up on the doings and not doings of each other's post-COVID lives and people watched. Not everyone who had a reservation was masked and patrons who were walking around-heading to or returning from the restroom, meeting other members of their party-were usually not masked, either. There also seemed to be a line of people either waiting for their reservation time, or seeing if they could get a spot. There was absolutely no social distancing in the line, most of those waiting were not masked and some of the people were actively hanging onto/leaning on each other. Sure-probably lovers and/or good friends (one would hope)-but still...

Between the traffic and the din of people at last let out of long confinement, lots of unmasked patrons passing our table, the noise level that was fairly high, plus the tilt of the table all made it hard to relax in spite of having quaffed several adult beverages. As a result, we cut our time short, got the check which arrived quickly, paid, tipped generously and headed off to our respective destinations. 

Would I go back? Probably not for awhile. I'm curious to try other outdoor dining situations, like Salty's, K'Far, Zahav's patio and BarBombon's charming looking alley seating. Heck, even a take out picnic in Rittenhouse Square would tickle me. 

Sampan certainly seemed to be doing everything right; maybe this was (for us) like once again dancing or dating for the first time in a long time-awkward and strange, but hopefully something that will become better and easier with time.

This was my first time experiencing a wax or a wax center.. and let me tell you. PHENOMENAL service. from the moment i walked in the door, i was greeted politely (even i was being a little rude being on my phone) but Olivia, the receptionist, was kind, attentive and friendly. she walked me through the entire process and gave me key points about not being too nervous, which really helped the entire experience. Between filling out some last points with registration and waiting for my specialist Jerae to come out, I was only waiting for about 5 minutes. (I came on a Tuesday morning/early afternoon before going into my next job).
