Only been for lunch but the dinner reviews sound wonderful. For lunch it's quiet and the menu is nice. I ordered the beet salad and it was fresh, crisp and sweet. I had it with an Earl Grey, the bar tender kept topping up my tea with hot water but in the end it was another teabag I needed. Weak tea is not for me.
The decor was lovely, exposed brick, cool mural on the wall, modern furniture and you can see right into the kitchen. It's a cosy vibe, with bright light from the long windows looking right out onto 124 Street.

The almond croissant is where it is at!!!

Aside from that, the other items on the menu, the pastries, coffee, are pretty good as well.  I would say more abut I don't have much experience when it comes to French food.   But being recommended by a French native friend, it was worth a try.

I think as far as paint points, this place can get pretty crowded and seating is very limited.  Their pastries can go fast, so if you come by here later in the day, you may miss out on some.  Lastly, this is located in Santa Barbara and the prices are higher than what you'd normally pay for.

Overall, I'll come by again, especially for their almond croissant :)

Before coming here for a work outing, I wasn't a Ruby Tuesday's fan by any stretch of the imagination. However, this formerly generic burger chain has upped their game. They've added some healthier options with their Light and Fit menu, and even a health-nut like me was able to order a satisfactory meal that I didn't regret eating later that day.

I ordered the three-veggie meal which allowed me to choose three sides paired with the salad bar. The salad bar isn't anything special, but you can load up on spinach leaves and carrot shavings if that's what you're into. I did go off-diet and snacked on the spinach artichoke dip that was ordered for the table. It came in a three-dip sampler with an okay guacamole, and a neon-orange queso dip that was left largely untouched at our 10-person table.  For my three-veggie meal, I ordered the roasted spaghetti squash, steamed brocolli, and sugar snap peas. The spaghetti squash was surprisingly low in sodium and very yummy; the broccoli was another low-sodium option, but was a little overcooked; the snap peas were drowned in oil and I skipped them.

I'm not going out of my way to hit this chain, but if I end up here again, I'll know what to order.

This is my favorite out of all the hot chicken places in Nashville with the exception of Hattie B's (which I haven't tried yet).

The chicken is juicy and fiery. I can handle a medium but they go up to a XXHOT to satisfy the fire fiends out there. 

The covered patio has four picnic tables which can comfortably seat six people each.  There are ceiling fans for the summer and heaters for the winter so dining is very comfortable. The staff is very friendly and will recommend the appropriate level of heat and sides to suit your taste. This is a big plus over Prince's, where they seem to barely tolerate customers.
Awesome place. Short rib ravioli was to die for and our server Nick was the best. He was attentive and so friendly!!!

Really surprised I have done a review for this one yet as much as I get food from here.  The owner and his team are are great and provide a really fun atmosphere besides the good food.  Speaking of the food my favorite sandwich is the Skywalker because of the combination of the heat from the pepper jack cheese and jalepeno aioli really mixes well with the cool ranch Doritos.  The ham solo as well as the das fritz along with the regular and cinnamon pretzels are all very good as well.

Theo's is my favorite spot on Tuesdays.  It's become a neighborhood hang out and a meeting point for our local walking/running group.  During noncovidtimes, we can all meet up and grab a draft beer and share pizza and stories.  

I know it's a pizza joint, but they have hands down the BEST Greek Salad in all of New Orleans.  We always get a small (the portions are huge!) and split a pie.  Typically the Expert, the Eccentric, or the Jammers.  I love the interesting topping combos they use.  It's off book with things like goat cheese and prosciutto and honey and bacon crumbles.  The crust is thinner and it doesn't seem like they use corn meal.  They also have a LOT of vegetarian and vegan options.    

The restaurant itself lends to a comfortable, neighborhood vibe. Parking can be tight, so it's great that it's right on the streetcar route.

Honestly, the only good things here that I have tried are their cheesesteaks and a slice of their Reese's special cheesecake. The cheesesteaks were fresh and their bread is to die for. However, the times I have tried their pasta dishes, I've been highly disappointed. The chicken in one pasta dish was bland and didn't taste very fresh and there is also a very unnecessary amount of oiliness in their pasta. If I do visit, I will get their cheesesteaks.

We've been wanting to try Hattie's for awhile & finally had the chance. The reviews are spot on. The food didn't disappoint. The customer service is excellent. 

The wait. This is the reason we've not tried it before. We have three small girls and aren't a fan of keeping them entertained in a slow moving line. Well, the line moves pretty good. A couple of the employees came out to talks with us. 

The food. It is great. Our only disappointment was we didn't get enough a variety of sides. We stuck with the tried and true macaroni and cheese and fries. My wife had "no heat" on her tenders. I had "medium" on the wings. The chicken portions are huge. The medium heat was enough to feel the heat and not overpower the flavor. 

The customer service. The cashier made recommendations to me for a bigger meal for less money than I had ordered. She knew I was ordering for a family of 5 and made that extra step to make it great for the kids. Plus, they gave us a generous military discount. 

I'll say it. Ready? Chick-fil-A is over rated. There. You know we're all thinking it anyway. 

Go to Hattie B's instead.

After years of driving past on my way to and from work, I finally decided it was time to try the food. Now, my fiance and I order food here almost weekly. With so many great food options in Indy, you know it must be good if we return to the same place that often. Everything we've ordered from the tacos to the chimichanga is fantastic. The portion sizes on the meals are huge and typically last for two meals. I also love that the avocados are fresh, ripe, sliced and not mashed into weird runny guacamole!

Beautiful restaurant very modern,love the decor.  The owner was so nice an they worked really hard to find us a table. The wait was no more than 10 min on this past Friday night. For a appetizer we tried the Fatayer (3 different pies stuffed with spinach,sirloin,cheese) an a awesome cucumber sauce. SOOO good the pies were so light, very unexpected. For the entree we both had the Mishwe a tenderloin brochette. Basically a kabob with 3 big pieces of meat an veggies. Absolutely delicious the meat was SO tender an this orange sauce on top was good. A mountain of well seasoned scalloped potatoes came with it. We had small salads that came with the meal, pretty good also. They also had a small side of garlic paste that was good with the meat too. Basically, I have found my new favorite Lebanese spot. Loved it!

What a welcome green space in Center City.
Fitler square has a cute little fountain, shady trees and lots of cute coffee bars and places to explore nearby.

Love this area.

How can you not love WaWa? This store is my local joint, so I'm there at least once every day. The real attraction to this place is the people that work there. Everyone, and I literally mean everyone, is super friendly and more than accommodating. The food won't blow you away, but for a gas station convenience store, it's a 5 Star restaurant. There's a reason that WaWa is so successful, just take a visit yourself and you will understand why.
We walked in here last minute and the customer service and help blew us away. They are amazing! Ladies you must go here for your dress.

We have ordered deep dish from here three times.  Hubby loves it and I think it's just okay, but I'm realizing that I just might not like deep dish pizza.  If you're not already a deep dish fan, you're getting a lot of crust (outer half crispy and inner half barely cooked), some toppings, and a lot of chunky tomatoes on top.  I have to eat with a fork and knife because everything falls apart.  Like I said, I just might not like the whole concept of deep dish.  I do like the special box that supports the weight of this very heavy pizza, like you're ordering something that needs to be contained.  That part was very exciting the first time, until I tried it.

The fried ravioli are not great and taste like any fried thing dipped in marinara.  

Unless you have a raging appetite or several deep dish lovers, this is a hard sell because even hubby can't eat more than two slices, and the pizza hasn't reheated well for us.  The crust just goes soggy under the weight of the toppings.  We end up with half a very expensive pizza going to waste.  Is it possible to make a personal pan deep dish?  That would heal the divide in our household!

Went here after taking the family to sesame place, and wow was it worth it. This was a great cheesesteak! Meat well cooked great cheese good hoagie bread. Their cherry soda was a wonderful surprise. Skip park food, head to Steve's you'll be glad you did!

I was moving from a second story condo to a brand new home. I was so stressed and thought many items would break. Ignacio and David came in, they were so strong and so fit, they moved my crowded one bedroom condo to a big home. They were so professional, diligent and effective. Instead of dropping everything on the first spot, they cared to ask where I want to move them. They moved things more than once with such patience. They had a roller so the dolly wouldn't damage the railing and the floor.
They acted more like couple caring friends help on me move. Thank you David and Ignacio for making this stressful event painless. The best movers I had encountered.

We came here on two separate occasions and spent at least $300-400 and each trip. Now keep in mind this is not pertain to all the girls working there but one of the girls try to add shots as well as other beers to one of the persons bills that was part of our party that was intoxicated thinking that she was going to be able to go ahead and sneak in extra charges but we caught it she threw a huge fit and the manager came out and did nothing. This fat African-American manager came out and had the girl tell the gentleman that was in a party that they needed his license to go ahead and refund the charges to his credit card that right afterwords they refused to give him his license and less he would sign and agree to the charges (which they took with false pretenses) we told them that they could charge the card but we weren't signing because we're just gonna go ahead and dispute it horrible experience manager refused to come out of his office for two hours we had to call the cops and they gave us the license back and told the matter to charge the card! The charges have been refunded through the credit card company but we wasted 2 1/2 hours of our life on something that should've not happened

This spot is one of 3 locations and probably my favorite of them all, due to how spacious it is inside and the consistency of freshly made food they have served for my takeout orders. Obviously right now during COVID-19 there is no inside dining and there are only a few tables outside to sit at. 

This location is rarely busy from my experience but that could be due to their location being off the beaten path and also the number of mexican restaurants we have in this town competing against each other. Everyone has their preferences in what mexican food should taste like, but I'm not too picky so Rudy's comes through when I'm in a pinch. 

They are known for their huge crispy tacos which are heavily stuffed with shredded chicken or beef, lettuce, and cheese. It's so overly packed that I usually have to remove a lot of the lettuce just to bite into the taco. No complaints here because once you bite into the taco, it is delicious! 

The salmon tacos are my sons favorite and the best part is their corn tortillas are homemade. His other go to item on the menu is the vegetarian burrito. 

My go to's are the chicken enchiladas, tacos and nachos. Selection of salsas are mild, medium and hot with your choices of green, red or roasted salsa. 

Overall the service here is always welcoming and friendly. The wait time is pretty quick for walk-in orders. 

Don't forget to wear a mask, bring hand sanitizer and keep your distance!

I don't even know where to start! I'm here for a wedding, I checked in on Thursday. On my arrival I received keys to a room and the key did not work.  I went back to the front desk advised them that the key did not work and asked if I can have a room on a the 2nd floor to be closer to the aunt that I am traveling with.   The attendance said that since I had not opened the door that it would be fine for me to change to the room on the floor with my aunt. I go into the new room and in the toilet there is feces, urine and toilet paper, there were flies in the bathroom, in the shower there's an open bar of soap and water stains, but the bed is made and the room is otherwise clean. Clearly someone had been in the room and used the bathroom. I go back down to the front desk let her know and she says that there is no housekeeping staff so I did the unthinkable. I cleaned my own toilet.   At this point it's about 2:00 a.m. I'm winding down and go to turn on the television. The television does not work! The attendant says she will change my room in the morning. The next morning I pack my bags and move to the new room.  The attendant told me once I get into the new room call her to let her know that I'm out of the other room. I pick up the phone to call to let her know and the phone doesn't work. I walk down to the front desk to let her know that I'm out of the old room and that the phone doesn't work in the new room, she tells me that she will send a technician. Today which is the day after still no phone I go to the front desk I ask her about the phone she says the technician will be to my room. I see the technician in the hall he says HE WENT INTO MY ROOM WHILE I WAS GONE and my phone line is dead. I go back down to the front desk and ask if they plan on moving me to another room? (I am here for another 48 hours I don't want to be in a room with no phone). She says there's no more rooms available and there's nothing she can do. For all of this trouble they offer to comp me one night. Not good enough!....I UNDERSTAND THAT WE ARE IN THE MIDDLE OF A PANDEMIC AND THAT IS WHY THERE IS NO MAID SERVICE (no sheet changing, no room service, no turn down service...) BUT!!!! WHAT DOES THAT HAVE TO DO WITH DIRTY BATHROOMS, WORKING TV'S AND WORKING PHONES?)

We light candles in  honor of Ernie at every Cathedral/church we enter for he is our Old Car Savior. 

We have 2 old cars- 1996 and 2004.  Ernie is fair, quick and honest. Several times I have gotten written estimates from other shops and when I take it in to Ernie, he fixes the same job for pennies on the dollar.   Needless to say, we give him a lot of business.

Well, today I was prompted to write up this little love letter to Ernie for the following reason:

I took my car for a simple repair at a closer shop and they estimated it would cost $168, require parts to be ordered and take 2 days.  And I had to wait for an hour and 30 minutes for the mechanic to turn up to get the  4-1-1.

On a hunch I took it to Ernie immediately afterwards. He fixed it with a wrench in 6 minutes for free! No parts, NO CHARGE!

Signed,

Thoroughly besotted with Ernie

Vui's catered a recent lunch for 75 people and the noodle bowls were a hit. Lindsey, the catering manger, was incredibly responsive and wonderful to work with. The food arrived on time, exactly as planned, and was a wonderful treat for our team. We plan to use Vui's in the future and highly recommend their catering options to others.
do not go here they will scam you. as you can see in previous comments a woman took us by the arm, forced shots down our throats and charged us $55. again do not support this trifflin business

This place lives up to it's hype. The coffee is very good, a decaf au lait at 11pm was perfect. Better are the powder sugar drowned beignets were absolutely delicious. The atmosphere of the place is lively and fun.  All at a very reasonable price.  Definitely stop here when in the Quarter.

Way overrated. 

The breakfast was mediocre at best. The bacon was overly salty. The fried potatoes that came with the Farmhouse breakfast platter were so hard they couldn't even be cut in half or chewed. 

The wait is ridiculously long and not worth the wait or the money.

I had heard nice things about this bakery, so last week on Saturday I placed an order for a small cake. It was my 25th wedding anniversary, the next week, so I thought it would be nice. My husband is very ill, and may not see another Anniversary, so I thought it would be nice. I went in to pick up the cake, the lady gets it and it's like a doughnut covered with frosting. I was shocked and wanted to burst into tears. I was told that's what I ordered, I didn't think it was that small. I was given a little plaque with happy 25th on it. It was bigger than the cake. When I cut the cake that night it fell apart, it was so dry, it looked like it was baked a week ago, needless to say I didn't have dessert,I threw it away.

Great steak house!!! I was determined to finish my 18 oz ribeye- it was so good and just the right marbleization. The tomahawk is 32 oz with a 60 day age. We also ordered their jumbo shrimp cocktail and definitely listen to the waiter's directions when eating them. Also as recommended, I put half a spoon of the shrimp cocktail sauce into the navy bean soup and it definitely gave it some kick. The king crab and shrimp linguine with pesto sauce was also amazing. We were so full that we didn't have any room for dessert! I guess this means we will have another reason to come back next time and hopefully try out their dessert.

We had a cooking mishap last night with dinner and hubby saved us by ordering Shake Shack so we could quickly eat something delicious. He ordered the new KFC sandwich and I ordered the Shack Stack with the Shroom burger and a regular burger patty (comfort food vibes). We also picked up a small side of fries with the new Gochujang sauce. The Shack Stack was cheesy, delicious, and consistent with what I expected. 

The new Korean inspired items were less impressive. The chicken sandwich was good, but KFC is typically very crunchy chicken and this sandwich was not. We've ordered KFC to-go from other places in the pandemic and it held up its crunch so I don't think the takeout aspect was the culprit here. The Gochujang sauce was a good sauce but it tasted like any other burger sauce or spicy mayo. That could just be my unfamiliarity with what Gochujang sauce is or should taste like. It was still a good sauce and the fries were consistent with what I expect from Shake Shack.

Great job with the consistency of the normal menu items and with social distancing, etc. at the store. "Meh" to the Korean inspired items from me.
Great food. A little pricey but worth it. Bread is awesome, philly roll is awesome and so are drinks and steaks.
Rice was reheated and burned and pork seemed it had also been sitting there for a few days. Black beans had no taste. Ended up not eating it

I haven't been here in a while but today was a disappointment. My party started with the cinnamon roll to share which would've probably been delicious had it not been cold. I saw an advertisement for red velvet holiday pancakes and got SUPER excited. I inquired to my server about the pancakes and she gave a warning saying though it states "Red Velvet" they actual don't taste like red velvet at all they taste like strawberry pancakes. I'm one who prefers toppings on my pancakes besides syrup and these were supposed to be topped with a cream cheese drizzle and crushed candy canes, so I decided to give them a try. 
The order was out in a decent time but there was much to be desired. I received my red velvet pancakes that I was so excited to receive and was immediately disappointed. It looked nothing like the picture and it wasn't topped with ANYTHING. I let my server know my pancakes were missing the toppings and she said she would bring them right out. Once my party received their food, my cup of cold cream cheese icing finally made its way to the table. I have never experienced received pancake toppings on the side but I was just happy to get my food. 
Overall everything I had and the rest of my party had including my Mardi Gras omelette was cold but I was super hungry so I didn't bother to send it back. The red velvet pancakes were indeed strawberry in taste and not anything close to red velvet. It was my first time ordering the city grits at the recommendation to someone in my party and it was a strange taste combination that i couldn't quite put my finger on. My colleague who recommended them said they are usually in a creamier consistency versus the grittiness we experienced. My other colleague on the other hand received brown guacamole and a brown lime to accompany the omelette he chose. 
I will say this visit was not a success and I'm not sure if I would be willing to visit this location again. I've been to the Magazine street location a few times and haven't experienced anything of this sort.

While visiting Philadelphia, I basically made it a point to spend as much time as possible at the Reading Terminal. My hotel was very close, and there was just so many different places to try, I couldn't help but go on multiple occasions. I visited Hershel's for breakfast on first morning there and it was amazing. I got an egg and cheese bagel sandwich with bacon. It was everything that a breakfast sandwich should be! The guys behind the counter were really nice as well. My biggest regret is that I did not visit again for another meal. There were just too many options in the terminal. Oh well. I loved what I got while I was there.

It's no surprise to me that this place gets a 5-star rating.  My sister and I live in different parts of California and decided to meet up in Santa Barbara and take this class.  Gina was wonderful in helping us schedule (and reschedule when work thing came up for me) and Saul is really an amazing teacher.  He makes it all look easy and keeps everything comfortable and fun.  He lets you do about 90% of the work, but he's right there to help out at every step, as needed.  We had a blast!  We each ended up with darn good looking bowls (if I do say so myself) and plan to come back and do it again the next time we're in the area.  

They also have some beautiful things you can buy!  But take the class, too, you'll love it!

We were looking for a local pizza place, no national chains, while in the area for the birth of our new grandchild. Found Magoo's on Yelp and decided it was worth a try. Did not disappoint. Based upon the reviews, we tried a meat lovers with half garlic sauce/half marinara sauce. Delicious! We also tried a pizza with sausage and mushrooms and marinara sauce. Again, very tasty. The lettuce salad was the surprise hit - surprising due to the home made ranch dressing - the only dressing Magoo's has. No need for any other dressing - this thick and tasty ranch dressing is not to be missed! We picked up out food carry out to take to the hospital to eat. Employee working the register was very accommodating with paper plates, napkins and forks when I mentioned this. Delighted to find affordable canned soda in their cooler - this enabled me to be sure everyone had their preferred drink. Magoo's is good, local fare and we will definitely be back! Looking forward to trying their specialty pizzas which are unique!
One of the funkiest cool Hotels I've enjoyed in awhile. The rooms, decor, the food - Top Notch.

Have been using Broad Glass for several years. Started with repairing rock chips in the windshield of my car. They have also replaced my windshield and a rearview mirror. The last work performed was a frameless shower enclosure in one of my bathrooms and a glasstop for my dining room table. All work was done quickly and at very reasonable prices. Broad Glass has my seal of approval!

The people working were professional however they were very understaffed and the service I received took nearly two hours.  The waiting area was also crowded and lacked air conditioning which I found unacceptable in 105 degree weather.

After visiting the Philadelphia Art Museum on a HOT July day, we decided to get a little AC, grab a beer, and a bite to eat. Black Taxi is conveniently close so we decided to try it, and a so glad we did! Met the owners who were super nice, and had an AWESOME cheesesteak and ICE COLD Yuengling. Highly recommended this place! Check it out!

Great service! Amazing food! We were staying at le maison hotel right across from Ruby slipper and since we got here we saw they were always busy so we had to try it! I looked at their reviews and everything looked really good. We were not disappointed! Come early i think brunch time gets a lot busier than their breakfast time.

Every Monday and Thursday the air in the Central West End is filled with the smell of roasting coffee.  It's coming from the roaster at Northwest.  I have been buying my roasted coffee beans there for years and would buy them from no other place.  Comfy chairs and wireless if you want to hang out for a pastry and a cuppa.  Very, very friendly!
best burrito place!!!! 10 stars!! Always fresh! And quick!! Live this place. Guacamole delicious! Nachos are the best!

Impressed with how charming and cozy the place are! The decoration is amazing, the waiter/bartender was kind and make us feel comfortable, every details makes a difference. Food is tasty and the drinks are well prepared and delicious. Certainly the best place to hang out in new hope.
Remarkable customer service.  I was in need of a tow for my vehicle and the service Far exceeded my expectations.  Communication is key in making all parties happy.  CTS is a no brainer!!

I've taken my dog here for training, boarding and daycare. The people are good and the services are fine, but they nickel and dime you for everything. After spending a substantial amount of money for training, I was told I had to pay for an "evaluation" of my dog before he could stay at daycare, even though the trainer who evaluated him had already seen him around other dogs in class. Want to have fido's nails clipped while he's there? $10. For a service that takes two minutes and my vet will perform for free while we're there. But I went along with it. Now rates are going up for daycare and it was already not cheap. I find myself taking him here less and less and with the rate hike it's going to be even less often.
I have two English springer spaniels. They are groomed beautifully at "I Love Dogs". There is an art to groom Springers and Bob does a great job.
Breakfast was fine. Eggs, bacon, potatoes. Basic stuff. Prepared as requested. But not difficult meal to get right. Typical restaurant food for Omni hotel.

Very friendly folks. I tried the Philly cheesesteak fries and wings. Fries are just as everyone stated. REALLY greasy. If you can get past the grease, they're not bad. I absolutely loved the cheesesteak-EXCEPT their bread which was a little tough and chewy. Imagine bread put in the microwave. I would try the sandwich again cuz the flavor was delish!! I'd give this place another try

A decent pho, but what's noticeable is the lack of veggie add-ins given. Now, to be fair, they say to ask if we want more, but it just looks skimpy when they first bring it out to the table. (I'm thinking they see a lot of people waste the bean sprouts, jalapeños, limes, etc. So, start people out with less.)

Yum! I enjoyed the two taco plate with sirloin steak and came with beans and rice. They also provide complimentary chips and have a fresh salsa bar with all different types of sides and topping and fresh salads. Honestly I think the fresh salsa bar takes this place to the next level. It's a very laid back, casual place with low prices for great food. Will definitely be back! I have to try that quesadilla!

I brought my friends from out of town to Hai Kitchen because of the multiple positive reviews. Not only was the staff rude but the food was over priced and the food was horrible. It was just Americanized sushi in  burrito form. I would have paid 5$ max

Love love love this place. 

They offer a 4 for $25 deal for sushi takeout and I'd say we take advantage of it at least every couple weeks. The Hurricane, the King Kong, Tornado are some of my favs. Lots of great options to choose from.

I have been here several times, but this time I sat out on the patio.  Tucson has some great views and sunsets, and this place takes advantage of that.

This trip I had the ribeye with the ranch beans.  It comes with a side salad and vegetables.  As usual, I ordered it medium rare.  It was just a bit more done than that, I like mine more rare, but still lots of flavor and a nice cut of meat.  I know vegetables are not exciting, but these were grilled to perfection.  Too often you get them WAY over cooked until they are mushy and loose texture.  These had flavor from the vegetables and the grill.  Really the only thing no great were the beans.  I wouldn't say they were too hot, but there was too much cayenne pepper.  My mom who was with me wouldn't eat them and not because it was too hot, flavor balance was off.

As you can see from the attached picture, the view is great.  I suggest going near sunset and sit on the patio.

Hands down. My favorite place for philly cheesesteaks in Philly! The wait was outside the door and perhaps 30-40 minutes but worth it. You can see them put fresh beef on and cook them in mass quantities for everyone. I had it without onions and with whiz. So yummy! (and perhaps I'm drooling now for more...). I went on a Saturday so it was busy. I don't know about weekdays but I'd suggest taking it to a square and eating it if the weather is nice. Seats are hard to come by in the chaos of the lines.
I can't say just how much coming to this small Cuban spot. Food hits the spot right after a run. Cafe con Leche is delish!

Had my first adjustment ever I'm not in pain
In fact I feel better!!
Dr Johnson is a class act , told me the pros & the cons
Love  Randi the massage lady , she is sooo good and apples just the right amount of pressure!
I can hardly wait to come back, looking forward to next appt!!
The Dylan Frittata was made to perfection and the cheesy grits were yummy and I do not like cheesy grits

This was my first ever visit to Belladonna Day Spa. The place is very spacious and beautiful. I received a gift card from my sister-in-law and decided to use it for the 50-minute massage. My masseuse was Jessica. She was gentle, made me feel relaxed, and relieved a lot of knots from my "computer neck." I felt like time just flew by! 

The only gripe I have is that while I had to lay my face towards the floor at the end of the bed, she covered it with a towel, which made it a little difficult for me to breathe since there was no circulation. It was hard to focus on relaxing because of that. However, in the end I was very satisfied with my experience and would consider coming back again, possibly to order other services!

I absolutely love the concept of this place!! It's a no brainer when you are with a large group of friends and want to satisfy everyone's craving. They have a unique and diverse set of restaurants that can please everyone. The atmosphere is awesome, and i love that there is a bar  too. 

I ate at the AZ rib house, which was pretty decent. The ribs were super tasty, but beware of the sweet and sour sauce! It will most definitely stain your fingers red for the duration of the day. I was a little disappointed in the elote lollipop. It was just elote on a stick! Unfortunately, the flavors of the elote were not that great when I tried it, i think because the corn was not fully ripe. Maybe I just got a bad batch!

Nonetheless, I can't wait to go back and try other restaurants in the food hall!!
This place says Nawlins but I wasn't impressed w the lost bread breakfast. The andouille and eggs yummy and the grits mmmmm!

I've only had coffee here so that's all I can go by food-wise. But I lmam seriously impressed by this venue, space, the light, design... Chictopia!!!
But parking is $10?!!! Docked off star on that..

Why 5 stars? Because this may be the only rum distillery I've been to, but it's my favorite!

   ---   ---   ---

I discovered these guys way back in the day when they were in a tiny bungalow in Seminole Heights and went by the name of Twisted Sun Rum. I've followed their path from a distance along the way and saw that they recently got the distillery up and running. I'd been meaning to make my way over to check it out and was finally able to.

I didn't realize that they don't technically sell you the cocktails - they offer them complimentary in hopes that you'll purchase a bottle of rum. The guy working behind the bar said that they have a couple different complimentary cocktails available and asked what kind of rum I usually prefer. I'm nowhere near the level of being able to tell you really specifically what I like, so I just mentioned that they posted on a photo of a Blue Hawaiian on Facebook the other day and that something like that looked right up my alley. He searched to make sure he had the proper ingredients to make that and had it ready for me pretty quickly.

It was as tasty as it comes for a cocktail, in my opinion. I usually prefer wine or beer, but this drink went down way too easily to be considered safe. I dug it so much that I couldn't pass up the opportunity to buy a bottle of the coconut rum. He also gave me a sample of that by itself and it had a very smooth finish.

If you're looking for rum in Tampa Bay, this is definitely the place to go!

Great service, nice ambiance, food OK. Came by for some breakfast after the farmer's market. Wanted to eat outside, but there was a bit of a wait. We were hungry so got seated inside instead, luckily by the window. For all our egg platters, we ordered them overeasy, but they came out completely cooked through - next time I guess we'll just say sunny side up to get the dippy eggs we were looking for! Hostess friendly, all servers were helpful, left with full bellies and still had some to go.
We don't have many restaurants here that serve good Peruvian food. La Mordida tops the list. Going to come back for their Ceviche.

First review ever so here it goes:

For the first annual Return of the Mac event, it was pretty alright. Overall it was enjoyable, but very overwhelming at the same time. There was a lot of hype but didn't live up to the expectations I had. 

The venue was nice but way too small for the attendance of the event. Good atmosphere but extremely poor layout and setup of the Mac and cheese vendors. Vendors needed larger booths and more spaced out. There were no predetermined lines so it was hard to even get mac and cheese samples most of the time. Event needed much more organization. 

Now and most importantly, the mac and cheese. 20+ vendors to try some but at the 5-7 time slot, some had already run out before even getting a chance to try and more so by 6. As for the food itself, I'd say only about 5 truly identified as true and good noteworthy mac and cheese. Several were too dry, not cheesy enough, milky, bland, hidden by meat or something else, or tasted like a different pasta dish. Definitely could have better overall true mac and cheese. 

My top choices: 
1 - Fat Dan's
2 - Cerulean's
3 - Clustertruck / The District

We love the Boba but we love the service even more! My sister doesn't like iced boba (I know, she's super weird) and many places don't offer hot options. The cashier was awesome and even though they don't have it on the menu, gave it a shot to get her what she wanted. She loves the drink and we'll definitely be back.

I've been doing business with Cathie for almost 4 years.  This is my go to place for incense, soaps and cologne.  Cathie and her team is always helpful, accommodating and make you feel like family.  A special tip of the hat to Jeff! Always cheerful and helpful.  Thanks guys!

Oooohhhhhh My Gosh........what a perfect way to kickoff my Friday. Unfortunately I arrived with 1hr to spare before closing so my pie selection was limited to 4 choices. I opted to purchase 3 out of the  4. I ordered the small strawberry-basil pie $5, small chocolate-coconut-walnut pie $5 and a coconut cream pie Tartlet $3. Why.......were each of those pies deliciously tasty!!!! I mean I didn't expect each one to be as good as they were. If you love pie or are looking for a sweet treat to tickle your fancy or need dessert for a dinner party or gift, you should definitely go here. The crust is light and flaky with a smooth taste that compliments the pie and the fillings are each soooo flavorful and delectable with the appropriate amount of sweetness. My mother makes the best coconut cream pie and it's soo hard to find one that even comes close, but the coconut cream pie here is hands down the best if you don't want to slave over a hot stove, stirring that homemade custard base. I can't wait to return to try their other flavors. I have to give credit to my fellow Helpers and of course Sauce magazine for my newest hookup.

.
My husband and I come here every morning when we're in Boise visiting family.  We live in Washington State, where there's good coffee, but no place as great as this.  Yum!

I love this place! Cheap good food with New Orleans charm . Make sure you have cash. It's a cash only establishment.   Everything is good.  My favorite is the  fried oyster po boy. A half of a po-boy is plenty for most ladies. A whole po-boy can feed 3 young children.

This looks like your typical hole in the wall Chinese restaurant in Chinatown, but in downtown Narberth.   Let me preface this by saying that I love the Empress Garden in Chinatown Philly (funny thing is that a friend who lived in Taiwan told me about Empress Garden unprompted - and I told him it was my favorite place in Chinatown)

Anyway, back to the China King.

As I walked in I was greeted by a very friendly lady and she was patient with me as I scanned the many options.  We were in the middle of a move and had nowhere to cook so I thought we'd give this a try. 

Decided to go with some typical fare:  
2 orders of dumplings
Orange Chicken
Pad Thai
Beef & Green Bean something or other.

Everyone thought the food was great. 
Kids loved the dumplings and Orange Chicken 
Adults loved the Pad Thai and Beef and Green Beans. 

All in all was great!  In fact, I'm getting ready to place another order as I write this review. : )

This place was awesome!

It was a pleasant surprise to find the best Chicago style deep dish dish pizza in southwest New Jersey.

The crust was amazing and the cheese was perfectly baked into the crust. The sauce, tomatoes and sausage were right in there as well.

The Deep Dish Mac & Cheese was very flavorful and had a nice crunchy cheese crust. 

The service was among the best day you had any where it anytime as our server Vinny was so helpful and pleasant and had whatever we needed.

They were even so kind as to switch off the monster trucks from the TV and put on the Phillies game.

This is a great place that I highly recommend to anybody who wants an excellent casual dinner experience in this area.

This use to be my fav restaurant about 3yrs ago. I use to go frequently but stopped for awhile and went back again recently in August for my moms bday, and it did not meet my expectations. I ordered sea bass, it had a weird taste my mom tasted it and immediately almost gagged at the strong taste of ammonia. I told waiter about it and got the lamb chops instead which were chewy. No one at the table was impressed with there order. It was edible, but for the price you expect it to be delicious! Service was great and they even gave my mom free fried doughnuts with sparklers for her bday. Food quality def. use to be better.

Great food, ambiance and the manager is so welcoming! The patio with live music is always going to win over my heart. The sushi is amazing, as well as the rest of the menu! But... super SLOW service, literally had to track down our waiter to take our order or get water, then he'd disappear super fast. The old fashions we ordered were pretty awful (however we are from Wisconsin and picky about our drinks). The biggest complaint I have is how expensive this place this, definitely overpriced for what you get/service! You can't charge five star prices at a patio with smoking, dogs, and beer!
It's rare I drive this far for Chinese food, but I stop here every time I'm in the area. Always delicious.  Hot braised chicken is a sure bet !!

Shrimp appetizer was great and the sweet and sour chicken was good. Unfortunately the other 2 entres were not good. We ordered Togo but the packaging was basically a paper box for very liquidy items, so sauce was everywhere and the boxes were falling apart. Was disappointed since 2 people found their meals inedible and there was a mess to clean up.

I was in Indpls for the holiday, and bummed that I didn't have time to go to my threading location for a clean up, and was thrilled to see this location on the way to my parents house! Speaking with Pam, I knew she'd do a great job! She's a licensed esthetician, and moved here from Canada. She using some space from her hisband's gas station, and I am thrilled with her work. I will be coming back here every time I'm in town now and telling all of my family about Pam!

The red chili stacked enchiladas with fried egg are amazing! This was a great place for dinner.  The table salsa was was nice blend of tomatoes. peppers, garlic and smoked paprika.  That was the welcome to what was even better.

The stacked enchiladas were simply fantastic.  Smothered in semi sweet, yet tangy red sauce that covered the soft corn tortillas and onions.  The fried egg on top made for a nice finishing touch.  Interesting to see them promoting RC soft drink products, something I haven't seem much of in my native Texas.

Ok...finally got around to visiting their new location (they recently moved).

They now have seats to chill on and it's a cute set up...but I'm about to lay down some critiques:

1) there's no WiFi (they should really look into offering that for customers)
2) there are a few "desks" and chairs, sorta like old school furniture. It's cool but not comfortable
3) the music during my visit has been rap/hip hop...with vulgar language at times...lots of "F bombs" and even that "N word" whoa (I don't mind the music but for a business, ehhhh)
4) my latte wasn't great, not bad...just not my fave

I'll be back, I like their look and feel somewhat, they did JUST open up here so they probably still need to work out a flow. There are 2 registers which can be helpful but customers don't know where to line up. 

When I walked in, I was the 3rd customer...I knew this but the guy behind the counter asked if I was ready to order. I told him, "thanks but it's actually her turn." It wasn't an issue but you can see where that could create tension.

I'm all for a new coffee shop where I can chill a bit and catch up on work. Maybe they're not looking for that here...perhaps they like the quick in/out approach. It's their business, they can do what they like...I'm just sharing some feedback.
Service was terrible the waitress always had smart remarks when she got something wrong and the food itself was bland. Hire people with actual customer service skills.

I'd keep my money or give to Jimmy Johns next door. Place serves garbage. Brown lettuce, stale ingredients, doesn't listen to customers order. Almost everytime is a let down. Owner needs to stay at home instead of screwing over customers (he is saving money by making sandwiches himself!)... For 12+ bucks go you can go anywhere else.

Not bad, the Hibachi grill was really good. Typical buffet, very good variety, the sushi was quite underwhelming, but the hibachi grill was above average. Not sure why, but there were at least a dozen pregnant women eating there at the time, none of them were together or in a group.

I am only giving 1 star because there is not a negative star option! I went with 3 other friends. I was in town visiting from Atlanta and wanted some crab legs. First,  the parking is horrible. It's a little lot behind the building and you just have to pray that nothing happens to your car. We go on in and end up seating ourselves. It's a Tuesday night so it doesn't seem to be that busy. Our waitress took forever to come over to us to take our order. It took us 15 minutes for our sodas to come. Well over 45 minutes for our food to come out. Finally when the food came out only 2 dishes came out. Or other 2 guests had to wait about another 10 minutes for their food and they were missing items off their platters. My crab legs were actually delicious...I don't know if it's because I was super hungry or what,  but my friends were very disappointed with their food. Their seafood platters were fried... No seasoning whatsoever. The waitress barely came over to check on us... At this point with the service...I had figured since gratuity is included in all checks over $50 why would she give good service. Her ass is guaranteed a tip regardless. We finish up our meals I asked for a separate check for my food (only because I had ordered additional food to go for my friend who wasn't able to make it). I was then told we couldn't separate checks when you sit in the dining room. I don't know if the server was making it up as she went because she didn't feel like separating the check.  No where on the menu did it not say you can't separate checks. The check was given to us... $160... are you kidding me??? She charged us for every soda refill... Didn't even give any kind of discount for the horrible service or for the 2 other friends in the party who were missing part of their platter. It's cool... We will pay and she WILL NOT get any additional tip out. 

It's really sad when you go out to eat to local establishments instead of these franchise restaurants and you have to regret supporting the local guy. The owner of this place really needs to re evaluate the nickel and diming policy and his wait staff. I am a server back home so it's very easy for me to tip more especially when good service is provided. I come home to Philly about 2 times a year sometimes more and I really look forward to checking out new places to eat and supporting small business. This establishment...I WILL NOT BE BACK... Nor would I recommend anyone to this place. Out of 4 entrees... Mine should not be the only one that was good. 

I don't know what this review will actually do for this business or even if the owner cares about this review. They look like they have been in business for a while,  but it's very unfortunate patrons don't know any better and it's become the norm and so common and acceptable for bad service at an establishment. I work very hard for my money and I don't mind spending it... But this establishment should somehow be held accountable and know that the people they hire from front of the house to back of the house should give consistent good service and good food. The purpose of people meeting up with friends and going out to eat is to have a good time. The highlight of the night should not be how awful of a time they had from service to food. Smh.

I ordered a pizza and have been delivered several times with no sauce being on the pizza. I called and requested another pizza, despite the rudeness of the associate. They sent me another pizza that was completely smashed. When I called to get a refund, I was put on hold and was hung up on. I called back and spoke to a manager. I was offered a store credit but I requested a cash refund, as I do not plan on ordering from Pizza Hut again. They always mess up my order and I would not recommend anyone to either Smyrna location. I will say the manager was very apologetic and called the GM to grant the cash refund. That is the only reason I'm giving 2 stars instead of one.

I enjoy the pho here at Tai Pan's. The broth is delicious. I get their slice rare steak bowl every time (see my photos) and have been coming here for years. The mint/jalapeno/cilantro/bean sprout side with the pho is always very fresh. Service is great and the Eastside location is wonderful for me and very close to the Park Place mall. The Chinese dishes here are only okay. There are much better places elsewhere if you feel like Chinese. We always were able to find seating and service is fast.

It's been a while since I've been here and so we decided to come here for dinner. It wasn't too busy when we got here which was nice. I ordered the Ahi Tuna burger with sweet potato fries on the side and it came out like a master piece. The bun was super soft and the Ahi Tuna slices were nice and thick. My sweet potato fries were also very crunchy and fresh. It made me wonder why I haven't been here more often! My boyfriend ordered the chicken burger and it also looked and tasted delicious. The service was good since it wasn't so busy. I am definitely coming back here again for food. They have a good selection of local beers as well. Local beers for $5 on certain days and they also have wing nights. Check out their specials it's pretty worth it! The only complaint that I would say I had was the water. Water is served out of these clear glass bottles... That look pretty old. I have a feeling that they pre pour water into these bottles and then give them to tables. It didn't look fresh... or perhaps the glass bottles had hard water stains on them or calcium stains? But that kind of threw  me off. I didn't really drink water so it didn't really matter perhaps this was just a one off... Other then the water thing I think the overall quality of food and service was good. I am definitely going to come  back here for food again!

We got into Nashville after an early morning flight out of Detroit and needed coffee. But not just any coffee would do because I had done my research and knew that Crema was somewhere we needed to try. 

The atmosphere inside is very nice - cozy and trendy - with coffee and merchandise attractively displayed without interfering with the ability to order and enjoy coffee. There's lots of seating if you walk around the corner, but we were able to sit near the espresso bar. There were hipsters everywhere - always an excellent sign when you're looking for coffee. 

On the advice of the barista we both tried the bourbon barrel sorghum lattes and they were just perfect. Creamy, not at all bitter, with a roasty, dark sugar taste that complemented rather than overwhelmed the espresso. (If you haven't had it, sorghum is like molasses without a metallic taste that you've likely not noticed unless you've tasted it to compare the two.) I paired my latte with a pear and rosemary scone that was almost perfect - not too sweet with just enough rosemary. It wasn't as flaky as I like my scones to be but I wasn't under the impression that they make them on site and it was a bit later in the morning so allowances have to be made.

Crema offers coffee classes that I would have loved to participate in but we were only in Nashville for a couple of days around New Year's Eve and there were none planned. Next time we're in town we'll have to give it another shot. But classes or not, Crema is definitely worth a visit.

My daughter and I ate here for dinner after attending a nearby birthday party.   It wasn't busy and we were seated right away.  Our order was taken promptly.  I ordered the Carnitas dinner.  It was "different" than any carnitas I had ever ordered before and I've eaten hundreds of carnitas of all styles before.  I could tell they took pork roast and cut it into cubes long before the roast was tender.  I believe, upon ordering, they must take those cubes and fry them to reheat and give it the texture carnitas generally have.  I was given two very small tortillas so I constructed my carnitas "taco" and found that even when doused in salsa that was on the table for the tortilla chips, it nearly choked me going down.  VERY tough and so dry I thought it might actually get stuck in my throat going down.  Our waitress did not visit our table during the 20-25 mins after our plates were delivered to the table.  In fact, because we were way off in a corner not anywhere near the other occupied tables, it was hard to get anyone's attention.  I thought that maybe I just need to make the best of this dinner and attempted to eat a couple more bites.  It was the same but worse now that I was focused on how it was SO DRY and TOUGH.

When our waitress finally did make an appearance, I told her about the problem with the carnitas and she apologized and said "I hope you at least liked the service."  I tried not to let my jaw hit the ground considering a) she didn't address that my food was nearly untouched and I just said it was inedible, b) she made no attempt to fix the problem, and c) she seemed only concerned about making sure she got a good tip.   

I asked for our bill and there was no adjustment for the fact that my dinner was nearly untouched.  She picked up my credit card and when she returned to the table, she placed my credit card and receipt in front of my 9 year old.  Hmmmm, what to think when the waitress comes to the table and places the credit card across the table from me directly in front of my 9 year old.  One thing is for sure, my 9 year old cannot sign the receipt and determine a tip.  ;-)  Needless to say, I will never go back and do not recommend them.  I think there are far better Mexican restaurants to choose from.

Had a phenomenal experience getting my Company Truck serviced.

Richard (Store Manager) & Terry (Assistant Store Manager) handled my vehicle with phenomenal care and their customer service should be the standard for all locations. Great conversation as well, awesome team here.

First Pep Boys experience and it was a memorable one, I live nearby in Belleair bluffs so I will certainly be back

Meh. The food is decent, our waiter was nice but this is such a "scene" place - in PHILLY. The trance/house is thumping/loud - so much that my husband and I could barely hear each other talk. The tables are teeny/cramped, and you're guaranteed to get smacked in the elbow at least twice while you're eating. The kitchen is also really slow...one app and two pastas = hour+ meal. 

The lobster spaghetti was pretty good, but the fettuccine was just ok. If you're down with trying to eat some decent Italian with "Castle in the Sky"-esque music, you might like it but there are so, so many other options in Rittenhouse.

I have come to this place for 2 years. I have tried going to places closer to where I live but they just disappointed me. Here they don't rush you out the door. Their aim
Is to please so iif something is not to your liking let them know. It's busy for a reason but if you can come in the middle of the day during the work week then you won't have to wait. 

They are also on top of the latest trends. And they are very CLEAN!!!  The pedicure tubs get scrubbed not just wiped down.
Prices are good but meat, deli, bakery and produce quality is lacking. Most beef cuts are tough as shoe leather. Bakery dosen't offer decent load of fresh rye bread. You get what you pay for.

It's a nice small laundry mat. It's was the only one I found open on Sunday morning. 8am The place was dirty. Trash needed to be emptied and the floor needed sweeping. Top loaders 1.50. Front loaders 2.25. Big front loader 3.50 Dryers .25 for 6 mins. Just O dryer for 10 mins. Got a restroom there.

Was walking the French quarter this weekend and saw this cafe decided to try something new, and so glad we did. The staff was friendly made the ambiance and experience awesome. Had the Heart Stopper...so very worth it, it's everything your doctor says not to eat. Drinks were awesome too, they made us an amazing fresh juice Hurricane no mixers, talk about refreshing. Went in the evening on a Saturday and sat outside, great location could still hear Bourbon St but less of a crowd. Friends had the Shrimp burger and truffle fries said they were amazing. Would recommend and definitely going back as a regular place to eat and drink.

Since I reviewed the Drew Street Library, I thought I would also review this one. It is big, clean and very modern. The staff are friendly,helpful and seem happy to be there. There are lots of special activities and events there. A full bank of computers and wifi. They have a little book store. A giant movie and music collection. On the second floor they have an upright piano which they let anyone play. It overlooks the water and a park.  Tax payer dollars being spent in the best possible way. Love this place.

Pretty good for a bar and grill. I wish they served teriyaki sauce with there wings. But overall I had a pretty good experience and the staff is very welcoming! This pace is usually pretty packed during dinner time (weekends),  so I would suggest getting there early!

Just tried a juice cleanse today --- the juices are all really great! The price (65) is really worth it for 3-4 lbs of veggies and fruits per bottle and they give you purified citrus water and two E3/Aloe shots to go along with the 6 juices (though the E3 shot is really bitter-- but no complaints, it's the real stuff). The juice glasses are super cute and you can tell everything is really fresh. Great job!

I didn't even know this place was here! The decor inside is adorable and the music is really nice. Super good ambiance. We ordered every taco on the menu, it took about 15 minutes to get out to us but they were all so delicious! The beef and pork ones were definitely our favorites.

One of my favs in New Orleans ...  Long ago when I lived in Uptown, I used to work at The Alibi (on Iberville right next to the back of Galatoire's) and the boyz from the restaurant would drop off crab stuffed eggplant (soooooooo good and still one of the best dishes on the menu in my opinion).

Food is phenomenal, atmosphere high-class, and superior service :)

Love this studio. Everyone is friendly and the sculpt classes are killer (S/O to Andrea, Megan, Beka and Gabby) and I also love the C2 classes (Madeline, Kristina and Brandon). I find alternating gives my body a break from weights but I still get a great workout at both classes. The weekend classes are always extra hard, which I love... or maybe that's just in my head? Haha 

I'm no advanced yogi but I do recommend the classes for everyone!! They're FUN, positive and leave you feeling refreshed mentally and physically :)

Armature works is the place to eat a nice lunch or dinner with a great view of Tampa skyline. I had to pleasure to enjoy a Shoyu Ramen from Ichicoro Ramen. The broth was very savory and flavorful. The components of the ramen included pork belly(amazing), bamboo shoots, egg and of course the noodles. The ramen was very delicious and great for the price. Can not wait to come back and try another meal at this wonderful location for food and a great time with other food lovers.
I've been here three times now and was never served (in a group of 4) in under an hour. The food is fine but the service is really bad. Undertrained, understaffed, patently unhelpful.
Meridian's best supermarket chain. Homegrown and better than the other chain headquartered in Boise. Good selection of produce, meat and bulk foods. Friendly staff.
Beatiful yard and nice setting. Great food! All the chop/steak are terrific. Best dining experience we had in New Orleans

I've been combing over the two and a half hours I spent at Etch, and I can't seem to find a single reason why this place would deserve less than 5 stars. Simply put, this was one of - if not the - best meal I've had in Nashville. 

The drinks were quite fantastic, and the wine list was extensive. The Butter Tasting pops up in so many reviews for a reason - it's a wonderfully enjoyable and unusual experience. The entrees were cooked to perfection and presented with care, with so many unconventional flavors combining in ways you'd never expect. 

Add a nice atmosphere, combined with a knowledgeable, courteous, helpful, and all-around excellent staff, and you've got a must-visit in the Nashville fine dining scene.

Cannot recommend this place enough. Must try: (Obviously EVERYTHING) but the Pink Lady, the Knight,  and the Tasty Pop. Cannot tell you beautiful they are!  The Tasty Pop and the Night have this beautiful lemon zest to them, and taste BEAUTIFUL with a Bottle of Butter Chardonnay (ooooh girl) and the pink lady has this amazing mae ploy sauce on it that just goes with the rest of the roll.  OH and the Yakiton is like a seafood eggroll. Literally a seafood eggroll. Who doesn't love eggrolls?  It's amazing. Just go. Try it all. But try the three rolls I mentioned above because they'll hook you and then you'll want to go all the time. I even convinced my sushi non liking husband to enjoy eating here! GO!

I'm giving it a four it was a nice restaurant but it wasn't something that I would pick out I had one small slice of steak and one sausage with rice and beans tomatoes cucumber and a slice of pie and it cost me $41 because I didn't get nothing to drink except water but it was a Christmas party for Work and that's where everybody wanted to go but I'll will definitely not come back again too expensive for my blood

I felt cool just walking into this place. It had an awesome vibe. It's almost entirely lit by candles which gives it a nice speakeasy feel without having to wait forever to get in. The beer list is impressive and the cocktails were outstanding and incredibly reasonably priced. 

My boyfriend and I stopped in before meeting friends for dinner and loved it so much that we decided to go back after dinner. This place manages to be a great date place AND a great place to drink with friends. 

I will definitely be returning soon.
Food was excellent. Piping hot and huge portions. I know what I'm having for dinner tomorrow!

Me and my girlfriend just had a date night here.  Everything was great! Our waiter John was soo nice! He was new but I hope he's our waiter the next time we go here (btw we're definitely coming back). The manager on was also very nice.  Overall great experience! Definitely recommend!

Order from this spot a couple times a week. They have my favorite crispy noodles for the soup,home made not the tiny dry noodle strip.Bbq ribs and fried wings are solid.  Enjoyed the pork dumplings and dinner specials.
Best happy hour in Germantown!  It also has a great patio area if you're dining with dogs.  It's a great neighborhood spot

I'm sooooo flippin glad we received a gift card to this karaoke/bar!

It's a separate restaurant all attached in case we wanted to just chill in a family environment or karaoke and have some drinks.

As soon as I walked in the customer service was on point, the Kareoke Host/Security was on top of everything, though he ran the place for a sec because of how attentive he was. The waitresses was awesome as well.

I had to change my baby and as soon as I asked where th bathroom was, they offered me a conference room were it was more private and safe (covid). 

I am extremely excited to say that we are big fans of wonderland (nightly kareoke sec of restaurant with separate doors and section away from the family restaurant side but all in the same building).

This Is The Hidden Jewl that everyone looks for that ain't crammed or crazy, just relaxed, country/rock/alternative place to relax and enjoy a peaceful but fun environment!

THE BLACK SKULLS WILL RETURN!
THIS TIME WITH THE WHOLE CREW LOL
I went with my wife and older daughter and baby, it was nice because karaoke started early enough to were my kids weren't out late or anything like that. Def a family environment!

I didn't get the name of the bada$$ host/security (tall, husky, homie looking, chill and Professional) and the waitress (no offense: the shorter one lol) But I'll tell you what, THEY MASTERED CUSTOMER SERVICE FOR SURE!!! 

I been to olive garden, red lobster, blah blah and these guys smoked them by far!!

Thank You Guys!
Scythe and The Black Skulls Will See You Soon!
With A Nice Fat Tip  

Good job guys!
According to their website, La Cite Francophone has decided to cancel their Sunday markets this season!

This is my first Greene Turtle experience so I can only give this review based off of my one lunch at this specific location. 

Walking in, I noticed the interior was clean and well kept which I appreciated. They were able to fit my party of 7 into a side booth and were quick with drink orders. For food I ordered the Crabby Melt off of the lunch special menu with a side of fries.

...Now cue the 40 minute wait time for our food to come out. We ordered mostly sandwiches and burgers so I'm not sure why our wait was so long. When my food got to me I found that the grilled sourdough was very oily, resulting in a much heavier lunch than I was expecting. The crab dip inside the sandwich had a good flavor and I can see myself ordering the crab dip appetizer next time. The side of fries were simply OK. 

For the type of restaurant this was, I expected the prices to be much cheaper. This seems like a laid-back, hangout spot with beer and burgers so I wasn't prepared to see the menu items reflecting prices you would see at classier joints. The average price of a dish was around $13. There are definitely places around that serve the same type of food at much cheaper prices.

Overall, a decent place to chill with friends or coworkers. Be prepared to wait for your food and look past your budget.
The place is rely fancy and cool like a movie star place.  My mom said she did not like the crabby legs.  They are small and was mad that they are little.  I hope I can go back there.

I try to always support local businesses, however this is one I won't be returning to. They were all college kids which was great, but they talked to me like I was stupid and didn't tell me anything about my oil change. They didn't say anything about the fluids, filters, etc. they handed me my keys, charged me and sent me out. Never once mentioning my free car wash. Then when I asked about it, they seemed annoyed at having to wash my car.

The coffee shop at Hobeys is by far one of the best values in town! I use to go in for their breakfast special when it was just over two bucks, many moons ago! It is over twice that now but still a value! BTW: I stopped going in for breakfasts on a regular basis due to the effect they had on my waistline.
    We recently had a late night dinner there, the specials. A pork chop diner and a thing called the "Belly Buster"! And it almost did,and I got a big belly to bust! The last time I tried one of these monsters , I cut it in half and brought it home! For $ 6.75 you get the biggest burger I have ever seen, with enough beefy territory to be covered with four slices of cheese! Top that off with a pile of fries and you got a Belly Buster! Good luck!

A perfect dinner to celebrate my son's birthday. Accommodating hostesses, and attentive service. Nice selection of appetizers, small menu plates, and sides. My son had crab cakes which he enjoyed. We enjoyed watching our server making my mom's dinner on the side of our table 'Sautéed Jumbo Prawns' - that's a plus for entertainment! Chilean Sea Bass is satisfying! I'll definitely come back and dine at Bimini again - oh and the 20% local discount is a PLUS!!!

Tried this place three times in last three years. Food is just awful. I am pretty easy to please when it comes to restaurants but they are consistently bad. Service is slow. Food is bland. Move on for other Mexican options.

If you are highly motivated by beer - you're gonna have a good time here. Wide selection of beer, from the foreign to the freshest of fresh, and even a lovely Irish Cider you really don't see out and about much.

I want to set aside the beer component of MKT for a moment and just talk about the food. I have long had a mixed opinion of the Century groups enterprises. While always a fan of Delux Burger Bar, trips to the Century Room have been hit and miss, and 100 just always struck me as incredibly weird. I was there once in a suit and felt massively under dressed. (No, it was not my birthday suit.)

So it was with some trepidation a friend and I visited MKT a week ago Wednesday for lunch, to see what it was all about. Hot off a decent Edmonton Journal review, I was optimistic.

I got very worried when the waitress informed me that the soft pretzels were off the menu, since they had not come in yet as the truck was running late. Little red alarm bells fired in my head: soft pretzels are so easy to make, I'm really only expecting frozen premade pretzels from Rexall Place and Commonwealth Stadium, or a chain event like Elephant and Castle.

My meditation on "what does this *mean* about the kitchen?" was interrupted by the waitress informing me that while the computer button was still disabled, the kitchen indeed was prepared to serve pretzels.

The brief rejoicing was interrupted by the pretzels. Bland, dry, tough, no sign of seasoning on the crust. Sure, the sauce accompaniments were tasty but cheese sauce and two mustards are hard to really give credit for.

I expected my pulled pork sliders to be a safe bet, seeing as it draws from the Delux stable of tasty burgers-n-things. Unfortunately the bread was very dry, and the filling just tasted of the slaw, with the slightest hint of pork. The side was fresh made chips, but at least a quarter of the order was soggy.

My lunch partner had a Thai lettuce wrap appetizer as her main, and while the components were fresh enough they were the definition of unremarkable. The chicken seemed to be just squirted with a Thai sauce after grilling, with a few sauteed julienned veggies mixed in.

Don't get me wrong, it was all ...fine. But that's it. Just .... fine. Knock a few bucks off and strip the place of pretension and I might even eat there again.

By far the most disappointing part of the meal was the visit from the manager. When I started to answer her question about how the food was, she immediately directed me to fill out a comment card as they were "taken very seriously". I would have preferred to complete the conversation she initiated, thanks.

I will drink here any time (hey, wanna get a beer?), but I'm only going to be eating here when circumstances dictate, it's just not a place I'd choose.

There's good news and bad news here. First the good: 1. If you need gluten free food in Concourse E  at Lambert Field, this is your only option, and 2. The food is great, and not just for airport food. My son, who is vegetarian in addition to GF, had the cheese plate, I had white bean and chicken chili, and we split the marcona almonds. All were excellent. 

Now the bad. Even for airport food, the portion size per dollar was silly small. Truly ridiculous. I know rent is high here, but this is well beyond reasonable.  The chili was $11 for a one cup portion, with a little flatbread. The cheese plate was insultingly small for $12. Not good, even when you have customers over a barrel.
I have an egg allergy and can't have them. I always make that clear when ordering a breakfast burrito to leave egg out of it. They put egg in and when I brought it back the lady said I asked for it.

The restaurant is big with a large patio. They have a lot of egg choices. I got the Greek Frittata  open face omelette with ham,artichoke hearts,roasted tomatoes,asparagus ,mushrooms with basil pesto and havarti dill cheese cooked in a iron skillet oh so good it comes with a side. Fresh fruit or grits or ranch potatoes they are the best. They also have sandwich and salads. The staff very friendly and knows what there doing.

I've eaten here many times and it is consistently good.  This time, I tried the soft shell crab special and some dim sum-shrimp ball plus a crab and shrimp dumpling.  My better half had salt and pepper shrimp plus a shark fin dumpling.

There must be new ownership, because the recipe for the salt and pepper shrimp had changed and they now use (an unecessary) breading on the shrimp which completely changed the flavor.  The soft shell crab was overcooked.  The service was poor.  The food came out all at once-appetizers and main course together.

The rating is now much lower than before.  Get your act together, please, you used to be excellent.
Chicken biscuit is the way to go; perfectly cooked chicken-crisp, moist & seasoned. Service was wonderful, as well.

I rode in the Smokey Mary this year so I'm probably a bit biased, but even just as a spectator, Orpheus is a pretty fantastic parade.  The floats themselves were gorgeous, I went to a preview party at Mardi Gras World a couple weeks before and it was so awesome seeing so many of them up close!  

Orpheus starts at Tchoupitoulas/Napoleon near Tipitinas, proceeds up Napoleon to St. Charles, then proceeds along the typical Uptown route all the way to the Convention Center.  It's a night parade too and the grand finale on Lundi Gras, so you get to see all of the amazing lighting effects on pretty much the entire route; this isn't true of Endymion.  The marching bands are amazing and the 610 stompers were in the parade this year so that was always fun.  The throws are awesome as well, I got a mini plastic light up guitar, a tambourine, flute, collectible cup, and a whole bunch of other stuff this year.  They also kept the music pumping throughout so the entire crowd, riders, spectators, everyone, was having a great time.  Orpheus is also cool because it's the only one of the 3 Superkrewes (others are Endymion & Bacchus) that is co-ed.  

If I could only make it to 2 parades (but let's be honest, I go to almost all of them), Orpheus would definitely be on that list.  I definitely recommend watching it near the beginning on St. Charles Avenue, where it isn't as crowded and there aren't any barricades, letting you almost walk right up to the floats.

I ordered the pho ga and shrimp summer roll. This was my first time ordering from here so I didn't know what to expect. Let me say I was more than pleasantly surprised! This was some of the best pho and summer rolls I've ever had! The chicken, shrimp and rice noodles tasted so fresh. I like that they had lots of cucumber in the roll. Oftentimes, I feel like I'm not given enough of the seasoning and extras to add to the broth but they gave more than enough. So yummy!

You want some pretty dang decent BBQ in Tucson? This is the spot! The only reason I'm not giving it 5 stars is because the seating area is tiny and we had to wait a while to get a table. But if you're not worried about the heat you can always choose to sit outside and work on a sunburn.  

I highly recommend getting the sampler so you can try a bit of everything! Good stuff, the ribs are to die for! You wont be disappointed.

I am going to close this account and go elsewhere. Here's why.

I've had my accounts here (3 of them), for more than 10 years. One of these accounts is with my husband, the other two are my own.

Recently, a smallish check (in comparison to my balance) was made out to my husband, who countersigned it to me because the check is for money owed to me. When I attempted to deposit this check in my account, the representative told me that according to Wells Fargo policy, my husband must be present because they had no proof he had actually signed the check.

I raised HELL!!! A "Customer Service Rep", whatever the hell that is, came over and told me there was nothing they could do. I didn't believe her, so I called Wells Fargo's 800 number, and the rep confirmed their "policy," which she insisted, was there to "protect you the customer."

If managers and supervisors are not allowed to override policies like this when an account merits it, then there is absolutely no point in banking here since I do so only as a matter of convenience. This bank pays a lot less than Schwab does for the privilege of having my money on deposit. Additionally, Reno has a local bank if I want to have a regular bank account somewhere. I'll just have to drive a little further.

Before I change to another bank, I'm going to find out about their policy for depositing checks first. Once burned, twice shy.

Bye bye Wells Fargo. You can stick your immovable policy where the sun don't shine.

Awesome:
- The main floor is a piano bar.
- The second floor is a dance party with great tunes.
- The walls of the dance floor are mirrored (check out my bad self and these moves like MJ!).

The not so cool: 
- No glasses of water, only bottles for purchase. Which leads me to...
- Peeps be rip-roarin' wasted on you name it. Hence the charge for water. So try not to get dehydrated while working up that sweat, and if you do, save a few extra dollars. Why? 
- Cash only.
Great breakfast Food ..,  service was good & friendly every time @ Waffle House .... Great Hang0veR FooD !!!

Love this place! It's clean and bright, serving great food made fresh in small batches. Manager Zoe and her staff are putting out amazing food in a super friendly environment. I loved the Super Burrito.  It was huge and delicious! We'll be back often!!!

Tried it out tonight with my husband as we're newly local & looking for a close sushi option. Got shu Mai (sp?)/shrimp dumplings- yum! Tender shrimp & wrapper, ok sauce. 
I'm pregnant (no raw for me.. :( ) so got the Angry Dragon & Dragon rolls, hubs got Eagle & shared mine. Shrimp tempura in AD was excellent - super tender & flavorful. Could've been more eel in D roll but good flavor & texture. Spicy tuna in E roll was said to be great too. 
Appreciated they placed raw & cooked on separate plates. 
Very attentive service - must've had 4 people refilling water, clearing plates, checking on us, etc. 
nice ambiance, good food. Will be taking the kids back in the future & trying out the Thai dishes!

I pass by this place on my way home and it's the best ice cream shop in the world. The staff is always friendly and they answer all my questions about blends. Even if its packed the line goes really fast.

Recently moved from NoLibs to Doylestown (we kick ourselves daily for doing so) and we had been wanting to try Honey for some time.  Decided to give it a go on a week night, no reservation, just walk in.  We got there for an early seating, around 6pm and the restaurant was completely empty. Before I could even put my umbrella down and look up the hostess quickly asked... Do you have a reservation? No hello, nothing. Fine whatever, we told her no sorry we didn't.  Without a word she grabbed her book and headed toward the back... Um okay? After about 5 minutes she came back and said she couldn't seat us until 9:30. NOW, I get it, I've work both FOH and BOH so I know it's a pain in the ass when folks come waltzing into your packed restaurant during prime hours without a res. And expect to be seated. However, the place was empty AND it was raining cats and dogs outside, lightening and all.
