Excellent service. Very detailed oriented Ana was great. I like the reward system which gives you discounts. Friendly and accommodating!

So far, my experience with this gym has been good.  However, I have to agree with one review about the water on the floor in the locker room and restrooms.  It has nothing to do with "someone's grandma" - the water is a hazard to everyone walking through. The tile should be replaced with some kind of non-slip tile, and there should also be a runner in the middle of the room, going from the locker room and showers to the rest room.

Really tasty jerk chicken, nice rice and peas and plantain.  I am not as crazy about the patties, but hey!  The rib "sandwich" is a monster.  Very nicely prepared food, exceedingly well priced -- and pretty popular at lunch, so expect to wait as each order is prepared one at a time.

First--I've not actually been here, because they canceled my reservation. My cousin's daughter was turning 21 and we wanted to have drinks on a rooftop--they are from out of town and came to visit us in Nashville to celebrate. I made the reservation several weeks ahead of time, because there were 8 of us and it's hard to wing it with that many people. The day before, I received a confirmation text, and I did confirm. 

The day of--ONE HOUR before our reservation, I received a text canceling our reservation for a "private party." No further explanation. I called, and the phone rang and rang. Rest assured I'll never give them my money. We had to completely recalibrate our birthday plans with 8 people on the fly, on a Friday night in Nashville--no easy task.

I had been meaning to come here for the longest time, and when Living Social came up with a $10 voucher for $20 worth of books, my backlog of reading material ceased to be a legitimate excuse. It took two people a solid hour to fill a big bag full of $20 worth of books (with tax, we went a little over), half made up of stuff we had been meaning to read, and the other half a somewhat random selection by authors we enjoyed. 

Most paperbacks are just a buck or two, and they cover just about every genre, so you're bound (!) to find something of interest. And the resident cat is a perfectly giant sweetheart. 

I just wish the place were bigger or better organized, as a lot of books are stacked in piles with spines to the side or wall and others are in plastic storage bins on shelves. 

Still, definitely check this place out before hitting up one of the chains or online bookstores.

We've been wanting to visit here for awhile, as I know the family who owns it is super sweet. They're from Cholula Puebla in Mexico and have signature items from their city on the menu (such as the mole). 

LOCATION: For some reason, this place seems hard to see from the road. The windows are tinted, so when you drive by, you can't see in. I think it would help a lot to lighten up the windows and add some outdoor string lights to add a festive vibe to the exterior. The interior is huge and inviting, so want them to express that on the outside too! There's a large parking lot right outside, so accessibility is super easy.

SERVICE: Our server was the nicest woman ever. She was incredibly smiley, friendly and attentive. We really loved her! A man came out to deliver our food and was incredibly nice too. Our drinks were constantly filled and we felt really well taken care of.

FOOD: I really loved the menu! I was surprised with some new menu items that I haven't seen out before. For example, they had bowls with your choice of protein (what I ordered), as well as 'healthy quesadillas' that were made on spinach flour tortillas with vegetables in the quesadilla. They also had guacamole and chorizo burgers, as well as great esquite (corn with chile, cotija cheese, mayo + lime juice). I REALLY enjoyed the guacamole we ordered, as well as my steak bowl. Mmmm.

DRINKS: They have an extensive drink menu, with tons of margaritas, mojitos, craft cocktails, beers and more.

Definitely come check out this family-run spot! It's a good one!

I've been here about 4 times and this is the only time I would have rated it a 3.5. They finally did a good pedicure, with clear and direct instruction from me. She was quick and good. I will definitely try this location again as it seems to have gotten better.

Flatbread Community Oven is on the East Side of Boise in The Marketplace at Bown Crossing at 3139 South Bown Way.  Once you pass the stacks of firewood at the entryway you can't miss the colorful bins of gelato in the deli case or the giant brick oven at center stage, either.  Flatbread presents a trendy atmosphere with mossy green walls, unusual light fixtures, stained concrete floors and a young wait staff. 

Dine indoors or out.  Inside there's the entrance dining area that has a large concrete community table, several small tables along the windows, and a bar area facing the brick oven.  (If acoustics are a concern seek outdoor seating.)  Beyond this eating area is a larger dining room with several tables placed so close to one another they lack privacy, plus patrons are forced to weave in and out to visit the restrooms so be certain to request a booth farther back if possible.  There's a terrific outside patio lined with string lights, tangerine umbrellas, and several tables that encircle a big fire pit. 

The menu consists of interesting appetizers such as Tuscan Lettuce Wraps (roasted rosemary chicken, pancetta, grapes, fontina cheese and herbs) and Baked Goat Cheese with Fire Roasted Tomatoes served with focaccia.  There are tasty Flatbreads like the sundried tomato, artichoke and ricotta; and a portion of these sales goes to the Idaho Foodbank.  Focaccia sandwiches, pasta and salads help round off the rather extensive Neapolitan pizza menu.  For $4.95 a child's meal of noodles, pizza or macaroni & cheese comes with a beverage and cookie.  Dessert offerings are comprised of fruit crostata, gelato and cookies. 

The "Pick Two" for $8.95 is the most popular.  Diners can choose two items: any pizzetta, half a sandwich, half salad, macaroni & cheese or soup.  It's available daily from 11 to 4.  We presumed Pick Two would be relatively quick as the small pizzetta shouldn't take too much time cooking in a hot oven but from the time of arrival to food being served was over half an hour.  Despite the unacceptable wait, the food was really quite good!  The soup of the day was a roasted tomato soup and although delicious the portion did not come remotely close to filling the bowl half way.  Of our mini pizzas, the best one was the Plucked & Peppered pizzetta with a delicious combination of chicken sausage, mozzarella, garlic, green peppers and caramelized onions.  The Chicken Arugula Basil salad was interesting and flavorful yet lacked arugula.  Our peanut butter cookie with crunchy chopped nuts was soft in the middle and tasted incredible. 

A tabletop card listed happy hour Monday through Friday from 4 to 6 p.m. with $4 pizzettas, flatbreads, wine and beer. 

Visit their web site to view their menu, http://www.flatbreadpizza.com/pizza.htm

While you are at it sign up for their birthday mailing list to get special offers, too.

We tried this place two years ago and it was everything people said. We are back in the area and visited yesterday and ordered a large Cuban with potato salad to go. Once again, Barracuda did not disappoint. We are looking forward to eating here over the next four months it is so good. I am usually not a big pork lover however the pork in their Cuban is unbelievably good. Next time I go I am trying the Margaritas!
Thought I was going to Wing Stop but to my surprise it's now this new place. The food was just okay. The fries needed salt and the hottest wings they had weren't hot at all. Friendly staff though.

The area outside is nice to sit out on a cool day. The inside was nice also. We chose to sit outside. There was seating right away but it is a Tuesday evening. Time between ordering and the food getting to the table long, almost everything took a while so have patients. This was my first time, the food was  I probably will not be back. There was no kid's menu but alternate was offered. The expensive prices doesn't fit the taste of the meal. I think ambiance is what you pay for. I poured crushed pepper on my pasta to get it down. I hate leaving bad reviews but I also hate paying for food thats not really

Solely based on take out

Hubby went to go PICK UP The Vegetarian lo mein for $10.99 and a fish dish with rice

Both very good! Wow

Even my kids ate it 

The lo mein was so good- it could've been a drop bigger but it was so good

Everyone was happy
Greatest sushi I have had in a while. I love there all you can eat bar. It's a great deal of you eat more than 2 or 3 rolls.

To be honest it could easy get a four star. The rooms were very large and nice. I basically had a one bedroom condo with large dinner table, full kitchen except oven, modern tvs, patio and furniture, great doc on the bay and a great pool. The location was also stellar, next to a great Italian spot, Publix, Walgreens etc. 

There was new tile floors, new granite, new paint crown moldings and more. 

All they had to do was put in new furniture and beds/bedding. They were cheap as they could be. I slept very poorly and my groom who stayed with me the night before had to get married with a crick in his neck. Sooooooo very close to being excellent. 

Made it very nice but forgot whats most important. A good nights sleep. Oh well.

Not the best pizza in the world, but far from the worst. The crust is pretty good - I'm one of those weirdos that doesn't actually eat the crust on pizza, because most of the time I find it just too bland and chewy. At Gianfranco, the crust is good enough that I eat the whole slice, if that tells you anything.

Can't say I've ever ordered a whole pie, but occasionally I pop in at lunch time and get a pretty cheap meal that fills me up. Lunch time is usually pretty busy, but the line seems to move steadily so it isn't too long of a wait. I've had a few of the flavors (chicken ranch always seems to be pretty popular with folks) but I think the tomato pie is my favorite. 

Solid lunch spot in Old City that fills you up and doesn't break the bank!

Tonight we ordered from Vetture's via Uber eats. We recently moved to the area and were looking for a local Italian restaurant. We were quite impressed. I had the eggplant Corey and my wife had the spaghetti and meat sauce. We also had the jalapeño poppers. Everything was so good, fresh and flavorful. We have found our new place and can't wait for the Covid restrictions to be lifted to check out the place in person.
Do not go they only treat their people like you should be treated if you are of different color they treat you like you don't belong in this country.

I've ordered the 8" Pepe 4 times in a row, only to get a kids turkey sandwich 2/4 times i got it. The other 2 times took over an hour to deliver and they never answered the store phone. Food is fresh, and the quality is still the same as any other, they just often mess up and take much longer than most. Wouldn't recommend.
Won't be going back here again, terrible service and we both got sick after our dinner. Save your tummy and go somewhere else! Very disappointed

Brought my dog in for a wash and trim, they complained how matted the dog was. We take good care of our dogs, When we got home I noticed him biting at his leg. Looked like he was burned by the blow dryer, took him to the animal hospital and his whole leg was burned. Never going back

Went here as a small group of 5. We waited about 30 minutes for anyone to approach is at the door. 
There were plenty of tables available.  A waitress apparently realized how long we had been waiting and found the missing hostess. 
We were seated at a booth. After waiting 45 minutes for anyone to approach our table and take orders, we left. 
I have no idea how the food is here since I never got a chance to order anything.

Only waited 15 minutes to be seated on Fiestas Saturday and were met with great service from our waitress and speedy food delivery. The bloody mary was on point along with the fried green tomatoes and fresh berries with whipped cream. We loved both the crab cake entree and wild mushroom omelet. 5 stars. Highly recommend.

Saw that this had 5 stars so we decided to try it..being from the northeast, where the Chinese food is the best, we have a hard time finding somewhere decent...the egg rolls were soft not crispy, the chicken was bland, the beef and broccoli no good, the sauce for the pot stickers was thick..thick? Needless to say we will not be back!

Had a great gel manicure at Pur nail spa! They lure you in with a glass of champagne and great customer service (only reason I'm giving 2 stars)! Unfortunately the manicure doesn't hold up so well. On my second day of my vacation my nails have already chipped! Only 4 days after I got them done!!! Gel is supposed to last for at least a week and a half if not two weeks!  So disappointed with the quality of of this manicure!! Don't waste your money here because you'll either be back a few days later to get them fixed or be in Hawaii with nails that look terrible after your spent $40 on them. Seriously bummed and won't be back!

UPDATE: I have changed my review to 5 stars because they refunded me! They offered to either redo them or refund me but since my toes (which I did at home) lasted longer, I figured I'd just take the refund.  Overall, not a great experience but at least they did everything they could to rectify the situation.

If you say bakery to me my eyes widened in my ears perk up! So I drive down to the bakery and meet Christine who is one of the owner bakers. I had called the day before to place my order all my breads were ready when I got there sliced bagged and marked. Walking in you notice huge Hobart mixers what fun from my old bakery days!Also ordered two sandwiches one was the Italian sandwich on Tampa Bay white bread the second was the BST with a boozy pig bacon! Both sandwiches are delicious tasty well seasoned could use a little more filling on that for the price but tasty and worth the bite.
I took one of each flavor bread plus half dozen-cinnamon rolls. 
The store has a very noticeable store front lots of glass with the name on front but the parking is tight they were only a few spaces in front of the shop. If you do miss the shop make your first right turn park in the next parking lot or around the block it was easy to get into the store. Fabulous and delightful bakery I want them to be there for ever!

For $200 of cost within the first  3 weeks then $79 every 3 weeks it is not worth the money. Nice people but, when you share your concerns they come to your home and photo the reasons why the product isn't working. ( plants with water in the pot etc)I gave it a try for 2 months but it's too expensive and provided minimal results.

Took a friend out to buffet lunch last Friday. We got there at about 12:30 and the place was virtually empty. No forks had to ask, no naan and a very limited buffet. Tried the fish curry and honestly the fish was so overcooked it was like chewing on an art gum eraser. Let's say it went downhill from there. The chicken tikka was so spicy my friend could barely eat it. Very disappointed with the quality of the food and service. So then we finished our meal and waited and waited to get our bill. The guy behind the counter was too busy screwing around on his cell phone to pay attention to the customers. I walked up to pay the bill and discovered this awful buffet was $13.99 per person plus they tack on a $1.20 service fee for using a credit card. Total rip-off don't waste your time or your money going to this disgusting and overpriced restaurant. Rest assured I will never be back and I'm sure this restaurant will be closed soon either for lack of business or by the health department.
Nice and open. Decent beer prices. Friendly bar staff. Great beer in a good atmosphere. We will definitely be coming back.

Stopping at the Morning Glory Diner was a happy accident, and happy we were. First, there is a dog friendly patio, which Reno and Ruby thoroughly enjoyed. Second, I loved the Lemon Nut Waffle! It came with this amazing whipped cream. Could have used more blueberries, so make sure you ask for the berry sauce. The waffles were so good with the berry sauce. Who doesn't love the tart & sweet combination of lemon and berries? I ordered a side of bacon. It was thick cut, and absolutely delicious. The coffee was just average, which was disappointing.

My husband got the biscuits and gravy special, and was very happy. I tried a bite of his potatoes, and they were delicious with a hint of rosemary.

After all the walking to and from the Garden District to the Convention Center for 4+ miles every day, I was looking for a tour that would pick me up and be a leisurely experience during my stay here the week of November 15th. The day before, I called and was able to book a 2 PM tour of New Orleans City for the next day. Even though I was out of the way, the guide, Darin Boue, whose family goes back almost 150 years in New Orleans, picked me up 1:30 in a large van/minibus before heading to gather the others. The van was almost full by the time we began, so probably you'll want to call well in advance during more peak season. Darin really made the tour interesting--he has a kind of avuncular quality that somehow fits with such a tour. He quite impressively gave his his narratives while navigating the tight spaces of the French Quarter or rush hour traffic. It is a tour for folks who enjoy history and culture. He described the history of the Quarter, differentiated between French and Spanish architecture, differentiated between different types of jazz, elucidating the meaning of creole versus cajon, gave the geographic history of the area, some terms that might be unknown like "bayou" and political history and even gastronomic history. We went past the areas most impacted by Katrina, including his brother's house, and he explained the mechanisms behind the flooding. He let us out at City Park to stroll around the beautiful live oaks with Spanish moss for a few minutes, we also disembarked at a "city of the dead" for 10 minutes as he regaled us with stories of the dead. So many interesting details were given in passing. We also did some "celebrity" tourism, passing the homes of Sandra Bullock and Anne Rice, for instance. My 2 friends and I really enjoyed the experience thoroughly, and I'd recommend highly to anyone visiting the area who loves learning something more than the best places to drink. Darin was fun and super informative. Since I'm a sociologist I loved learning about the subcultural aspects of the city. From pick up to drop off it was about 3.5 hours.. My recommendation to the company would be to just collect the money upfront or online rather than split it up into a deposit...just an unnecessary step for something that costs under $100.  Another suggestion would be to make the tour slightly longer (like 4 hours) and give a bit more time at several stops, maybe the company can build a relationship with a local food place to give samples or somesuch of gumbo or beignets or whatever they think would be inviting. The base cost was $45, well worth it, and I also gave 25% tip because it was well deserved.

I lonely go here for their TOGO cheeseboard. Nice selection of unusual cheeses, fruit and crackers for under $20, although portions could be larger, tastes fresh and quality is there. The restaurant has a nice German Beer/ Bar atmosphere to it. A full deli and gift shop with large selection of chocolates, jellies and gifts. 5 stars

My husband didn't get his work done that he was supposed to due to them canceling his appointment and them never calling us to let us know. I will never go back to this dentist ever now they are charging us for a stater plate that was never done they got paid by the insurance and still are charging us for something that was never done... and we can't contact them due to issues! But i give them 0 stars and will not recommend this place to anyone! They are scam artist and can't be trusted

Stopped by one of our fav spots and got the pimento cheese bacon burger with waffle fries, it was fantastic! Menu recently changed and they only serve BBQ on Wednesdays now which is a bummer because they have the best BBQ. 
Service was friendly and food was great per usual. This is always a place I bring people that are visiting NOLA and everyone loves it.

Fun t-shirt shop on Oak Street in the Uptown district of New Orleans.  Create your own shirt with dozens of designs of iron on transfers.  Sale racks are often a considerable bargain.

I still want that hemp USA flag that is not for sale that is only for decor.

Just popping by to say thank you! NuNu gave me an early reservation for a larger sized birthday celebration. They were so pleasant to coordinate with and were really accommodating for our size including a small baby. The staff was great and put up with my pesky parents/in-laws who were a little out of their element and probably wished they were at an Olive Garden instead, by the end they were converted tough! We had a gluten free and a soy free guest and NuNu was great about making sure they could prepare things specifically for them to eat. 

On top of this, the food is great. Many rolls, skewers, appetizers, katsu, curry....you name it we ordered it. Everything was delicious and beautifully presented. Drinks were delish too. 

 THANKS NUNU!

THE BEST CHEESESTEAKS AROUND! Do not cross the bridge and go to Philly, Genos and Pats do not compare. The owner or manager is always friendly! He recognizes you after like three orders and greets with a smile. I get cheese fries and a cheesesteak hoagie at least once a month- I've been ordering here since I was a kid. I love Benny's.

They offered free cinnamon rolls and other samplers at the counter. A famished me grabbed a few and gorged on them until my order was ready. 

Chunky cinnamon bread french toast with caramel syrup, whipped cream and strawberries. Perfect filling and yet a simple, breakfast. Crunchy on the outside , soft on the inside and just add all the toppings and it is delightful.

We vacillated about whether to rate this a 3 or 4. The restaurant was clean, the food was fast and hot, and we had very good service. We did not try the coffee. There was a twenty-thirty minute wait for two people on a Saturday am. My husband had the biscuits and gravy. The gravy was flavorful and not too salty, the biscuits appear to be baked in a sheet pan and cut in squares. While we have no problem with using that technique we really felt like the biscuit was more cakey than biscuit like. I had the half order of eggs Benedict. The egg was cooked perfectly just like on a cooking show really. The meat and sauce were both good but it could have used a bit more of both on the English muffin. Additionally my husband ordered two over east eggs, the waitress kindly informed us on how they cooked their eggs and my husband changed his order to over medium. They were cooked just perfectly!

I've been following this store on Instagram for awhile. If you're not following them do it now! They're always posting cute new items for sale, which you can buy online too. The store itself is tiny, like all the stores in the Annex shopping center. They're all made of out shipping containers and very charming inside. Everything for sale is Arizona/Tucson themed and reasonably priced. I bought a sticker for $3 by a local artist. There are loads of cute stickers! There are also T-shirt's for $25, water bottles, pins, books, hats, patches and so much more. It's really a must see if you love all things Sonoran desert. It's a great store that supports local artists, inspires pride in Tucson, and invites those new to the desert to explore and learn. Support local. Live local. Check this store out!

Extremely friendly wait staff in a lead at atmosphere. The beer selection is varied and suitable to all palettes with the "core 4" being great "go-to" beers and the seasonal fair goes beyond standard fair

Great beer choices. If you like beer come here. The bar is dark and comfy. When the weather is nice some lovely outdoor seating. Terrific burgers also kike the pot stickers. Pretty much everything is done well.

A gorgeous, stunning, charming and romantic destination. Extremely friendly and capable staff. Extremely professional staff in the spa. Massages were first class. Facials were first class. It  features pools and jacuzzis with incredible views of the sunset. For the money, this place - the property, surroundings and service - exceeds expectations. We only ate one meal on the property and it was fine. Highly recommended.

We used to like this restaurant a lot. However, tonight the food was of questionable quality. Chicken rubbery and shrimp mealy. Maybe it was an off night, but to have both chicken and shrimp consistency not great, I think the quality of the product seems lower grade.

I took my daughter to this salon and this is my daughter's review.  This is a terrific salon for many reasons. First, I was welcomed and quickly became part of the conversation within the salon. I immediately felt comfortable and the people were very friendly and engaged me in conversation  I have had a lot of problems with my very curly, fizzy hair and decided to have a keratin treatment. Tamika was fantastic, she told me exactly what she was going to do and gave me tons of great advice on how to manage my hair . My hair looks better than it ever has before. My experience was fantastic!

My husband brought me your Spaghetti Bolognese home for dinner & it was absolutely  delicious!!  Any way of getting the recipe, or some of the main ingredients?
Thank-You so much & Happy New Year!
Josephine

I Visited your Moorestown NJ location today (10/10/19), and would like to tell you about my horrific visit. I have been to many of your locations and have never had any issues before. The service has always been pleasant and the food has been great, but after today, I will never set foot in one of your establishments again. I went in with a friend of mine  for breakfast, there were not many people there, since it was only 8:30. Our order was very simple. She ordered a vegi- omelette, no cheese (due to allergies) a plain English muffin and a side of fruit... and mine was simply, a side of scrambled eggs and an English muffin. First her's came out, smothered in cheese. When we reminded our server, she said no cheese, he just said "oh that's right" and took it back. Then, my small plate of scrambles eggs came out with my English muffin. I took one small bite, and then with my second forkful... a long dark thick hair came with the egg. To say I was disgusted, shocked and sick to my stomach, was an understatement! When the server came back over with my friends new omelette, we showed him the extra ingredient in my eggs... his response was simply.... " oh, did you want another one?"  
We asked to speak to a manger who came over an let us know that the omelet  would be taken off our bill.  We could not even finish our meal, we were so disgusted. As a manager and my friend a small business owner, this is NOT how you handle a situation like this. 
The server never apologized,  as we were leaving the manager never made eye contact with us or spoke to us again. All we got were excuses and a bad case of nausea.... Oh, and our bill that should have been covered due to this incident...  we were still charged for the eggs, English muffin and coffee. We will be sure that all our friends are aware that this is not somewhere they want to go.

Very friendly staff to eager to help which is definitely the highlight of the store. What I also like about the store is the fact that there are many cute accessories that are Nola based.  You can definitely go in there and find you something that will show your Nola Love at reasonable price.

It's in a great location on the Magazine Street strip. Parking can be a little hassle but normally you should find some meter parking or free parking on a side street not too far away.
Live band music! Delicious food and wine.  It will be my go-to place when I am in Nashville.

My hubby came to GW Fins for dinner tonight due to great rave reviews of the restaurant on YELP, over other seafood restaurants near the French Quarter.  based on the other reviews, we had great expectations overall.

FIRST IMPRESSION:
The hostess did not smile at all or even look at us, so I greeted her instead as we came in.  It's not like she's so busy! The place was not busy at the time we came in.  There's NO EXCUSE for a frown when you're a hostess.  She looked like she did not want to be there at all.  


SERVICE:
Our waiter was Ricard and, he was AWESOME!  He tried his best to cater to us, among at least five other tables he had to cater to.  He was friendly and informative with the menu. The funny thing was that there were 2 guys in a suit that just seemed to be standing around until the end of our dinner and at that time, they came over and ask how was dinner?


DRINKS:
AWESOME! AWESOME!   
key lime martini was so deli-sh!
Fins-Cosmo was great too.

We wanted to start with an appetizer but we were full with all their bread we got, and we didn't want to keep waiting so we passed on an appetizer.  On the positive side, the bread kept coming.  It's was warm and fluffy with a touch of sweetness.  For an Entree, I had the Scalibut with lobster risotto, and a couple of sweet peas.Three seafood items on one plate,  I loved it all and especially on ONE plate.!  I highly recommend it.

My hubby had the Parmesan crusted flounder.
He LOVED it!  The cheese wasn't overwhelming.  Just right for him.

To finish we had Creme brulee
They did not spare on the the vanilla bean, that is for sure!.

In the end, I agree with the YELPERS that the food was great! 
Service, however, left something to be desired, with exception to the bread guy and our waiter.

Thank goodness that I found Linda at Supercuts almost 2 years ago! She has helped me transition from a once a month hair colorer to a gorgeous silver fox! Her demeanor and professionalism is outstanding!

Stopped in yesterday, everything looked so good and fresh I had a hard time deciding what to take home for our family dinner. I ending up getting a big bag of Cheese Ravioli and Rose sauce....INCREDIBLE! My family loved it and we will be visiting again real soon to try some more of your products. Thanks so much!

The staff is typically unhelpful and rude. I used to be a member, but based on how customers are treated i will not spend any money there. Go elsewhere. Overpriced and rude. The girl at the checkout with glasses is very nice though.

This review is for the service department. I have been there twice to have my Audi Q7 serviced. Both times the service department staff were courteous and helpful. They always called to give me a run down of what was wrong with my car and also what the estimated cost would be. My most recent visit was quite an expensive one and the service department actually gave me a little bit of a discount which was nice. The other nice thing about taking your car to be serviced here is that they do give you a loaner so you don't have to arrange for rides. The cons of this place are the labor costs, around $150/hr and the assessment fee they charge you which is 1 hours worth of labor. I would rate this place higher if they would drop the service fee as long as you agree to have the work done at the shop. Overall good experiences though.

This pharmacy isn't the best.  The folks in the pharmacy are snooty when you have questions.  Simply saying they never had any problem or heard of the situation is not helpful.   I miss my old CVS pharmacy that knew what customer service was all about.  ;(

We stopped in for cocktails before our walking tour.  I'd intended to ask for it to go, but I'm glad that I didn't, so we could watch Brian craft them in actual glasses.  He put a lot of artistry into the effort, spinning the glass to coat it with bitters, ensuring even flavor. 

We chose the Sazerac and the Vieux Carré, both cocktails with long histories that started in New Orleans.  They were appropriate selections for this long-standing establishment. The bar is fun, especially with the historic paintings hung next to more recent newspapers across from an impressively large mirror bordered by columns.  I'd had it bookmarked to try the food as well, but there was no way that I was getting through 45 bookmarks in a little less than 3 days.  Next trip!

This place gets a lil more critical review because of the meal in comparison with their price-point ($$$). 

First off service was super slow. It took us a good while to get started on our bottomless mimosas. Once it got going tho, their refills were on point and attentive! 

However, i'm not going to base my review off how fast they can pour a bottle. I got the Seared Pork Rib Chop medium rare.... except instead of medium rare I got it well done. The plate was also kinda messy, as if somebody dragged a spoon around it while it was being carried to the table haha (but not haha). It looked like a plate from outback steakhouse, just pricier.... and that's the thing: at $20+ per plate, standards are raised a little, ya know?

The the spinach and sweet potatoes were good, pork chop (although overcooked) was still pretty good. Still, the entire experience was sub-$$$

Came here for the first time with the late Governor Frank O'Bannon when i worked in his office and who loved this place.  Before we left the office, his secretary begged us to bring back some peach cobbler. This place is the real deal if you've got a craving for some killer down home cooking.

This is a great after work hangout. Especially if your trying to pick up a hot guy in a suit... Because let me tell you there are many. 

There is a great beer list and apps. I recommend the fried avocado... To die for! They also have a ton of tvs and they are always playing the good games. So if your with a boring crowd. No worries there's still entertainment. 

So if your in the flirty mood and want some beers head on over to misconduct.

I don't understand why people like this place.  It's a 3am bar with okay food that's served late, so I guess I get the industry crowd, but the service is pretty bad, and drinks are way too expensive.  For $6, I can a much better IPA at iTap, thank you.

Pedro's Smog Check is Santa Barbara's best kept secret. Not only they have superb, fast, trusted service but you can also bypass the DMV hustle and bustle and get your car registered here while you wait. This is a one stop shop for all your automotive needs! Go here, you will be beyond please with their customer service and their aide array of services.

Why is it so hard to find good pizza delivery in Tucson? Is it me or does everyone here like chewy, tasteless pizza dough? I had great hopes for this place but alas, I was let down. Absolutely tasteless; sauce, dough, even the "sausage" topping (who slices sausage on a pizza?).
Well, my hunt continues and I'm really sorry to say but Domino's has a better pizza.

We recently had our home stuccoed and this left the windows in some rough shape. The response time to our inquiry for assistance getting things cleaned up was fast. While there were a few miss spots, Ethan did an exceptional job getting things cleaned. We will definitely have him back for future cleanings.

A good place to get breakfast.  The staff are all very nice and the service is good.  Our order came out fairly quickly and was just right. I had a western omelet with home fries and it was delicious.  Wife had eggs with toast and scrapple.  We shared the scrapple as we have to have some whenever we are back in NJ. 

The Sage is under new ownership and is rebranding as the Mt. laurel Diner.  They plan a menu revamp and renovations to the restaurant.  The renovations are long overdue but I look forward to coming back in the future.
I enjoy this place when visiting Philly. The breakfast is really good and the pub / bar is great for a quick bite at dinner. The Union League Inn is my favorite place to stay as well.
The best pizza in Boise! Staff is always friendly and helpful. Nice & clean and great selections of good quality food.

My experience today has been the worst I've ever had here. I've been bringing my children here for over 9 years. Today is our 3rd time back in 3 weeks (2 emergency visits and 1 scheduled visit). My son has been in a lot of pain following the last 2 visits and completing his antibiotics and 3 bottles of Motrin. This 3rd visit and for the first time ever I requested to go back with him to figure out what's going on. Dr. Marcella Herrera was very loud and rude when she told me I couldn't go back with him. She said (in a very thick accent), "I did you a favor by allowing you to come in for an emergency, if you don't like that you can't come back with your child you can find somewhere else to take him!" I was very upset by her tone and words in front of my son, it also shows she don't care about him his pain. I talked to the office manager and she explained very politely that it's just not enough room in the room for me which was not communicated to me by Dr Herrera. I requested a different dentist who would be professional, respectful with good communication and who cares. My son was then seen by Dr Danielle Lockwood.
Best pizza in town!  Hands down!  Staff is great and pizza never disappoints!  I get pizza here all the time and it's always great!  I highly recommend especially if you like thin crust pizza.
Great pulled pork sandwiches, friendly staff, quick service!

For those that are a little bit more health conscious, but want the joys that come with a burger, this is your spot. The presentation is like night and day compared to a typical fast foot joint where they throw a burger in a greasy bag. 

It's mostly sit-down with a server, though you can order to-go at the bar. 

They sell the Impossible Burger here, which is a meatless patty that purportedly tastes exactly like beef. Eh, I think it still tastes like faux meat. Good option though for those that don't eat meat.

Thick cut fries.

Solid service, everyone here was nice and responsive. Huge plus is how sustainable the food packaging is, everything looks like recycled paper. Only qualm is that it's a bit pricey. A burger, fries, and drink cost around $20.

I had no idea this was the old gallery! Crazy! 

This place reminded me of the fashion mall in Vegas. 

They have some really cool lighting throughout. 

You get dumped right into it from the train which is cool if you are taking the train to Philly. 

There were a lot of stores that still weren't open despite the fact that the grand opening was in September. 

There are a lot of places to get food. Chickie's and Pete's, chick-Fil-A, Philadelphia pretzel factory, etc. 

They had a cool floating Christmas tree that has a light show set to music every half hour. It was cool. 

There are very different vibes throughout depending on where you are. 

It looked bright and clean. 

The bathroom needed some tending to. 

It's easy to get to, is in the hub of Philly, has a lot of stores (including outlet stores) and many more on the way.

I recommend checking it out if you're in the area!
Always able to find great treasures here! Always something new to discover! I really enjoy coming here

AMANDA C. is the best! When I started going to her my hair was crunchy and left for dead! She has brought it back to life and has me feeling brand new! I highly suggest her for all your cut and color needs! You can even check her work on Facebook or Instagram, she is a true artist and miracle worker!!
Delicious food, my Uncle (who is a huge foodie) absolutely loved this place when I brought him.

This place is okay, but not great. I've been to this place quite a few times because it's close to campus and I love Japanese food, but the food has failed to amaze me. My friend and I went here a few days ago, and the server paid no attention to us. The green cheese cake tasted like it was pre-made a few days ago and was still frozen (it was hard to chew on). If you want to go for the decorations and atmosphere, then go ahead. If you want to go for the food, there are lots of other, better Japanese food options in Tucson.

I found this company on Angie's list.

My refrigerator died the Friday (evening) before Thanksgiving. What bad luck!  I called Better Homes on Saturday morning, and they had a technician (Brian) at my house on Monday. He was great! He knew that it was a defective on/off switch within a minute, and he fixed the wires so that my refrigerator was working within minutes. As my refrigerator is old, he also gave me advice on what brands are best when it is time to replace (he also reviewed good ovens and dishwashers). What great service!

I can happily recommend this company. They are based in Clearwater, but they do come out to Hillsborough County.

I get the same thing every time I come here. Jumbo shrimp hand drawn noodles schezuan style - medium spicy. Now, I can handle spice pretty well, so if you order hot, just be prepared! The broth is so flavorful and delicious. They have pickled vegetables at the table which adds just the right amount of tart to the soup. There are also plenty of meat options and vegetarian options. Just make sure you have cash because it is a cash only establishment. They do have an ATM on site if needed. The only issue with this location is that it is tough to find parking in the area.

Just bought a BMW from Mike at Tampa Bay Auto Network. Believe it or not, the car was BETTER  than described. We bought a 3-year-old off lease 135i that was pristine. 
A tree fell on our 2016 Miata Special Edition and the insurance company totaled the car. Geico was NOT fun to deal with on the value of the car!
Found the perfect replacement on line at a very good price and Mike T. was very easy to deal with. Put a small deposit on the car while we fought with Geico. Mike held the car for 2 weeks until we could get down to pick it up.
The whole delivery was just as smooth as butter. We checked out the car - looked virtually new (and I was in the car biz so I know what I'm looking for) - did the paper work and were on the road in slightly over an hour. Very laid back no pressure sale. They had never cashed the deposit in the event I changed my mind. For that good a deal and great service I didn't even mind the 8-hour round trip.
Thanks a lot Mike.
Beautiful car.
Great place nearby for Pho or other authentic Vietnamese cuisine. Out of the other restaurants around this place that serve Pho and this place has the best.

We were in the area visiting family for Christmas and kept driving by this place. Finally we went in Thursday night at around 9pm. It wasn't very busy, but the staff was super attentive and pleasant. And although it isn't very PC to say so,..we noticed two tables of Asian people about our age (late 20's/early 30s), so we figured this place must be good, lol! Overall we were very satified. Appetizers were half off that night. We had edamame and dumplings w/ sesame sauce. For dinner we had the Scorpion roll, Buddha roll, and Spicy Tuna roll. The Scorpion roll is quite spicy but very good. The others were very good too. Almost better than the food was the music. Think 1998 hip/hop radio ( Total, Mase, Missy Elliot, Ginuwine, etc) Just kinda took me back at little.  I would def. recommend this place. Our total bill was under $30 for two.

One of the best Italian restaurants in the area. A very diverse menu and excellent waitstaff. Our server, Devyn, on our last visit, moved around the dining room effortlessly and was extremely pleasant and accommodating. I've never had a bad meal here and just consistently great food.

I have been coming here for a while.  I love their food and I have always been treated well.  Their pick two is my favorite.  Their strawberry salad with chicken is my favorite.  My husband loves their bowls. Just ate there today and will continue to do so.  There are plenty of great choices. You won't be disappointed !
Highly recommend!!  Everyone could not have been nicer.  Food was delicious!  We ordered several sushi rolls, Chicken Fried Rice & Magnolian Beef and all was yummy!  Think we found our new spot!

Mac and cheese. Sooooo good! Do not pass it up! Who knew this would be the place to have such a food? 

Still waiting for that Diamond Cheddar...

I believe the measure of a good bookstore is one in which you go in expecting just to browse, and come out with an armful of books that you just discovered you can't live without.This was my experience at Subterranean.

We've walked up and down the loop a few times and always passed by this little shop.  Until last weekend, I was convinced it was once of those wierd stale bookstores that just peddled used copies of "A Brief History of Time."  Boy was I wrong!  So glad the hubby dragged me in there.  I saw so many good books (a good bookstore is like a candy shop) that I wanted to get, and settled on an photo guide book of sprawl (ie. urban sprawl, suburban sprawl).  Doubt the big bookstores have that instock.  And that's the charm of this place.

Nice, clean restaurant with an excellent wait staff.  We've been there twice and the food is delicious.  I'd like to try something else, but the fish sandwich just keeps calling my name.  I took one star away because they have TV's in every direction which I hate, especially when we have our children with us.  Doesn't anyone have dinner conversation anymore?

Was in Largo for an event and somehow we ended up here for lunch every day. They were great! By the 4th day our group had grown to a good size and the service was just as good as it was the first with a small party. The best part is that their menu has a good variety of dishes. Will definitely be back when I'm in town.

Stein Mart has not made it onto my regular stop rotation, but it does deserve a nod.

If you are searching for just one thing...it may be worth a trip.  This location has a lot of costume jewelry.  I would look here for earrings or a necklace to make an outfit perfect.  I found purses upon purses, many name brand.  Shoes, Clothing, Luggage, Pets, and Housewares also fill the space.  

Pull up coupons on your phone or print before you get to the store.

Everything we have purchased for this store has been amazing! It's so nice to have such a wonderful Polish deli in the Brandon area. I used to drive to Clearwater but I actually prefer European Flavors and it's so much closer. The staff is incredibly nice and there is always something interesting to try.

Went at lunch time with some work friends.

Food was good. Flavors were solid but execution was poor (example: Beef Brisket was more like jerky).

Service was awful. Orders were all messed up, took longer than 1 hour from time seated til time served. Was a full 2 hour lunch all told from the time we sat until the time we paid. 

Since it was a lunch event, that's not reasonable. Most of us only have a 1 hour break for lunch.

Would return but not on a workday. If service is the same the 2nd time, will not return again.

I just switched from Gulf South Eye Associates b/c I was fed up with my long-term doctor there. I was misdiagnosed twice, and 4 hour check up appointments don't fit into my work schedule. I went to see Dr. Brock Songy of Lakeview Vision Source, LLC on Harrison Ave. He also has a location in Gentilly, and I can confidently say I officially have a new eye dr.

There are mixed reviews ranging from 1-5 stars and I read some of them. All the ones I read made sense to me; not just people getting pissy. Good constructive criticism. 

Luckily my first experience on a date went really well!

We went on a Monday matinee so we were the only ones in the theater. The server comes out just as the movie begins playing, which was fine because there was only two of us. I read another review with a fuller theater and I can see how it could be distracting to others as well as to yourself when there's multiple orders going on a once. Also the server kept coming in and out during the movie. Which was fine to me but again that can be distracting to others. 

***I would suggest servers on stand- by before the movie starts so people can get a head start on deciding and ordering instead of showing up when the movie starts. 
***I would also suggest the tabs being collected at the end maybe?

The food was pricey but that's expected of any movie theater. Tasted great though! We got the coconut breaded chicken with the shrimp add-on ($1 for three pieces) and the brownie sundae. Again the food was satisfying... Better than the food I had at the Villagio Dine-In theater in Carrolwood. I also got a strawberry margarita which tasted fruity with a kick to it ;) 

The seats do not recline so I'd recommend not sitting anywhere before Row D, but they are comfy. I'll admit the Villagio theater has more comfortable chairs that recline too, but smaller trays. The trays here were an appropriate size with metal tabs to keep your plates from sliding off. There are also call buttons on each of the trays to contact servers. 

Our server was nice, patient, and helpful to us as well so props to that. All the other employees we interacted with were friendly and helpful too. Also the cleanliness of the lobby, theater, and bathrooms was spotless! Very nicely decorated throughout the entire establishment. Almost makes you forget you're in the middle of University Mall!

Somewhere between 3 and 4 stars sounds about right.

It's nice to have a bar like this in the neighborhood. Solid beer selection, fairly reasonable prices, and a bar menu that does the trick if you don't feel like making dinner when you get home from a long day. The bar itself has a nice casual atmosphere, and there is outdoor seating for when the weather is nice. The staff is also pretty friendly.

Owner is rude, I believe he set a record for most "F" words in a 30 second time slot. 

The END

The service was great and food decent. I will say the Chargrilled Oysters DELICIOUS! Even if you've never had oysters try them delicious even one of my friends who dislikes fishy taste loved really good. The Po Boys were really good as well!

My first visit to Piero's, to celebrate a friend's 50th birthday: a small party of 6, reservations made ahead of time, for a table near the window.  My husband and I arrived first, and were to be seated in a booth for 6, immediately next to the entrance, next to a window... but the one separating the reception area from the main dining room.  Not the window my friend had in mind, when she made reservations.  The hostess did a great job rearranging seating, to enable us to get a spacious table further in the dining room, with plenty of elbow room and breathing space - thank you!

But that was about all the credit I can give to Piero's:  the service was quite slow, even though the restaurant was not at capacity: we arrived at 6:30 pm. The person who delivered to miserly bread basket to our table had no personality or desire to engage with guests, and literally slid the basket across the table. The prices were a bit high for the area and the unusual location [felt like it was the first house in a residential development which was recently completed].  The saving grace is this is a BYOB, else our bill would have been beyond astronomical.

The appetizers were a typical Italian fare of calamari and antipasti - nothing in the form of unusual flavors or unique presentation that set these apart. For the main course, we ordered 5 halibut specials at $35 a pop, and I selected Zuppa di Pesce [i.e. frutti di mare with linguini] at $26. They had only 3 specials left (?!?) so we eliminated one, and replaced another.  When the food (finally!) arrived, I found my Zuppa lacking seafood for the quoted price: enough calamari and little neck clams, but not enough shrimp or crabmeat.  Also, everyone unanimously said the halibut was dry, tasteless and lukewarm, and the portion was not worth the price.  We called the waitress, and pointed out the problem: we insisted the birthday boy's entrée be replaced, but no one else wanted to wait forever for another dish. I hinted the desserts for the "sufferers" should be on the house.  We ordered coffee and dessert [with a candle for the big boy].

Long story short: nothing was comp'd, not the birthday boy's entrée, not the desserts, nada!  No one from the kitchen or management stopped by to connect with the disappointed customers [plural - customerS].  Clearly, the owners are not concerned about repeat business.  And I know none of the diners in our group will go out of our way to return.

Drove to Logans on Friday night. Got here at 8:15 fully expecting to get their Prime Rib which they only serve after 4pm on Friday.. After putting the order they come back 5 mins later to inform me it is 86.. REALLY? It hasn't been 4 hours. Drove 15 miles to get here..  Should have gone to Outback..

I'd give it more stars but maybe they should've put money towards training their staff on how to complete orders v remodeling the restaurant.

 It's bad when you're not giving everything from the first time only to go back in to get what they forgot. Then get home and still have missing items. Service here has gotten worse since they reopened.

I love this place! Fresh made salsas everyday, slow cooked goodness on every page of the menu and friendly staff. I tend to stick with the barbacoa tacos but even when I stray to other meals I am never disappointed. The lengua is tender and tasty, the al pastor is flavorful and cooked on a coal fired spit, the octopus is ridiculously good too.

Ok here's the thing about my experience here...I showed up here with 3 of my friends last Friday night. We came here because we wanted to play their board games.

As my friend and I were buying beers at the bar, the bartender was speaking to another patron. She asked the patron "are you working this weekend?" "No" he said. Full of irony, the bartender replied "I know I am definitely working this weekend. I've got a $4000 vet bill to pay off. And the thing didn't even survive!" My friend, picking up on the irony, harmlessly and un-maliciously giggled. This slightly intimidating woman then turned to my friend, did a double take, went to black, and with utmost nastiness she said "Do you think that's funny!?" "No, no, I'm sorry" he replied. "That's terrible!" We all felt so uncomfortable after that. 

The bartender then proceeded to spend the rest of the night being unbelievably rude to me and my friends. She neglected to bring my friend a drink as she was serving me and my girlfriend. She kept giving us the "evil eye" all night. And she needlessly bumped into my other friend on several different occasions. I actually wanted to stay but my one friend made sure she didn't buy one drink more to make sure she didn't patronize such a rude bartender any more than she had to. I gather the bartender is the owner of the place, given her rapport with many of the other patrons and the cat tattoo she had on her upper arm. 

Look, I understand that what my friend did could be seen as insensitive. But to be completely honest, her statement to the other patron was smothered in irony, as ironic as saying "I spent $4000 on my car and the darn thing is still broken!" It was a mildly humorous thing to say. There was no sense of tragedy or mourning in how she said it and it certainly wasn't worth her unbelievably rude response and behavior. 

But way to make your customers feel unwelcome, intimidated, and uncomfortable! There's no excuse for that kind of behavior, nor was their any excuse to spend the next few hours being absolutely rude to us!

I'll just go through a few things I've had in lieu of doing a more general review:

1. Southern fried chicken.  It's awesome.  Crispy & juicy (boneless) chicken breast on top of mashed potatoes with some gravy and succotash. 2. Late night burger.  Had this last week and it's listed as new on their menu and it was awesome.  Open face burger with chili verde and bacon and a fried egg?  Come on.  Chili verde is my jam and what I gauge every mexican restaurant on, and theirs was better than many.  

3. Avocado egg rolls.  Super good.

4. Calamari.  Better than most.  I wouldn't say it's exceptional, but it's above average.

5. Spinach and artichoke dip.  Again, very good.  

6. Ahi poke.  It's a bunch of good quality fish and nice ripe avocado.  I.e. it is lovely.

There are not enough horrible adjectives to describe the treatment by these sleazy people! Do not buy a VW here! I would drive over the hill to Roseville Auto Mall and get a better deal and much better treatment if I were you. They do every sleazy car salesman trick in the book, such as "bait and replace" where they advertise one low-ball price, but then they don't have that car in stock. So they tell you they will give you a much "better" car for the same price, but it's not the same price at all. They change what they said and say "NO, I said the same 'payments' not the same price." They just increase payments for 3 more years. Or something similarly horrendous.The dealership T.O.'s you.
T. O. stands for "turn over." You're sitting in a salesperson's office, thinking about how much more fun it would be to replace your hard drive in the dark than go through this, when your salesperson returns with reinforcements. The new smiling face asks for more money. And then the salesperson asks for more. And then the dealership chaplain comes in.
The T. O. system operates on the principle of "fresh faces can work miracles." A miracle, in this instance, is defined as more profit. And as long as you give, they'll keep asking.
The "note" system.
Rather than the T.O. system, some dealerships use the note system. In this technique, the salesperson steps out, returning with a nice note from the sales manager asking for more money. And then another note, then another. Usually, they come back with five, and usually the last two ask for raises of odd amounts of money for instance, $113.29 or, finally, $23.19. The note system has one basic problem. It makes you think the dealership is negotiating when it's really only play acting. Consider the "odd" raises. These are simply designed to make it look like you're really a hard bargainer. You know, you think you've got them "down to the pennies." Many web sellers use versions of the note system.
The Four-Square system.
The salesperson divides a piece of paper into four squares and then asks for your "wish list." What do you want to pay a month? What do you want for your trade? What do you want to pay for the new car? However ridiculous the sums, each is written in a square. Then they ask for a large deposit and your signature in the fourth square.
Then they begin to "work" you on each square separately, starting with a figure far from yours and very slowly negotiating down, constantly scratching through figures. By the time they finish, the paper is illegible, you're frazzled, but the salesperson is smiling. You've agreed to pay an additional $1,200 to $1,500 profit.
The four square system is probably the worst system in use today because it was designed to produce some very nice profits by confusing you. Don't deal with dealerships who use this system.
Spot Delivery, or "Yo-Yo" selling.
"You can drive it off today!" That is the most expensive statement any car dealer or web seller can make. Spot delivery means emotion is ruling you rather than good sense. It also means you (very conveniently for the seller) won't have the opportunity to compare costs and terms. Never buy or take delivery of a car on your first visit to a dealership or a web site. Be patient and the price will tumble.
The Leasing Scam.
Many dealerships will try to switch you to leasing on the spot. Don't fall for it! Read this excerpt from this on-line Leasing guide, and you'll see why dealerships try to switch you: http://www.dcu.org/streetwise/auto/leaseguide/index.html
Last but not least important, stay away from "Tucker". Worst sales person in the history of selling. He lies and treats you like an idiot. Well, we all know what "Tucker" rhymes with!
BTW-we left and went to the Ford Dealer. We ended up buying a much nicer car for the price we wanted rather than deal with VW's lowballing our trade-in, treating us stupid, raising the price dramatically from what was advertised and giving us a lesser car. Ford gets my vote.
