* monkfish egg rolls-they give you three fun sauces, lychee lee (drink), the Chinese 3.5 spice adult hot chocolate, crab rangoons (the chunks of shrimp give it a nice texture), General Tso's -the spice level is top notch, you won't realize you are eating organ meat, and the almond cookie, and my husband advised the pork dumplings were the best that he's ever eaten, he also enjoyed the wings and peanut butter miso cookie

My only issue was that one of the times we went the hours on the store front and online advised it opened at 3pm. When we arrived we were told it was just the bar and food was available at 5pm. I also feel the drinks could be a bit stronger for the price point and size.

Love this place!! Food is amazing. Friendly owners. Nice atmosphere. Our waitress, Irene, was a doll!  She had been our server the previous time we came and she remembered specific details of what we ordered and talked about which was very impressive!
I took my husband here for a quick drink and we stayed for a few. Drinks and food are amazing!

I highly recommend Blue Lotus Salon. Judy and her staff do a wonderful job of making you look and feel good! The salon is stylish and the stylists are all friendly and make you feel welcome and relaxed. Have a cup of tea and read the latest celebrity gossip while you are waiting for your color to set. Judy is also always giving back to the community. Blue Lotus is amazing.

ordered 5 pieces fried wings, about 10 bucks.

this is my third visit, consistent quality, crunchy crispy outside, soft n juicy inside, tasty.

i can't finish 5 of them at once.

4 hours later, finished the remaining two, surprisingly it was still crunchy, unbelievable!!

**
i will be back :p

Just went to this restaurant, my wife ordered a bacon chicken ranch, there was no bacon on her sandwich. The guy did only charge for a chicken breast sandwich, but wasn't what she ordered. I then showed him two chips and asked for two drinks and make them meals. We paid and asked for our cups l, which he said you didn't order drinks. We asked if he could fix it and he was apathetic at best and didn't know how to fix the situation. It was very weird and awkward situation, so we left with our chips and our wrongly made sandwiches. There was no effort to fix the situation. We usually like this subway a lot, but these two new people didn't help out experience at all. We just wanted a little better customer service and since we are giving them our business, we would've liked them to help make fix the issues we had. We were willing to pay or whatever, they just didn't offer a solution to fix it.

Sakeya is a fun party spot. The venue is attractive and modern, and not confining at all. There's a sushi bar and several dining areas, all conveniently near the Avenue of the Arts.  The space is better than it was before (when it was named Kaizan), providing better crowd flow (when there's a crowd, of course) between bars and the dance floor.

Prices per drink are decent, and their sushi tastes fine. Not a bad place to start a night. It's not super close to many other places, but it's hardly a far walk either. Worth a visit!
Great Mexican food and atmosphere. Slow service but a must try if you live in Tucson.
Hard to get an appointment. Hard to communicate with their front office staff. It doesn't seem like anyone there cares about the patient (except the doctors if you ever get to sit in front of them!).
Fantastic Museum, I spent the entire day there...
Nice little restaurant next to Annata's    Fantastic wine list to pair with there fish entrees

Had the chicken tikka masala and murg vindaloo. Neither were very good. The chicken was very dry and the flavors of two dishes that should be very distinct were hard to tell apart. Both tasted overwhelmingly spicy without any of the complexity and nuanced heat that even Indian fast food places can deliver. Would not come back. However, if you are willing to give this place a chance, you will get a discount if using cash payment.
Owner replied to my post, I respect that and have adjusted my score. Bad days happen. Otherwise usually great food.

Pretty bad experience. Came here Labor Day weekend and this was about the only place open on the French quarter. We waited 30+ minutes for a table. Service was slow, they seemed to not have enough staff. There was only 4 options for food: fried shrimp, hamburger, alligator or French fries. We've heard legends about the hurricane but I couldn't even drink more than a few sips. It didn't taste good. $60 plus tip for mediocre food, drinks and service. Would not return.

The sweets here are seriously delectable. I called their Orlando location because I could find any info on their website about hours but I was redirected to the Baum Market and the hours are the same. I bought several items - a guava cheese hand pie, a hazelnut rose cake, a breakfast turnover, and a few other things. Omg everything was so delicious. I'll only knock this place slightly for the breakfast turnover because although delicious, there could have been more filing. I think it had vegan cheese and sausage; it was really good (flakey, buttery), but it had too little (or maybe I'm just over the moon about it!) Still...I can't wait to hit this place up next time I'm in st. Pete.

This is simple.

Orgasm on a stick. Bring cash though - and their hours are always not the most convenient - but for what you get - find a phone and call someone who cares.

Eat Popsicles and be happy.

Sent a work mate on a whim that this would be the bomb people acclaimed it to be . I WAS NOT LET DOWN! This warm bacon infested cheese melting eggs potato's and  spice puts this place on my radar ever hungry morning. After eating the 3.5 inch x10 inch + freshly grilled tortilla shell with all those fixings a nap or way to use all those scrumptious calories as work fuel was needed. Thank goodness work was in order!

I love going to wineries. One of my favorite places to go is the Stetson winery in Arizona. However this winery is actually the end point, there's no real tour to go on on site. They just have the end product there. They have at least 20 different signature kinds of wine that are simply irresistible. Jonathan's pass is a fun little beach side walk along area with shops and restaurants all the touristy stuff you can fine. But it's incredible. They'll let you sample just about anything and they have seating outdoors right next to the cigar bar for you to sip on your wine or one of their frozen wine smoothies.

They do deliver winds around the country. However I've always had to stand up until the past few years because I haven't had a chance to go back but I have Mr. wine so much. Also worthy of note there's a bar above that opened that's part of this establishment that has a homemade brewing facility within it. So you'll find a lot of wine selections there as well but with a fun festive environment. Upstairs or downstairs you're guaranteed to have a great time

The staff are always knowledgeable and pleasant. And if you tip them well the pours are definitely generous :-)

Pass this place right on by on your way to plenty of other places that know how to season and make food taste great.

I've been here 3 or 4 times, as I do my best to give every restaurant a fair chance to stand on their own 2 feet.  I just don't see the attraction...  Here's what has me baffled...

How hard is it to season an omelet?  How hard is it to not bake your own fluffy biscuits or flavor the gravy instead of pushing out crappy biscuits with Sysco bland gravy?  Oops...  I saw the picture here.  It looks like they forgot the sausage in my sausage gravy.

Cheap - yes.  Bland - yes.  Worth going back - NEVER.

Great place for a relaxing or business lunch. Menu offers great sandwiches (corned beef was tops) and really good burgers along with many more items that are just right for lunch. The special 15 dollar lunch includes any main item on the lunch menu along with either a salad ( great one and good size) hummus, or their delicious goat nuggets which are local chicken with siracha and blue cheese - different and delicious. Overall, this is a cool place with great food and a really quality bar.
Good bar to watch a game too!

My absolute go to place!! Martha is amazing with facials and microdermabrasion! My face has never looked better!! The laser is also completely worth it! My hair is much finer can't wait till my next appointments!

So, it was my second recent visit.  There's a pandemic going on. My travel plans have been cancelled.  I opted for a "stay-cation."

The hotel is pretty cool for the most part, but my stay was marred by a lot of little things, some of which were preventable. 

Upon checking I handed my license and credit card to the staff member at the front desk.  For whatever reason, she didn't hand both of them back to me.   She threw one on the counter.   I'm my opinion, this is very thoughtless and impolite.  It's actually a pet peeve of mine.  I just think if you are in a service industry, particularly hospitality, you should always be polite and thoughtful when dealing with customers.  

There were a handful of other small issues that got my attention.  For example there was long, straight brown hair in the shower.  I don't have brown hair, or straight hair, or long hair...   The bathtub was dripping when I came in, noticeably.  The fixtures in the bathroom looked odd, some grayish and chalky.  I'm guessing there may be some type of sterilization process or something but who knows.  Also, my television was on when I entered the room.   Odd.  

One morning in particular there was a lot of noise outside of my room door. There were multiple internet issues also.  

Again, all of the issues were small, but after the bad first impression, the small issues stood out more than they otherwise may have.  

The bed was comfortable.  And the rest of the room seemed clean.  I only interacted with housekeeping once.  It was a pleasant interaction.  

It was my second recent stay.  You could do a lot worse.  The value was okay.  No room service and nothing complimentary.  That was slightly disappointing but understandable since the world is so strange these days.  

I may very well stay here again for a few nights if the pandemic continues and I need a "fake getaway," but it won't be my first choice.

Do not get delivery from here.  I ordered a large pepperoni pizza.  Pizza toppings and cheese slide of the pizza to the box.   Called to say something and the lady on the phone gives an attitude.  First and last time to order this crappy food.
After the owners reply to my review I go back for more proof. Next time don't mess with a future lawyer.
It was awesome and delicious. The hot pot was really good. There was plenty of food and the service was great. The food was very fresh and the price was worth it.
They have the best jalapeno Mac and cheese!! I cannot resist but to put an order in when I walk by this place. The best part is You're also supporting a small business owner!

Jim Stocker and his team at Big O Tire on Kietzke Lane is as good as it gets when it comes to the real meaning of service.  In an age when customer care is more sizzle than steak, Jim continues to go above and beyond. 

With 3 vehicles (it's be 4 if he did bikes), we have gone to him for all tire, shock and preventative maintenance for 6 years.  His team has also been timely and on the money, no phantom problems to jack up the bill like too many other places.  If he can't do something, he'll tell you and recommend someone that has the same high level of ethics as he does..again, an anomaly in auto repair!

When your car needs care, and they all eventually do, do yourself and your car a favor, Call Jim at Big O Tire.

Everything is delicious! It's usually not too busy, so service is typically quick and attentive. Both drinks and food are reasonably priced and portions are generous. My only complaint is my pants don't usually button when I leave!

Did a drive by this weekend to see if they are still open. Closed for business, building is empty.

It's a shame that they could not make a go of it. Unfortunately the area surrounding the building does not cater to an upscale bourbon bar. The one time I did go in was a really good experience. I learned quite a bit from the bartender about the various types of bourbons and whiskeys. The cocktails were top notch. They probably would have survived had the bar been located closer to Lowery Park or in Seminole Heights.

The hotel itself is nice. Our room itself was large and clean. King bed with decent sitting area, modest balcony. Glad we took the garden view and upstairs room- the ocean- front views would be a ripoff for the $60 per night upcharge anyway, but there were homeless people everywhere and it would have felt less secure. Also, I hate resort fees normally, but during COVID when all resort amenities are cancelled it's extra infuriating. $30 per day didn't cover much, and we also had to pay $30 per day for parking. So be prepared for a $60 per night in fees for things that really should just be included in the room quote.

We liked the workers here. Elsie was a good host who ignored our eye rolls on the "resort" fees and parking fees, and checked in us with a professional disposition. We had some requests over the weekend that were handled professionally by Elsie and others. No complaints about the staff. 

The beach across the street was nice to look at, but turned into a homeless camp during the day, with lots of rough people hanging out partying. Cop cars came and went all day. At night the beach was closed to camping, so the homeless dispersed except for a few on the hotel grounds and adjacent parks. Didn't feel unsafe, just mainly sad and creepy, but that's not the vibe you look for in an expensive resort. 

Between the hidden fees and the homeless problem, I probably will stay elsewhere next time.

One of our bartenders at another place recommended this place...he recommended Frenchman Street period. We came here because we heard this place was the best one. 
Eh, it's so darn small!! If you don't get here early enough, you can't even squeeze yourself in. Live music was great and cute little outdoor market next door. Next time, I'm coming during the day so I can actually sit and listen to some talented people play.

We ate across the street at Wild Root care (highly recommend) and we stopped in to get an iced coffee before we walked the Freak Alley which is just a few feet away. I order an iced chai latte and it was soooo good. My husband ordered an iced caramel macchiato and it was very good as well. The employee who worked there was friendly, young and hip. They also have Idaho Kombucha in the refrigerator. There was also a large tea selection if you want tea. There was much more there but we were in and out pretty quickly.

I really like this beach bar, They have seating outside on the patio looking at the beach, they have chairs in the sand and they now have fire pits in the sand too. What i really like is the fact that they have decent food! The gator bites here are the best i've ever had and I highly recommend them. They have typical bar food but it's not the poor quality beach bar food that seems to be the standard in the area.. it's actually good. On our last visit we of course ordered the gator bites and chicken quesadillas both were delicious. The only complaint is the service, but i think it's to be expected especially in the evenings when it's super busy.
Pat and Valerie are the best and support bicycling throughout the community and region. I highly recommend them for anything cycling related.

Excellent company & service! I am so pleased with this service and company. Joseph arrived promptly, and was able to repair my frozen lock, not replace. This saved a lot of money. He even explained how to attempt to open the mechanism myself if the need should arise in the future. The lock works like new now! There are a lot of scam companies out there. This one is great!

Are you kidding me, this was a Whole Foods? I have been to a bunch of Whole Foods stores in many big cities, but this was by far my favorite. It was so close to our hotel that after sightseeing, we walked there, went shopping then took a Lyft back to the hotel. This store was massive, with mini eateries, a huge butcher shop, a giant bakery section and prepared foods for dayyyyyysssss! My family and I hung out there for a good while and ended up picking up some goodies to keep in our hotel room. I just wanted to shop 'til I dropped. Every aisle I went down, I discovered something new that I have never seen at any other Whole Food store. It was so exciting to be here because it was just so darn inviting. If you are a Whole Foods fan, you will definitely fall in love with this store probably each time you visit it. Thank you for blowing my mind and keeping my shopping experience an exciting one!
I think their birthday cake just as good as walmart birthday cake.

**** UPDATE:  True to their word below, I was contacted by the manager at the Bonefish location. We had a good discussion about what was right and wrong that night, and he is going to make things right.  So... updating back to 4 Stars. It's o.k. to  have a bad night once in a while if you acknowledge it, and try harder. Thanks for making the effort.  


I generally love Bonefish Grill.  However, tonight's visit was not good.

First, the restaurant was very understaffed.  Even the staff were complaining.  Plus, it seems that Bonefish no longer has bus staff, so the servers have to do it all.  Tables turn over slower, and there are tables everywhere with dirty dishes.

It took about 10 minutes past our reservation time to get seated.  Everything was slow.  We wound up being there over two hours for dinner, with no appetizers, dessert, or coffee.

The most annoying part though was my dinner.  I ordered the 7 oz. Filet Mignon.  When it arrived, it was not a filet -- it was a sirloin that was maybe 1 inch thick.  I've eaten many filets, and this was not one.

I asked about the mistake, and no one -- not even the manager -- would admit the steak was not a filet mignon.  They offered to cook a new steak, but by this point my dinner companions were half done with their meals.  I said I would eat the steak.  If was...fine.  It was not medium, it was well-done.  And it tasted like something I would get at Chilis or Fridays.

The manager said he would "take care of it."  I let it go at that.  When the bill arrived, they adjusted my meal from the $23.99 for the filet mignon to the $17.99 for the 7 oz. sirloin.

I didn't need a free meal or anything, but something other than just charging me for the steak they tried to pawn off on me would be nice.  A free desert maybe?  I wound up eating a steak I did not really want and did not order.

You can do better, Bonefish.  Try harder.

An Asian restaurant on the east side of town that I'm willing to go back to a second time. Only other place from Kolb rd east that has earned my repeat business (Ba-dar). Too many nearby places are so generic or just plain poor tasting. 

Place was quiet, orderly and the service was fast. Staff was very attentive and polite. I ordered the sesame chicken. Had great flavor and wasn't 90% breading like others. 

So far they get 4 stars to start and I'll go from there.

We ate here on our last night in NOLA and it did not disappoint. My partner had the vegetarian spinach ravioli made with a sauce that they use to flavor oysters. It was fantastic! I had the BBQ shrimp and Greek salad. We split a banana foster for dessert.

A rating of 1star or non if communication is the goal of the latest Charter TV RAP commercial

They have succeeded in having us turn off every new Charter rap communication that comes on our TV set.  Most annoying commercial on TV.  Would never listen to it.
Good thing I'm already a customer.  I would never become one after this commercial.

Great place for Tea! 

Went in with a group of 10 gals for a birthday event. It was quaint and a homey place.

I had the blueberry pomegranate tea and it was so delicious! Others had different teas, but it was all delicious! 

The scone was absolutely delicious, especially with the lemon spread. All the little treats on the tiers /scones /sandwiches are homemade. 

We found out that the tea room was run by 2 sisters, one is in charge of making scones/cookies, and the other is in charge of the tea. It is a great partnership that has lasted 18 years. I can see why people would come back for their tea/scones! I am also waiting to go back.

I'm really digging how Edmonton is really embracing variety of foods. We're getting a lot of new ethnic love, especially from the Korean scene and I'm really happy that Nongbu is not the run of the mill Chinese influenced Korean restaurants.

It's situated right across from the Pint off of Whyte Ave and like most places on Whyte Ave traffic was quite challenging. We rolled up around 6PM on a Friday night and as luck would have it we just missed an empty table for two by 30 seconds. As previous reviewers have said it was quite busy considering they've just recently opened. Tables were squeezed in on the main floor (didn't get a chance to see upstairs) so you will be hearing conversations of other parties.

The interior is a really cool concept. The grey colors with the industrial rafters and walls gives it a very loft and modern look. To even out the cold look, there's quite a bit of wooden accents and themes that counter-balances it and brings a more homely and old school charm. It also is pretty cool to see old Korean films projected on the enormous wall. 

As expected, we waited until a table opened but but was warmly greeted and checked on very often and was also served the signature corn brewed tea. Refreshing!

After taking a look at the menu, we noticed the logo of the restaurants was a pretty cool play on Korean and English. Upon quick inspection, it looks like NoBT but Tina pointed out the O with the tiny subtle character on top is actually a character that makes the "ng" sound and the T is the character in "u" sound in Korean. Very cool design choice! 
We decided to start of with some makguli (x2) because hey, drinking amiright. Our lovely waitress who was a blast to talk to recommended we change our original ssam (salad wrap) with noodles and tteokbokki was going to be much for two so we just settled on the ssam (shareable) and tteokbokki. She gave us different drinking styles of the makgulli telling us how the real OG's in Korea party down with makgulli. We opted to listen to the owner's suggestion to shake and mix it as the new kids of Korea prefer. Smooth and delectable, it was very thirst quenching on a hot day. 

The ssam's came out quite plentiful. The portions of pork was a nice surprise to see as they clearly did not skimp out on them. They tasted quite heavenly with the right amount of fattiness and muscle. Naturally greasy but you aren't a shining mess after. The staff were quite accommodating as they provided wetnaps for my greasy meat hooks. The romaine lettuce was quite fresh and the garlic and large jalepeños really highlighted the fantastic dip and pork. This dish, a staple of Korean home comfort really defined the beauty of simplicity. Every part of the dish really came together and shed away from being over complicated. Experimenting with the side dishes of pickled radish and kimchi gave it subtle unique flavors. The bowl of soup you receive also drives home how simple and heart-warming flavors the staff is going for. Sweet and mild which doesn't take away from the flavors of the ssam dip.

Although I've never been to Korea, the tteokbokki here felt much different than other Korean restaurants. They don't look like they've been just tossed in a microwave and their shape is much thicker and didn't taste plastic-y. And how it danced with the sauce, oh my! I had extra and it was great to mix it with any left over rice I had. Speaking with the owner, John, all of the dishes we were eating were made in house and daily to ensure freshness.

For dessert we chose the Melona bar with Milki. I forgot what the cool kid term was but it was essentially a Melona bar (which you can buy at TnT or any Asian supermarket) mashed furiously into a cup of Milki. The resulting product was like drinking a creamy Ramune. Sweet highlights of bubblegum and the creamy honeydew flavors were a great way to wind down the amazing dinner experience.

Our waitress often came by to check up on us and soon enough we were chatting up a storm about music and movies. It was pretty cool to have someone that has a pulse on what is happening back in Korea!

Nongbu means "peasant" or "farmer" in Korean. Genuine and straight to the point that brings people back to Babyface's "Simple Days". Others have pointed out that their menu is small and not much to choose from. I beg to differ as this is often a good sign as they will be directing their attention to what they can absolutely deliver quality dishes on. It's about quality and not quantity. I would be rather worried if a restaurant would have pages upon pages of items. If you're still not convinced, look at the rave and attention 3 boars have as it's a clear example of how less is sometimes more.

Sorry WJK,  you just got bumped to #2.

TL;DR: very cool interiors, homemade food experience. fresh and tasty. Young staff that is in touch with the changes of Korean culture.
Can't do a coffin shaped nail. Nail tech used a metal cuticle pusher underneath my nail and made me bleed from it then continued working without cleaning the tool.

Terrible
Location. Never open during business hours. Rude customer service. Just all around the worse McDonald's I've ever seen and I've never had issues with any of them before

We've been here a number of times and have always enjoyed it! Tonite we tried a few new items - queso dip with chorizo & steak & shrimp. Both were amazing. Combine that with a couple of awesome margaritas, and you've got the perfect end to your day!

Get place to look for a new car.  The sales team is easy to work with.  The cars are as clean as if they were brand new.  The general manager is an great man to work with.  I would go back and buy other vehicle from them any time

Very rude. The girl that works the register seems to hate customers. Their food is horrible lately. They do not care. Found a rotten bug in food and they refused to give a fund. That is bad business practice. Eat there at your own risk.

This place is so cute and the coffee/food is delicious!! It is also an old house that was turned into a little coffee shop. One of the best parts is that it stays open until 5, great for a study sesh after school or on the weekends:)

Sandwiches are good but they are not made to order so if you go in the afternoon they might not have what you want.

i had the turkey croissant and it was decent; not sure if it was worth the $6.75 though.

Also not a lot of seating - lots of people camping out here to study

After a beautiful day at Peddlers Village, and wanting something to eat before heading home, and going to a restaurant we had been to before was closed for renovations, we passed by here, and after Yelping it decided to eat there.
We were real glad we did.
My French onion was good, and her chicken noodle was quite tasty.
Stephen the waiter, recommended a dish and it was scrumptious, the chicken and sausage .
My wife's lemon salmon salad was delicious, as per her.
The cheesecake crunch as pictured was fantastic.
Forgot to take the pic before attacking it.
We thought the service was good and the food as well.
We will certainly take a cruise up there again.


Well, upon a second visit and hearing no response from the management concerning that visit, I would suggest to stay away!!
While the food was still good, the service was deplorable!!
The waitress just didn't seem as if she wanted to be there.
I met my brothers and wife along with my wife there to celebrate a birthday.
The waitress was no help at all with the offerings that night.
And I was really thirsty no more by the time the next drink got to me and my dining mates.
To top it off, she was asked to bring a dessert to the table with a candle.
She did not bring that dessert nor the candle.
When you have meals at this pricepoint, you should have the service required with it.
We have no need to ever return there at this point.

I like the ambience and service of this place but wish the food was better.  I had their wonton soup which was overcooked and I didn't like the texture of it at all.  Their hot and sour soup was a little better.  The rice they serve up is a little watery and pasty.  I wish the meats were more tender.  This may sound strange but I enjoy eating the food after I take it home with me.  When I reheat it at home after everything cools down in the fridge, it tastes better than eating it fresh off their pan.

Oh boy. I always say I'm never gonna go back here because something about this place makes me make terrible decisions. Keeping that in mind, that's usually my intention upon walking in here, so it does it's purpose well. It's the definition of a college bar. After midnight everyone is blacked out and everything is sticky because it's covered in spilled cheap liquor. That being said, no matter how gross and loud and trashy it is, it's always a blast (from what I can remember).

I'm a big fan of Borderlands, especially the Citrana- it's a perfect sour, summer beer. The brewery itself is nice and open, and overall inviting. They have a foosball table as well, which makes it a super fun place to spend the night drinking and hanging out with friends.

Went here last night for the first time and had a really great experience. To start we ordered charcuterie and cheese board. The waitress (Maureen I think, she was excellent) suggested a cheese called Blohorn and it was seriously the best cheese I've ever had! We also got the guanciale and the chorizo and both were delicious. The toasted/seasoned bread was perfect. Next we had a special-roasted sunchokes which were cooked and salted perfectly. We went on to the gnocchi-all I can say is order the large plate because you will want to eat them all! They were so light and the sauce was so flavorful. We also had the beet salad which was served with a creamy dill sauce, which was such a delicious complement to the salad. For an entree we shared the chicken roulade. We had wanted to order the duck special but they were sold out :( The chicken was my least favorite dish, but still very good. For dessert we got the chocolate ganache and berry cobbler. The ganache was rich and creamy and just the right portion size. I didn't care much for the cobbler-it was just different than what I was expecting and had large chunks of apple and I think too much cinnamon. The service was excellent and it was priced affordably! For two with all the food above plus a glass of prosecco and red wine each and two cappuccino's at the end of the meal the bill was $126! We will definitely be back.

One of best Thai in Philly. 
They have a starter- 'Indian pancake with curry', the curry is very much like the famous South Indian curry called "kurma". So happy to have found this place! 
Cheers

Best carne asada fries i have ever have in my life. Go again and again and again. 

When you go, the employees are very kind and the service is extremely quick. 

The churros are fantastic. This is what good Mexican food is.
Friendly staff and great location. Ken and Ted came back and forth to repair&replace the appliances, and they are very efficient.

Sorry I'm being generous with two stars here. First and last time at this establishment for me. I ordered the Boise cheese steak upon the recommendation of the nice lady behind the counter and was very disappointed, especially for the $10 that I paid, I feel it was worth in the neighborhood of $3-3.50 seriously.
The meat was very sparse lacked any sort of flavor, it was perhaps the most bland sandwich I've ever had. I tried adding salt and even ketchup just to make it palatable. I can name at least ten other places to get a cheese steak sandwich in Boise (included fast food chains) that are head and shoulders above this one, I feel so ripped off! 
At least the place looked very clean and the staff seemed friendly.

Horrible service, even with a club member card they were unable to help us in anyway. Most of their rewards are handled through the app which is a really bad app that doesn't work most of the time. We were unable to get what we came for because their app was down. Manager came over and was just as clueless and un helpful. Horrible place, have been to many round ones this is the worst one ! Just do yourself a favor and go to DAVE N BUSTERS

Perfect place for the whole family.  Order at the counter, seat yourself, and then someone will be at your table with delicious chips in no time.  The staff were awesome here.  One of the best Mexican Food spots SB has to offer.  I love all the seafood options.  Get the Los Agaves Seafood  Burrito.
Staff was nice, but I waited 2+ hours to get a Covid Test. I had an appointment time and was seen over 2 hours later. Waiting room wasn't even full.

They literally take away plates you are working on to kick you out 30 minutes before closing. They spray the cleaner all over and around you and your food so that you finish up and leave. I was working on my food and this waitress brought out boxes to hand them to me out of no where, staring at me and waiting for me until I grabbed them out of her hands. And another waitress came and quickly took away all our plates, even dropping a spoon on my husband. Ridiculously rude service.
I thought this place would be mediocre since its owned by a franchise king. I was wrong. The place was amazing and the service was as well! I am definitely going back!

Thanks for fitting me in quickly. Ashley was great and had no problem once I said my cut was off, the keratin didn't take and my gray roots were still showing around forehead and temple- BUT Covid19 hits - who would think. I know she would have fixed it but we are on lockdown. I spent way to much to now have to self correct- this a 4

Always consistent, fast, professional and quality Greek food... staff was professional and available...

GYRO meat was tender and awesome. ..

Great job..

Had brunch/lunch on Sunday in Bellevue.  Brunch menu is extremely limited.  My son asked our server about the build your own waffle option on the brunch menu.  Her response was "I don't know anything about the brunch menu".  Seriously?  Perhaps she should have offered to find out which would have been the appropriate response.  Drink refills were very slow as well.  I don't dine here often and that's a good thing.

If I could leave no stars I would.  Cindy is pushy, bossy and at the end of the day, she not only hung up on me, she neglected to tell me about a dangerous situation her people apparently discovered.  She told me that she didn't want anything to do with my fireplace and then wanted to charge me to remove the product...and then charge me $400 in a restocking fee,  I also never saw the reduction in my cost for the $175 measure fee  in my invoice.
