starting off with 3 stars for the Ardmore Music Hall...Please impress me on my next visit so we can get upto 4!

Saw Rusted Root last night, my first trip into "Brownie's" since the renovation.

The building has changed...altho the bars are in the same place, they got rid of the front "pool table" section, and removed the elevated seating\tables that were next to the pool tables. (update:  they just moved the tables and for a price they you can reserve them in this raised seating area)  They also moved the stage from the side wall, to the end wall next to the bathrooms...the venue seems smaller and more cramped than Brownie's did after they cut off the pool room area.

Since the stage moved...there are actually bad places to sit\stand, see and listen.  We ended up right outside the bathrooms near the old "pizza and wing" window, basically we were behind everyone on stage but the drummer...so we were very close, but looking at the back of most of the band.  Additionally, the speakers point straight out front so the sound was NOT good where we were located. 

4$ for miller lite bottle...4$ for a lager draft...2$ for a coke and subsequent refills...It's not sink or swim, but hardly highway robbery either...The bar area fills up fast, then people fill up the spaces around the bar making it very tough to move in there.  This also adds to the cramped feeling...the bartenders did great, there were 4 behind the bar with a barback and they did a very good job with a crowd on hand for Rusted Root.  If you can get a spot at the bar, THIS is the best way to enjoy the show\eat\drink.  They do have food, but I couldn't imagine how i would eat anything crammed into a standing position without even a place to put my drink.  I'd also note...whatever you order from the Mediterranean inspired menu has to be brought out of the kitchen thru a throng of 6' tall people by a girl who has to hold the plate over her head just to make it thru the crowd.  I could have sampled from several passing plates last night if I chose too.  Just saying...If I were the AMH, I'd be looking at more hand foods that people can eat standing up...this might be a  great place for turkey legs or other food on a stick type options.  

The food I saw looked pretty good.  I am actually disappointed the "pizza and wings" window was closed, that was a fantastic way to quickly feed a bunch of people at Brownie's.  

The men's room was a disaster...I don't think it saw any renovations.  I'll use the ladies room next time!

Restaurant area is a bit expensive but the food was good. Pool table on 2nd floor was missing a ball, but staff let us use the downstairs one for free since we had already swiped our game card at the upstairs table. Fast service and nice staff. Good drinks.

Chorizo burrito for breakfast was like Trump had built the wall, the eggs were hot and the chorizo was cold.
There was no rush as the Sunday crowd was two people and one guest.
Come here for happy hour! 3-6 pm I believe. They have some really great sushi specials.

This is my first time getting liquid gel/hard gel nails full set is $40. They're great Katie made sure to match up my nails, was very gentle with my hands and nail beds, made sure I like the process every step of the way. She is very professional and I can't wait to come back and explore more services. 

If you're coming in the afternoon make sure to book an appointment. I came in the morning so they were able to take me right away.
Awesome place to get your phone fixed! Fast services, great pricing, and friendly employees! I'll definitely use them for future phone needs

I went running in the Richland Creek Greenway for the first time today, and I love it!  As I've become increasingly disillusioned with dodging cars on the sidewalk-free streets of West Nashville, it was so nice to be able to run in a great, natural setting, on well-maintained paths, and without oncoming cars...

A few things impressed me.  First, there are at least four access points to the greenway (two in Sylvan Park, two off of White Bridge Road), with parking at each access point (= great accessibility).  Second, most of the paths are under a canopy of trees, which provides nice shade on hot days. And third, the paths seemed to be well constructed and well maintained - the three bridges are quite cool, and the paved paths seem ideal for biking or rollerblading (in addition to running or walking).

I think the Greenway project is awesome for Nashville, and I highly recommend Richland Creek Greenway as a great and easy place to get some exercise, experience some nature, and just be outdoors!
With lobsters to taste and with a feeling of being in Main?. Like a tiny little shack, Philadelphia is nothing like Main
It's average and nothing to write home about. Cuisine is gringo style-so if you desire more authentic, you may want to look elsewhere. Chips and salsa are good.

I have wanted to try this place for a long time.  I made it there today and even though the wait is annoying, it is part of the charm.   I have been thinking about the bagel and whitefish salad I had.  The whitefish was very good, but the bagel was just fair.  I am not sure why the bagel was not a winner for me.  It was good, but the pop up bagel shop in my neighborhood has much better bagels.  Also, the iced coffee was so weak from the melting ice it was lousy.  I am not sure I will come back here.

If you are talkin' roast pork sandwiches or Italian hoagies, sorry Philly, Lenny's got you beat.  Usually working behind the counter, Lenny has the most flavorful, juicy roast pork I've ever had.  You have a wide variety of peppers to choose from, from the hot goat horns to the tangy reds to the sweets.  Make sure to pick up some provolone as well.

The Italian hoagies are well worth the global nuclear caloric bomb you will inflict on yourself.  The meats are top notch, and the rolls...

The roll is the secret ingredient to any deli sandwich, and Lenny's fresh Conshohocken Bakery rolls turn a great sandwich into ambrosia.

Skip the chains and the gimmicky hoagie shops and make a bee-line right to Lenny's for your next roast pork fix.

Came to New Orleans with my hubby - while he was at a conference, I had ample time to explore this great city. However, as a solo explorer, I did feel a little limited on what wandering I could do by myself. Fortunately I stumbled upon New Orleans Secrets tours. I enjoyed this tour company so much that I ended up taking three separate tours with them over two days - and am looking forward to touring more with them on my next visit to NOLA!  I started with their French Quarter History (and Cocktails) Tour with Alexandra, which was an excellent orientation to the very interesting history of the city, a peek inside some of the city's top-notch restaurants, and opportunity for mind-blowingly delicious cocktails (purchased separately at the tour-goer's discretion, with no pressure to purchase). No swill well drinks here, my friend!  Everything was expertly crafted (both the drinks and the tour). As an afternoon tour, it was a nice way to catch some of the daytime energy of the French Quarter and see the area begin its transition into the evening scene. The following morning I joined the Garden District Tour with Richard, which was filled with engaging historical, architectural, and cultural heritage info. We spent roughly the first half of the tour in Lafayette Cemetery, and Richard did an excellent job. Admittedly, before the tour I thought the above-ground cemeteries to be a mere curiosity, and otherwise didn't give them much thought. Richard's tour provided context that was fascinating! The Garden District was also presented in an engaging manner, and the area is so beautiful it warrants a visit each time you are in New Orleans. No cocktails on this AM tour, but an opportunity for coffee and upon the conclusion you're close enough to Commander's Palace to enjoy a 5-star lunch (just bring some dressier footwear in your bag - no sneakers, but blouses with "dressy" non-distressed jeans should be OK for lunch... Commander's Palace does have a strict dress code for dinner. It's amazing and absolutely plan to include that during your stay). Finally, that evening I re-joined Alexandra for the Ghosts of the French Quarter Tour, which was a delight! She does an excellent job sharing some of the factual historical records of the French Quarter's more grizzled stories, relaying some of the city's fantastical lore, and makes the tour truly enjoyable for both believers and skeptics. This tour included two stops for drinks at (again) top-notch places, again purchased at the discretion of the tour-goer with no pressure. Overall, I'm genuinely impressed with New Orleans Secrets - their guides are engaging and knowledgeable, there's good depth of information, the tours are well-paced, and the cap the group size at just-right numbers (8-10 per tour, maximum). Definitely fantastic for history buffs and nerdier types like me (ie., not bawdy drunken tours). Meet-up locations are easy to find, and the guides are helpful in recommending any subsequent activities/restaurants/etc. that you could want. I can't wait to go on their Voodoo Tour, Night Out Tour, and Foodie tour when I next visit!  Next time I'll know to book my New Orleans Secrets tours first, and then build the rest of my stay around them. You should do the same!

I went to that place because it was ranked number 1 in New Hope. But it was the worst experience ever. I waited 20 minutes just to be sited. After we got a table we waited 15 additional minutes just for a hello and water to the table. Then, after a few additional minutes the waitress took the order. No drinks, no appetizer, just the order. Then she brought water. We waited more than an hour and fifteen minutes to got the food. Within that hour no-one asked anything, if someone needed more water, if was everything ok, nothing in the whole hour. After it, the food was salty and with lack of flavor. I won't come back in my life.

This is probably my favorite restaurant on the north side of Indy. The only thing wrong with this location is that it's not large enough! There is always a wait, especially for weekend brunch. Of course, there is a good reason for this. I've never had a meal at Patachou that wasn't original, made with high-quality ingredients, and tasty as heck. I love their omelettes with goat cheese or cream cheese, and you have to try the Cinnamon toast. It's so buttery and cinnamony, you won't be sorry. I have also had their Cuban breakfast when I wanted to hit my nutrition goals for the day - it was good for me and so tasty - who would've thought to add Pesto? Only Patachou. My other favorite thing about this place is the 4-5 blend varieties of coffee from which you can choose. And of course they're all great. Friendly service, beautiful decor and ambience... I just wish the restaurant was twice this size!

The location and view are amazing! The quality of food is excellent and the locally-brewed beer is very good. The only draw back is it can be very loud when busy, making it difficult to hold a conversation with your dinner/lunch partners. This place is pretty cool and we look forward to returning!
Love everything about this place. Greater as we walked in the door. Got to taste prior to purchase!  Fresh bakes cookies cakes and pies. All delish! This is our go to for a sweet treat!

I really wish I could give a better review....but the management really ruined this place for me, hence the two star review.

We ordered a dozen chargrilled oysters and when they came out, not only were they cold, but one of the shells was missing an oyster!  When we brought this to our waiters attention, he told his manager and they offered to give us a free dessert....ummm ok...shouldn't you have at least brought us another oyster...those things aren't cheap!  We then proceeded to wait 25 minutes for the rest of our food to come out...and guess what...it was cold!  I am not talking lukewarm, I am talking about ice cold French fries and barbeque shrimp that maybe they thought I wanted cocktail style?  We flagged down the waiter who in turn brought over the manager, he apologized and promised to get us new food...well...about 90 seconds later our food was back....I guess they figured they would just throw it in the microwave???  My dad's steak was chewy, which should not be the case for a filet, they didn't even put fresh fries on the plate!  We were so annoyed, but were hungry and just wanted to get out of there so we told the waiter we didn't even want the free dessert, when he brought us the bill, they had not comped a single item!  Any other fine dining restaurant would have made up for sending out cold food, but not The Southern and their manager Jimmy who was less than apologetic.  We felt bad and didn't want to stiff the waiter, but we were not happy with our experience, the manager that night.  The worst part is, the items that were cooked correctly were actually really good...but the lack of customer service sealed the fate of The Southern for us.

What a great experience! I've been a Mercedes Benz of Fort Washington customer for 12-15 years and watched the dealership steadily go downhill! I visited Keenan today and had a first class experience, and will now be a Keenan customer! I've always loved the automobiles and now am excited to be with a class dealership.                                 

I just bought a car from Keenan and truly regret ever going to Mercedes Fort Washington. Truly a first class experience from salesman (Paul) to service, highly recommend checking Keenan before you let Mercedes Fort Washington rip you off!!!!!

My love for Wyliepalooza (and their original spot in  Irvington) is well-known, but there's something so charming about this SoBro location! Maybe it's the cute blue shack or the walk-up window along the Monon Trail. Maybe it's the string lights and picnic tables out front. Either way, this spot serves up delicious hand-dipped Wyliepalooza ice cream in creative and indulgent flavors that are usually packed with gobs of goodies (I tried peanut butter cookie dough this visit and OMG). During COVID, this spot scores extra points because you never have to go indoors to pick up your ice cream if you use the walk-up window. I see many Monon Trail bike rides for ice cream in my future!

Just had my first visit to Gander Mountain. As usual, I made my way straight back to the gun counter. Thomas K was so helpful, and informative, and never made me feel out of place being a woman in the gun department. That is a hard thing to come by. I look forward to many firearm purchases here!
Nice hidden Gem. Area is not so good but live band, bar and good drinks. I would definitely come back.

Beautiful pastry cafe in Edmonton 124st district, reminds me of a fancy pastry shop in Paris. Upon entering Duchess you can tell this place is a cut above the rest. I read their macaroons are world renowned and that's no BS they are exceptional. They also serve coussants, tarts and such. You can order custom cakes and baking for events if you need. They offer coffee, espresso, lattes etc. For all your cafine needs. It can be very busy on the weekend but the line up moves quickly it's just getting a seat that could be the issue. Highly recommend, take you inlaws for browning points the lady's will love it.

Frequented this place quite often in dental school. The food is OK, though they've been two times at lesser where my order took an extremely long time, while the rest of the group had their delivered in 10 minutes of so. Both times I requested a refund since my lunch hour was over. Their cheesecake also taste like cardboard with the consistency of cottage cheese. Not good.

Was in town on business and just happen to come across this place.  Everything about the Noble Crust was fantastic.  Ordered the Noble Pig pizza and the first bite was just incredible.  The flavors were so good I demolished the whole pizza!  Our waiter very good and very helpful.  I need to plan a trip back to St. Petersburg just to eat at the Noble Crust.

Overall, I had a good experience. The restaurant itself is very nicely decorated and has a great atmosphere. However, I think the live music kind of cheapens it/makes it difficult to actually have a high class dinner. The music is good, but it's really loud and is only a few feet away from where everyone is sitting.

The food was good- the chicken puff pastry appetizers were wonderful and I highly recommend them. The margarita shrimp entree was a little lacking in the flavor department. The snapper was very well-liked by my boyfriend but it was a little too strong tasting for my liking. The berry cobbler dessert was also delicious.

Overall, I would go back but I would go early, maybe around 5:30 when the band isn't playing. I think the band starts around 7, so if you don't really like listening to it while you eat, you should get there early. It's a very good restaurant but just not great!
Great food. Great staff. well packed hookahs and very fair prices.

Mr. M seeks to rate on a world-class/world-leading dining scale, not one relative for a particular town.  To be balanced, for St. Louis, this place is a 5 and one of the better experiences in town, on the international stage, a 3, hence the 4-average rating.  Was in town for a Monday early bird dinner and had a solid experience!  The Metropolitan Sq. building is a high rise downtown corporate building and you're dining down the hall from a lawyer/auditor/white collar office, in a sterile office building (though the art deco marble in the lobby strongly resembling the historically significant Mohrenstrasse U-Bahn in Berlin's red marble).  The view is striking and despite the low-ish ceilings and rather unremarkable tables/chairs.  It will take your breath away and you'll be having the best view in town.  Normally, great view = horrible food, but not the case here.  Food-wise, there are both home runs and called third strikes here, but when the menu excels, it is world-class.  Service was friendly, not formal, some might even say casual (but certainly not neglecting aspects of proper service).  The before 6pm service featured a $33 or $36 menu with a house salad, cheese bread, entrée choice, and Chef's choice of desert (ie., no choice).  Both the cheaper options of pasta, chicken parm or marsala, or salmon ($33) to the pricier beef entrees (tenderloin au poivre, or tenderloin tips over risotto; $36) represent significant savings over $55 for filet or $43 for chicken marsala on the regular menu.  Italian red wines ranged from $35 to $100+ and were helpfully arranged from lightest to heaviest.  And wow, great stuff...a red friuli for $35 and the choice of the evening, a $45 '16 Barbera d'Alba.  The Barbera shone, reminded me of dinners in the Piedmont and paired so well with everything due to its versatility.  You're hard pressed to find a wine of that quality on US shores at that price in such an upscale restaurant.  Started with toasted raviolis ($16), the St Louis classic of square-shaped mixed meat raviolis that are deep fried in a light breadcrumb and served with a sweet sauce.  Kemoll's are among the best in St. Louis and were made in house and didn't taste like the duopoly of toasted ravs found in most StL restaurants.  Very meaty, hefty rectangles of ravioli with a hearty slightly-sweet meat sauce.  The main, of beef tenderloin tips over risotto sang and whether by intention or not, tasted of very Northern Italian cooking (think near the Austrian border)....a beautiful risotto of great flavored texture and a hearty beef stock gravy over the meat tips.  It was profound.  Dining partner's filet was solid with a very flavorful cream sauce.  Now to the negatives: the breadsticks were very heavy....bread and a very heavy (and oily cheese mix) that lacked flavor.  The house salad with the famous dressing was a one-dimensional salad with a very thick dressing of a Parm base, but not very much liquid, resulting in a salad that clumped together.  The chef's choice dessert was a one dimensional, rather-too-sweet chocolate cake; sugar flavor overwhelming chocolate taste.  Dinner for 2, featuring the early-dinner special and a bottle of wine with the add-on $16 ravioli ran $135+$15 tax= $150 pre-gratuity.  This is a St Louis experience, with glimmers of greatness.  Wine was amazing yet some items disappointed.

I came here the other night for restaurant week.  Contrary to other reviews I've seen posted, I was able to make a reservation in advance on their website.  They are not on Open Table.  I came here mostly for its location because I was taking a friend from out of state here.  We were able to sit outside and it was a really lovely evening.  The scene is picturesque, and my friend really enjoyed the atmosphere of the neighborhood.  

I want to preface the review by saying the reason I am only giving them 3 stars is for the food, but the service was really outstanding.  I spilled red wine on my white pants and our waitress was able to scrounge up a tide pen from somewhere and also gave me a hot towel to put on the stain after I used the pen.  The steam nearly lifted the stain right out.  Much kudos to the waitress!!  Very lucky to have had her!  

Onto the food, It was good but I was not incredibly impressed.  For the first course, I had the grilled corn on the cob with chili aioli, feta and lime.  This was my favorite part of our meal.  For the main course, my friend and I split the potato crusted ahi tuna and the chicken milanese.  The couscous that came with the tuna was very fresh and delicious.  I had higher expectations from the tuna and felt that it lacked flavor.  The chicken was simple and very good.  Very crispy!  Even though it was fried, the arugula made the dish feel lighter.  For dessert, we had a mix of cinnamon risotto, chocolate lava cake, and creme brulee.  All were simple yet very delicious.  

Overall, I might come back here again for the atmosphere, but I was hoping for more.  If you are going to stick with simplicity, the flavors need to be more prominent.

Excellent all around! The man running the front desk was nice and extremely organized. They had 4 people signing in at one time with complete protection. 

The nurse who took me back was nice and personable. The doc was fantastic! Even talked to me in depth about cough drops. 100% would recommend to anyone!

Great service, Great atmosphere & great food. We had a reservation & we were seated right away which doesn't happen at many restaurants. Our server, Lisa, really knew the menu & helped us make great selections. She definitely made the whole experience! The food was delicious too.  
I had the Tempura Shrimp & Vegetables and loved it.  We will go back!

Drew Loftus Manager, saves the day with a fantastic experience. I am truly grateful for his knowledge, professionalism, courtesy, and customer care.
Zoe

This place has consistently slow service. Tonight's visit took the cake. We waited 20 minutes on the phone to place an order for pick-up. We ordered the house special pizza. It took 30 minutes to get our pizza, and it was the worst pizza I've ever had. A frozen pizza from Walmart would have tasted better! The bottom
Of the pizza was soggy, and very doughy! Save your stomach and go somewhere else.

better than the one on 12th and girard mainly since 9am and everything is ready to order( girard location not so much )

full selection of breads,sandwiches and never crowded (when i go anyways) 9-930am.

the dude, sandwich maker doesn't seem the happiest and talks a lot of s*it under his breath while making sandwiches but the hell with it, the sandwiches taste good. i'll take the hatred for a fresh sandwich anyday of the week. Dude gets the order right 9 times outta 10 but if its a big order don't expect the sandwiches to be labled. he looked like he wanted to jump the counter and do some mortal kombat type beat down when i asked last time

UnFing Believable. 

Fatty Brisket. Melts in your mouth. No sauce necessary. 
Popovers.  (who has popovers these days?)
Mac and Cheese. 
Gourmet Deviled Eggs with bacon. 
Ravs with brisket. 
100 Bourbons. 
Friendly and knowledgable people.  
A+
Best in the Midwest?...including Texas..

We had lunch here yesterday and were pleasantly surprised. The Bistro is decorated comfortably with nice touches and the service was truly some of the best in the area. My kids each had a gluten free pizza, which is second only to Risotteria. It was a great combo of a delicious crust, great tasting sauce and just the right amount of cheese. I had the salmon salad which was good (the guacamole tasted a little funky to me) and the salmon was cooked a little more than I like. Our server gave us samples of the tomato bisque, which was very good. One last thing, the iced tea was fresh. We will certainly return.

This place is dining as an old-school experience, kinda like New Orleans itself. Went here with my girlfriend for her birthday, and it was worth the $$$ price for the service and the spectacle.

The fun began with a friendly bartender who gave us some useful breakfast-place suggestions when we asked, and then offered to have us seated well before our reservation time.

It went on from there with a table by an old-world-style courtyard, and waitstaff who knew exactly when to check on us and when to leave us alone. Steak Diane and Bananas Foster made tableside, as much theater as food. And then when we let slip it was my girlfriend's birthday, they brought out another decadent dessert.

All in all, it was an experience to remember!

Love that a Thai restaurant still exist after a pandemic. The staff doesn't look like they are westernized and off track. Looks and is ran by authentic workers. Love the desserts. My second time coming hoping for better quality of rice. Glad the red pineapple curry was good. A bit soupy.

It's such a cute place, and it's stocked- literally, to the ceiling!  I like that this store looks so organized and neat.  Much cleaner than Daiso stores I've visited.  I'm an old fan of Pink Panther, so they have cute plush dolls and very soft neck pillows of every color and animal.  Highly recommend this store.  You have to pay for shopping bags though.

perfect espresso. Im a barista. I live 3 blocks away and noticed Synesso and Malkonig grinder in the window. perfect espresso every time. Vegan menu looks delicious. Also, sent people there and heard the vegan cheese steak was delicious. my friend took one to go after devouring one in. 

  The coffee is reanimator and they also have drip and ice. It's done impeccably I'm crazy picky. go get yourself some you south sillyians!

I have always liked the keg. My mother enjoys it and always prefers to brings us here for steak. This place is very popular because every time we come there's always a wait. We always forget to reserve but it's not a long wait. Special occasions it is. One time we went and the longest we waited was 45 min. The servers are good and fast at their job. Seem to know i what their doing.

I could not write it better than ET comment... my father in law and mother in law both fell out of there beds one fall resulting in a broken eye socket. Awful hospital I would not bring a stray dog there. Nurses are loud at night like its a party, very few times to check on patients no food or water.They would Rather have patients in bed than tring to help them out of bed to use bathroom for convenience for them not to have to help them in and out of bed.

I love the coop! It has been such a great find in my IV bubble while going to UCSB. The staff is always friendly and they have a great organic produce selection. Also they are constantly doing little events with free samples! Lots of healthy options and vegetarian/vegan alternatives. Can get pricey though!

This bar was next to the hotel I was staying at last week. It was very convenient in terms of location for me, specially in Feb weather. I tried quite a few different things. The baja shrimp tacos, the Buffalo wrap, and the breaded chicken with mashed potatoes and broccoli, they were all delicious! I would definitely come back and eat at Wolfies! The downside was that it's probably going to be busy! I found myself a little overwhelmed one night because it was very crowded and didn't feel like they were keeping people 6ft apart! The staff was so nice, i had 3 different servers/bartenders and they were all so sweet! So keep that in mind if it's a busy night. And it's the only reason I didn't give 5 stars.

Looking for decent seafood, we dropped in to give Shells a try.  We tried several dishes from shrimp, scallops to chicken pasta.  Overall decent service and portions but there was nothing special about the dishes - just seemed average to me.

I was looking forward to my brunch meal at Amis and based on the reviews and menu I saw online had high hopes.

The meal started out fine - we were seated, offered still (bottled) water, etc. But then our waitress disappeared for about 15 minutes only to come back to inform us of some changes to the menu, including some items which we planned to order. So on to plan B - which can be difficult when your dining partner has a few food allergies. We asked if they could make slight alterations to some items on the menu and they said NO. This left the only item on the menu which my wife would eat - a ribeye steak. She wanted to try a few other items but was disappointed at the lack of flexibility in the kitchen. The steak was flavorful and well cooked. Wish it came with a sunny side up egg.

I ordered the pasta with roasted squash and walnuts, which was filling but not as flavorful. Also had a cornetti stuffed with apricots which was good, but not sure I would pay $5/piece if it were served at a bakery.

Fresh squeezed blood orange juice was a nice touch.

Overall, the good was food, but I deducted 1 star for the lack of flexibility in the kitchen, slow service and very high noise level,

We left a little less than impressed or full, so stopped at a Garces place on the way home.

He littered all over the property with water bottles that he never picked up because they were still there after they left.

I then separated all of my items that were also containers into the back bedroom so it could be loaded last because it would be going to the on-property storage first that was in my building.
