For a son who cares deeply about his mother, I highly appreciated how they treated her and made her feel better and helped her. I thought it would be very expensive as my mom's travel insurance didn't cover it. But Dr. Kleinova's payment was extremely fair and they took off the x-rays. 

What can you ask for more?  Honest care, High Quality work and fair price. 

So I HIGHLY recommend her and her office.

Another French Club outing!

There was a big red flag when I first came in: we had yet to be seated. The coordinator for our group made a reservation on Monday for a Thursday dinner at 7:30. She even called that afternoon to verify the reservation as well.

We were not seated until 8:15.

Sure, we were a group of about 20, but still. When the person says that there's a group of 20 coming, you best be able to accomodate that many people at the time we say we're arriving.

So, while we waited in the bar area, I ordered their house red, which was really nice. While reading the drinks list, there's a wee panel on the left hand side that explains the history of the restaurant. To make a long story short, the great-grandfather of the current owner settled in Indianapolis from Italy and opened a restaurant on Illinois St. This was back in the 30s. The restaurant was a big success but, an "incident" caused the original restaurant to be shut down in 1940 (their words). Which leads me to wonder what kind of incident was it? A fire? Mass shooting? Carbon monoxide poisoning? Generalized anti-Italian sentiment that was growing around that time? Regardless, I was really confused. I'll have to check the old Indy newspapers to see if there's anything regarding this hella vague "incident."

While waiting, they were kind enough to offer us appetizers at the bar. I had the toasted ravioli which were also really nice. They're cheese ravioli, so if you're a vegetarian, you should totes try them. For my meal, I order the Veal Picatta because, as a recent college grad who can barely boil water, I cook pasta for myself most nights of the week. It was pretty good and I paired it with a house salad with balsamic vinaigrette dressing and polenta. Once I got towards the end of the plate, I tasted the drippings of the mix of veal, broccoli, and polenta on my plate and it was *really* salty. I was a little turned off by it.

Anyway, we all sat outside and it was a lovely atmosphere. I'm always finding an excuse to venture out into downtown, and this was worth the trip.

Quick vegan review here, to help fellow vegans coming through.  They have a few veganizable options here, and for that I am very grateful.  For starters, you can get the hummus dish or the Middle Eastern (minus the tzatziki sauce).  As a main dish, there is a veggie burger made with Match-Meat (an STL company), a Portobello Wrap (omit the aioli sauce), and a Hummus Veggie Wrap (sans the feta).  I always get the Veggie Burger because I'm a fan of Match-Meat. In order to veganize the veggie burger, you must request the gluten-free bun. It's pretty thick and dry, so I'm not a fan of that bun. You'll also need to omit the chipotle mayo, which is unfortunate because you can get a 4-pack of Just Mayo vegan chipotle and garlic mayo from Sam's or Costco for under $5. With that gluten-free bun and no toppings (ketchup didn't cut it), it's underwhelming.  If I lived in STL, I'd bring my own bottle of vegan mayo to help a burger out. But again, I do appreciate that they're thinking of veg*ns and offering veg-friendly options. As meat-free diets continue to become mainstream, I'm sure they'll continue to improve in this area.
Really cute place! Every thing I ordered was excellent - pastries, manoushe, hummus and Lebanese omelette.  Chai latte was also super!! Would love to go back for dinner. Noise level is a bit high.
these bagels slap. & the bagel sandwhiches are worth the price. in conclusion, i love it here.

This is our first stop after leaving the hotel on our way home from Reno to San Jose. The bagels are always fresh and the staff are friendly. It's a small place with about 5 tables. There's a lot of really cool artwork on the walls. I get my usual #4, scrambled eggs, Swiss, tomatoes, and avocados in a garlic bagel. I've tried other ones too but this is by far my favorite.

I came in on a Tuesday to change my name due to marriage. It was around 3pm, it was pretty full inside, but I left about 20 minutes later. It went quick! Take a ticket, wait for them to call you, have all your documents ready- simple as that.

If you have children its best to make sure you have something to keep them occupied. The security guard had to keep advising a woman to turn her phone on silent. Her child was watching cartoons on the phone. They advise everyone to keep quiet so the interviews can be heard clearly. 

They do not allow food or drinks inside, so with that being said, I recommend eating or drinking prior to entering the building. They will make you throw it out or put it in your car.

Overall I had a great experience.

New bbq in Carolwood area. First off, the place is huge! Even though it was really busy we worked our way through the line pretty quickly.  They have a large variety of options and they have a huge sweet shop. My order was to go and they messed up on the sides a little but I caught it before we left so it was not a big deal.  Very yummy will definitely be back again.

Bottomless mimosas + bananas foster french toast = brunch-perfection incarnate. This place offers yummy food, tasty drinks and is perfectly positioned for people watching. Our waiter was sweet and attentive, the food was yummy and delivered in a timely way, and the prices were beyond reasonable. The decor borders on tacky and it feels a little disjointed but, all in all, a great brunch spot in the Quarter.
Great place! Really enjoyed the locals, the food, the entertainment& the drinks/bartenders &food too!  Ya'll come on!!

They just left throw up on the floor for 20 minutes at the table next to me and then tried to force me to clean it up saying I knew who did it..... I will never coming back. Tried to tell them I didn't know who threw up and to stop yelling at me and the bartender Molly screamed at us and told us to lose our attitudes. She's now screaming profane words. Don't come here unless you want to clean up strangers throw up :)  would give 0 stars if I could.

Having come here 50+ times in the last 2 years, I thought it was finally time to write a review to juxtapose my negative review of the creepy, beat Noodle City experience.

Appetizers:
The spring rolls have evolved into authentic, fresh goi cuon- comparable to the quality of LA or Bay Area restaurants and arguably the best Asian dish in all of Goleta. The egg rolls and chicken wings are good and satisfy a craving for either.

Pho:
The pho has improved so much with time. The meat quality puts noodle city to a shame. Brisket can be very good on an on day and makes the broth delicious. The noodles are solid but come clumped together which is where I see there being room for improvement- still as we are in the SB/goleta area, only Empty Bowl has noodles which are better.

Bún tht nng:
If it's too hot for broth or I'm just craving this dish/anything with fish sauce- phamous does a solid and simple version of the noodle dish. Nothing to complain about (would like it if there were more meat perhaps) and with this dish alone I am full.

Service:
Excellent. Nice people, family vibe, extremely pleasant and kind.

Miscellaneous:
Beer and wine would make this establishment finally take over as the preference for college kids who go to noodle city just so they can get a drink with their soup. A loyalty program would be a huge draw as well (every 10th bowl free?).Would love to see this place be the only place within an hours drive to serve Banh Khot. 

All in all, phamous is a 5 Star for where it is and what it is.

I booked an appointment online, and when I arrived, I walked in and said to the girl near the counter that I had a 4 pm appointment. She replied, okay, said she's coming. A woman approached me and said hi, so I replied I have a 4 pm appointment; she said, what do I want? I said I formerly requested online a cut and perm (it seems strange that before being introduced as whoever she was, she could introduce herself, but that didn't take place the entire time I was there.  If it was supposed to be her client, you would think she knew what services I said I made an appointment to get. It's courteous to be introduced and eased in, but that was a backward fail. I don't work in a salon, but I would assume you know the services someone booked online if you were given a client in a salon (I booked the afternoon before).
Then I was invited to a chair where I would show pictures of what I would like from my perm (which was a stacked spiral).  Upon proceeding, I made it through the rods installed and to the shampoo chair where I would get drenched in water all down my neck and back to do the solution, then neutralize and rinse (which may or may not have been avoidable, I don't know how it happened while I'm laid back in the shampoo bowl, but it did and by a lot). I was given towels beside the one's she had placed. Then she tells me I'm halfway there ("too beautiful," she said, I assume because the rollers were out and the product was rinsed). She sits me up and tells me to go back to the chair (her station). 

Next thing she comes and starts combing my hair with a fine-tooth comb. . This should not be done ever on permed or curly hair because it causes the curls to break and causes frizz which is the worst thing to happen, and especially minutes after a perm was processed.  With permed, you use a wide-toothed comb, but not until 24 hours after a perm. I told her that. She had to borrow a wide-tooth comb from a lady across the room. As if that was still to be used instead at the moment. I don't know if the perm would have been less frizzy or not, had she not used the fine-toothed comb or not, but several times after she went through with the wide-toothed comb, what does she do? She was using the fine-tooth comb again, multiple times and times again. At this point, my knowledge I have seemed not to matter because I put my hair in her unprofessional hands. I didn't know what or how to change what was unprofessionally happening and to my hair. I am not a licensed professional, but I knew these steps weren't supposed to happen. Then she cut and blow-dryed without a diffuser; she didn't have one, I suppose either. Then she asks me when the hair is 40% dry (as in a manner like she is done). "How do I like it?" Omg! Really I said it looks like Ramen noodles and is uneven in the cut. I said I suppose it's not your fault my hair didn't take much curl, but the cut is horrible. I said, what do you do?  So, she starts cutting some more. 

 I had to just accept this mess. I am not sure how my hair took the perm is entirely her fault (though her mistakes and lack of care made it worse for sure) or just a product fault (perm solution - I asked her if she was using an alkaline or acid perm, and she proceeded using alkaline on highlighted and lightened colored hair). I do know her lack of know-how and proper care of hair wasn't there. I have read and understand the service given lacked knowledge and best possible results. Even though she still kept positive energy (through multiple mistakes, after it was too late to fix totally, only subtle improvements), I still left her a $20 tip and paid for both services (perm and cut), I don't believe I properly received here at InSignia. I have to advise against her perm skill. Her lack of product to complete the job with ease (wide-toothed comb, hair diffuser, I assume her not having an acid perm, which is recommended for my hair) was a fail, but I'm walking away with my head; down!   The experience I described is reviewed so that you may reconsider a likely result! The hairdresser I explained is named Nancy (Vietnamese). I don't dislike her as an individual human being (especially because mistakes can happen, but not from a skilled hairdresser), not because of her personality, but she lacked the skill and care I needed and expected today; as an individual whose confidence and pocket$ were at a lasting loss - BEWARE!
This link below informs things done in error, and so will other sources, but what can I do NOW!?
https://softerhair.com/aftercare-recommendations-and-products-for-permed-hair/

i love this place. I went here probably a couple months ago and forgot to write a review. The food is fresh and so good. They staff is friendly and kind and the bathroom is so cute and clean! you can always tell a restaurant is clean from their bathroom!:) It is sorta hidden but worth getting to!

I don't get the bad reviews. Sure it's not a Ruth's Chris, but out of the TGI Friday's/Chili's/Applebee's/Outback lineup, Applebee's wins by a land slide. I got the quesadilla burger, and it was delicious. Very innovative. My only complaint is I asked for it cooked medium well, and it came out well done. But that can happen anywhere, and furthermore, I'd rather they be far on the well done side than the medium or rare side. The onion rings were also pretty good (still not touching Tony's Cafe or Maryland Avenue Sub Shop) and our waiter was attentive and the food came out quickly. No, if you're visiting the area and want Delaware cuisine, of course don't go to Applebee's (why are you picking a chain when searching for local food anyway), but if you are looking for a cheap place for lunch with co-workers, Applebee's is perfect.

If you are into a normal busy/crowded sports bar, this is the place for you.

A simple menu with decent options of drinks, and with friendly staff.

The owner is rude (who tells their clients that they have to feed their kids from the food bank because customers don't tip enough?) Her skills are from the 1980's. For the prices that are charged it's a complete crime.

Small place inside the San Augustine market with a small basic menu. They had seasonal lattes such as a Mole latte and a few others however none of them sounded delicious to me so I decided to take the basic girl route and order a vanilla latte. The latte was very good but not as sweet as I like my coffee. 
I did like that the coffee was smooth and very delicious but had it been a bit sweet with better sounding flavor options, I would have given it 5 stars. Also my latte cost $5 and it was a small size. They didn't offer a 20 ounce.
Normally have great service, however felt belittled by Brandon at the front when coming in and didn't feel comfortable after this occurred.

We wanted to try out Bully's tonight, Google had good reviews. Decided to do take out and not cook it being so hot today. I got the Fish Basket (fish n chips) and the fish was obviously cheap frozen stuff. It was shaped like a diamond and deep fried to where the beer batter crust was hard. It was 1/4 inch thin. No slaw or lemon wedge which was weird. Just fries and fish. Fries were ok, tarter sauce was cheap. Not worth the money at all. Was so disappointed. The staff was very nice. Tried to order mashed potatoes and gravy, but it wasn't on their new system. Felt bad for staff trying to figure out the new system. Wont return based solely on the quality of the food.

Didn't think fries and soup could count for a lunch but i am stuffed. Chili was better than the veggie soup just because of the uniqueness of vegan chili. Both the sweet potato and russet fries were seasoned enough I like them better alone than with the sauce. Tried aztec ketchup, pineapple chili pepper sauce and chipotle mayo. All 3 were ok, but I really like the two flavored salts - onion on the russet and bourbon sugar for the sweet potatoes. Make a honey based sauce for the sweet potatoes and i'd be in heaven. I'll be back for sure. Also like that they compost.
Excellent food. I love the homemade rolls, the crab cakes and the avocado crab fritter. We had a large party upstairs and they accommodated us nicely.

I am giving the Hyatt Regency St Louis a one star due to their lack of regard and safety for Covid-19 precautions.  Their website talks of their commitment to following Covid procedures.  That is not at all accurate for this location.  

Check-in with valet and the front desk was easy and non eventful.  The front desk had stickers on the floor to keep guests 6 feet apart while waiting.

While walking from valet to the front desk I did notice two people not wearing masks and I wondered why they weren't being told to cover up.  

About an hour after check-in I went back to the lobby to wait for my pizza delivery.  While waiting, I counted TEN people, in different groups, not wearing masks inside the lobby of the Hyatt.  Not one employee told them to wear put on a mask.  I asked a g
front desk agent (you can't miss this guy, he is about 6'4" and at least 260lbs) if the Hyatt isn't requiring masks.  He told me they have to wear them at the front desk.  I asked him if that was the only place they had to be worn and he repeated his statement and shrugged his shoulders.  But wait - it gets worse.  As I was walking away, he said to the guest next to me, "It's Friday night!", waited a few beats then repeated it loudly enough for everyone to hear him, "It's Friday night!".  It was to insinuate that the crazy's come out on Friday night and I was that crazy person.  I asked a legitimate question in a respectful way.  He must not have liked that I was trying to get clarification on Hyatt's mask policy.  This front desk agent humiliated me.  As a former front desk agent who has worked at two different 4star hotels, I was floored by his response to me because he was so disrespectful, unprofessional and felt very comfortable deliberately mocking a guest loudly enough for the entire front desk area to hear.

I am traveling across country with my son and we chose not to fly due to Covid.  I researched online as to what I thought would be our best option for a hotel stay during a pandemic.  Clearly I made a mistake as the Hyatt does not take this seriously and fails to follow simple precautions for the health and safety of their guests.  

The Hyatt Regency St. Louis is a failure on so many levels.

This brewery and bar have been a fantastic addition to the neighborhood. The beer is great and the prices are even better. The brewery has a few light snacks on their menu (soft pretzels, etc) but there is typically a rotating food truck that pulls into the historic warehouse space on weekends. The interior feels very welcoming and is large enough for big groups. Plus gender neutral bathrooms!

Catering to those in the neighborhood without vehicles or those who don't have the energy or wherewithal to go elsewhere. 

This is a facility for bill payments, payday advances, check cashing & other things of that sort. 

I got a money order for a friend & was outraged at the fees for other services. The percentages on repayment of payday loans... Can you say #loansharking??? Sheesh!!!

Ample parking as it's shared with other retail facilities in the strip mall.

Food is great, but we ordered online and didn't get an email confirmation. But checked our account and the money came out. An hour later we call and they never received our order, and apparently only one person can refund so we have to wait two days to get a call about a refund, and since the people who work there can't see that we paid they can't just put our order in while we are on the phone with them. Not to mention they said this has happened before, so why not fix the problem! 
Don't order online!!

This place doesn't deserve a rating but I give it one star only because I have to.  We were not acknowledged when we arrived and conceded to wait 30 minutes for a table.  We were finally seated and were not waited on for ten minutes.  I had to find someone to see if they were willing to take our order!  The waitress that eventually came to our table was inconvenienced by having to take our order!  We are the customers, Miss!  We waited for atleast 20 minutes after placing our order and still nobody came to check on us until a waitress said our food would be out in 16 minutes!  We thankfully left and will never come back again.  The sad thing is that they said they were so busy but there were many open tables.  Avoid this place at all costs unless you want to be frustrated and thoroughly disappointed!

I ordered delivery on a Sunday night.  I decided to try the Pad Thai with chicken and fried calamari.  Delivery was very quick and easy.  I had the food in less than 30 minutes after ordering.  But, I was given a $3 delivery charge, even though I was in a supposed free zone.

The food was very mediocre overall.  The fried calamari was not good.  They looked like the frozen onion rings from Burger King, and were chewy and tasteless.  The dipping sauce helped, but it tasted like canned sweet and sour sauce.

I was really craving pad thai, and after looking places up, I decided to give this place a try (it's in the name right?).  I asked for it a bit spicier, and they nicely obliged.  But the dish itself just did not have much flavor.  The peanuts were too hidden and everything was just bland.

There are too many great asian restaurants in Philly to come here again.

Shame on Ikes coffee re the man ripped off from the $20 bill. Everyone knows if the cashier doesnt place the bill on the cash register until giving the customer his change they automatically must take the customets word for it!

Poor customer service I have complained multiple times over a 4 month period, and my problems have not been addressed. To quote a Discover Card ad "Some companies just don't appreciate the power of conversation." One time they even told me I can't guarantee anyone will get this. Three times later, the Manager on duty said "I have not heard of this". Rather than being a good manager, he was very threatening, escalatory, and proceeded to say he was the only manager of the store, there was no one above him. Turns out there was both an equal Co-Manager on Duty, and the he was not the store manager, but rather just the manager on duty.

Went there for the first time today because I really wanted a "Wine More, Bark Less" t-shirt that I saw in the window... so they really know how to window dress! Walked in and wished we'd brought our dog... the bakery counter looks awesome, but I didn't pay attention to whether they had grain free options. I did, however, notice that they have a lot of made in the USA pigs' ear treats e.t.c, AND Kong toys (could not leave without getting our 4 legged girl one of those)! I will agree with the one yelper regarding the service.... I tried to engage the server in a quick conversation in the empty shop ("I saw this shirt and had to have it because my dog is always barking"), but she was having none of it, which was a first for me in Indy.

What a nightmare, I would give less than 1 star if I could. We booked a block of rooms for our wedding recently at this location and they made it our whole experience stressful from day one. The sales manager we worked with seemed completely incompetent and had extremely poor communication skills from day one. They had only one working elevator which I should say was semi-working since one of our wedding party got stuck at one point. In our room our sink was clogged, the room was gross and the vents looked like they were not cleaned in some time. Another guest did not have a working toilet. The upper floors had a strong mildew smell. We also wanted to pay for breakfast for our guest the next morning after the wedding. The front desk was supposed to hand out vouchers to our guest but tried to make us do it. When it came time to pay for the breakfast they lost the vouchers our guest handed in (server left with them) so they elected to make up a number to charge us which was much higher than our guest count. So it took them ~2 hours the day of checkout to get this sorted out. Long story short, I am surprised this place is in business. Save yourself some time and look elsewhere. If it wasn't for this place, our wedding would have been perfect.

Cindy's is my 2nd favorite nail salon in New Orleans. I love the neighborhood/location - lots of street parking available. The shop is larger than most I've been to - very clean. The ladies offered me a beverage - a glass of wine was a nice touch! :)

We Will not be returning. So we made reservations and we were late getting there due to the very limited parking. Then we sat down and checked out the menu. Listen, if it's good food and good portions, I don't mind spending a little more money every once in a while.  Now this place was way over priced for the portions that we were given. We spent $158.00 on two meals, two very small alcoholic beverages (20)and an appetizer with 4 shrimp cocktail and 3 shrimp sausage balls($22). One of the meals was a scallop meal. It tasted good but for 32.00 I got 3 fancy scallops dressed in a tomato & cheese sauce. My husband had a fish dish ($34) I tried it but didn't like it too well. Sort of made me wonder if that's what dirt tasted like. They did a good job plating the food to look fancy but I could spend less and go to Fogo De Chao and had better food.  Then there was the forced kitchen  gratuity on top of the high priced meal.  However, what really did it for me was the bathroom. They had one bathroom with multiple stalls... however it was for men and women to share. Glad we didn't bring our children. Listen, I understand that there are people who are transgender but there are a lot more people who aren't.  It's not safe to mix both genders in a bathroom.  Especially one with a bar! Seriously, use your heads people. I'm just completely sad and disgusted by the bathroom situation. 

Update::
Thank you for the reply. No I was not aware of any other restroom, which is why I was irritated. No I don't feel like I would be attacked specifically by a transgender person. Just really for general safety, not just me specifically but anyone. Whether the person is a male, female or transgender or if they choose to be an elephant.. just specifically it's unsafe to mix the two genders together. I'm glad to know that there isn't only an all gender bathroom. Thank you for sharing that there's male & female bathrooms.  As far as parking goes, we weren't sure if there were specific parking rules or not, which was why we decided to wait till one was open in the parking lot. I still feel like it was still pretty over priced though.
They did a wonderful job! Very clean and still following many COVID protocols. Will definitely be back and would recommend to my friend!

Some of the best wings you'll find in the city. They're smoked and flavorful and fall off the bone when made right. The Wake N Bake burger is another favorite. Ham, cheese, tater tots, bacon and an egg makes this burger live up to its name. They always have good beer on draft. The Dirty Tots are wonderful and so are the Beer Cheese fries.

I shopped here for Halloween less than two months ago. I was greeted well and it seemed like a nice enough store. At checkout, I asked what their return policy was and they said it was store credit and I was fine with that. They did not mention a 7-day limit and when I looked at the receipt I didn't see anything about that. I ended up not using any of these clothes so they just sat in the bag as I knew I'd return it one day.

When I decided to return this morning, I saw the 7-day words on the receipt. Had I known or had this been mentioned to me I would have prioritized coming back since I didn't use these clothes at all. I decided to go in anyway and explain everything.

When I came in, a woman was ready to help me. She had to get a second woman to help do the return. This second woman had no customer service knack at all. After I talked, she immediately and blanketly said it's clearly stated on the receipt and also that these policies were posted on the wall (a sign with a bunch of small text that I didn't see, wasn't made aware of when I first came in and certainly I don't see customers taking the time to digest when your goal is to shop). Was she also not listening to what I said? I said I didn't see it the first time and so it's been in the bag the whole time and that I didn't see it until this morning when I looked at it again.

I'm not saying I deserve a return. I also understand having a consistent policy for all customers. This was my first time shopping and it wasn't communicated clearly there was a 7-day window. The way this second employee responded it was also clear she was impatiently waiting for me to finish because I could tell she wasn't listening to me so she could respond as soon as possible her robotic response of the longly worded sign high above eye level and the receipt (which I already acknowledged I missed the first time). I came in knowing I missed out on some things but was met with  stone cold nothingness.

Ok, I just read this other 1-star review on this site. I don't know if the person I interacted with was Dinette, but I wish I confirmed now (this person had longer dark hair). The "demeaning" and "insulting" has some resonance and the pointing to the receipt as proof of her righteousness definitely feels familiar. Either way, I agree the customer service is unacceptable, and the return policy needs to be communicated more clearly. We're all living in a difficult time and everyone needs more empathy.

Great byob that's on the smaller side (what you see from the window is what you get), with some great dishes, that you can turn into a great next day leftover by ordering a side of glass noodles or extra rice.  Waitstaff is very friendly and helpful.

Food was really good, service is dismal. A jillion wait staff running around but nobody knows what they are doing. Wrong appetizers, double delivery of appetizers, bread not delivered until late in the main dish course, plates set down in front of the wrong diner. Waiter was visibly irritated  by our chatty group.  Small issues but there was an issue or a mistake with EVERY interaction. Lovely decor, great food lousy service.
Delicious fresh burgers with beautiful lettuce and accoutrements. Vanilla shakes & fries were also good. I plan on returning.

I had the rocktoberfest and the nitro cherry lime sour. I enjoyed them both. We had fries and burgers from the kitchen. The veggie burger was house made and delicious. My husband enjoyed his burger too but the highlight really for us were the skinny fries that stayed crispy until the last fry was gone. There is plenty of rooms for large groups. The service was great and I will certainly come back and try their other beers. 

They don't require tips and pay their staff a living wage. Any tips you give are given to charities. How cool is that!

Had good experiences with my computer at your store in the past. This time brought my older MacBook Pro in to be diagnosed for a screen problem, I ok'd the diagnostic fee ($45). When I came to get it they added on labor charges to diagnose even though I had not authorized any work to be done. Rather than $45 it was now $75. Interesting policy, easy way to get money and lose customers.

Our first meal in Edmonton couldn't have been better. Lovely, well-appointed space sets the scene for a wonderful meal. Started with the charred cauliflower, which had us speechless. Very, very good. I went with the short rib tortelloni and it was perfect, rich with flavor. My girlfriend was in love with the gnocchi. Pudding for dessert was a delightful capper to the meal.

Clean place with helpful staff who really know what they're doing relating to all things hair and makeup. However, I heard one employee loudly ranting about how she was "never going to cut [person]'s hair again because she made [me] look bad!"  Her sentiment is understandable, but don't say that in a place where other customers will hear you! She wasn't in the back or anything - she was in the middle of the store saying this for everyone to hear. It was very uncomfortable, and given some other reviewers saying "X refused to do my hair/eyebrows after I gave her feedback," I felt like I was treading on eggshells.

As for my actual eyebrow wax, it was okay. I noticed the stylist NEVER double dipped, and she used clean sticks for every wax. She shaped well according to what I asked for, but when I got into the unflattering light of my car, I noticed she had missed large clumps of dark hairs. I don't recall her waxing those crucial places, but didn't say anything during the wax since I assumed there wasn't enough hair there to wax- wrong! She also did not clean up with tweezers as much as she should have, so I had to do that myself. For a $25 wax, I was really not pleased. Once I cleaned up myself, though, the shape and form she did looked really nice. I am also pleased with whatever moisturizers and lotions she used afterwards, because I did not have much redness and did not break out.
Brought my 3 yr old daughter for her first pedicure. Service was great, clean and friendly! We will definitely be back!
This is some of the best ice cream I've ever eaten.  Always has been... and I hope it always remains!

This is by far the best sushi place in the temple terrace/ new tampa area. I used to work here and I would eat it everyday. It is still one of the only places I will eat sushi because it is just that good!

I am not completely and totally sold on this place yet. I went in and told the place I'd like a pedi and nail fill and they did quickly seat me. They didn't ask which pedicure I wanted, so they did their own thing, which was actually fine but had I wanted something different and was preoccupied or something, (sometimes I'm making appointments on my phone as I get my toes done), I would've been upset. They did a good job with them, but my right big toenail broke in 3 days, and that was with gel polish on. So, I was a little upset about that. 
Then, moving onto the nails. They could tell I was wearing pink & white so they had the products used for that, but didn't ask me what shade of pink I wanted, didn't ask me if I wanted my nails cut down, and they shaped them how they wanted them. I had to speak up and tell them to cut them down and shape them the way I wanted and he didn't seem too excited about a customer telling him what they wanted. :-/ the guy was gentle, and did a good job which is always good in my book. I am going back and I will do another update when I do.

 Update:: I went back today (previous review was from Oct 2021). The owner (I guess he's the owner since he does all the calls), was super friendly and in a great mood. I walked in and told him I wanted a pedi and my pink and white nails to be switched to gel polish. He didn't have any problems with it at all. So, I had my pedi done and the girl who did them was very quiet and didn't speak a word...that's fine. I don't mind a quiet person because I'm one who actually doesn't talk much (believe it!) she did good but I assume I either didn't have any ingrown nails or she didn't dig them out - one or the other..:but she was gentle and it was putting me to sleep lol. 

Onto the nails. The girl was ok...not the best but also not the worst.  She did good about not hurting me, she asked me if I wanted square nails and I said yes but they're square rounded. I don't like that. She tried to haggle me into getting dip power, and I don't like dip powder and at first she wasn't taking no for an answer, but she might've picked up on my annoyance and stopped. She didn't say much after that. I love the color, and I love gel polish and I think that's where I'm going to stop from how on. The other stuff isn't for me. 

All in all, I will stick at 3 stars.

I was looking forward to trying this place, I hear things from my fellow West-siders about this being a place they frequent. I was not blown away...

First, LOOK AT ALL THE COLORS!!!! This place is sooo brightly colored and the lights are sooo bright, I kinda love it. Anywho, this place was packed when we came on a Thursday night (good sign). Seated promptly & chips and salsa were brought quick by the chips guy, yay! These were good, not my favorite ever but good. Service took a while to get drinks ordered but was attentive from there. Not super friendly, but I could also tell he was quite busy.

We ordered the small cheese dip to go along with our chips and salsa because I was craving a good cheese dip...this was not a good cheese dip, I was so sad. It was ok and overpriced at over $3 for a small bowl of cheese (see pic).

I ordered a chicken dish and my husband got some type of burrito. He liked his alright but wasn't raving about it. Flavor was decent for my chicken dish but it was a bit dry. Guac was tasty and helped with that. We both enjoyed our meals but were not super impressed. 

I would definitely give this place another chance to try out their drinks and something else from their menu, hope to be wow-ed.

The food was overall good but not great.  The hot fried chicken sandwich was great.  The hot chicken and waffles was ok, but they put syrup on the waffles which made them soggy, and the breast was not battered very well.  I liked my scallop dish, and I like the concept of crab rice, but the rice was a little hard in places.  The peach cobbler for dessert was terrific.  
This place obviously has a following.  It was packed on a Sunday afternoon.  I would recommend a visit if you've never been here.

3 stars for the Tap...what?

I have fond memories of this place. On New Year's Eve eve, 2004, we had an informal, impromptu rehearsal dinner here, and every time I walk to the back of the second floor and take the one step up, I recall my fiance sitting there crying, freaked out by emotional overload. So on sentimental value alone, this place is a 4.

But I'm not reviewing memories, I'm reviewing the overall experience, with a focus on my dinner there last Saturday night. The Tap is loud and crowded, in a way that lets you know people are there for the same reasons you are, and enjoying it. They have a solid beer list and a solider menu. You can debate why Phillymag put them in the top tier of Philly restaurants (a nod to frequent advertisers?...nahhhh), but Standard Tap has found its niche and just carved it deeper and better. They expanded upstairs and built a fair-weather roof deck. They'll take your phone number and call you when your table is ready. This was handy, as we escaped the noise and fled down 2nd to the 700 Club when they told us we had a 40 minute wait. 

Our party of 5 got a great booth at the very back of the second floor, which alleviated the crowd and noise sensation elsewhere - the front room was so far beyond relaxing, I'm glad we waited as long as we did. the waiter was attentive and brought our drinks quickly, and was a good sport about our fickle ordering. 

We weren't super hungry, so we split an appetizer of grilled octopus. This was some thick, beefy tentacle, and some of the best I've ever had. Grilled octopus is a lot like chicken - if cooked well it's got a tender, meaty consistency, and will taste like whatever you marinate it in. And oh man, the marinade was like a summer BBQ. It was a sizable portion, with little cherry tomatoes and olives as garnish, and we destroyed it. I can't recommend this dish enough. 

For dinner our table ordered two Standard burgers, a pork sandwich, chicken pie and mussels & sausage. The first three items arrived at the same time, and we waited for the rest. The chicken pie arrived next, and looked pretty fantastic - it's a free-standing pot pie, i.e. no pot. And then we waited for the Mussels. And waited. And waited. The server came back to check on our drinks and seemed a little surprised that one dish was missing. Quick on the draw, he said that that was on its way, but another 5+ minutes of waiting signaled that it was totally forgotten. When it did arrive, we were pretty bummed and most of our food was going cold, and asked to have it taken off the bill. Good thing, too, because it was overspiced to the point of inedible by all but the most hot-sauce crazed diners. When we complained further, the server said that the poblano peppers can really heat it up, but they didn't call this 'three alarm mussels', so it seemed like BS to write the heat off as normal. I tasted it and it was shit. And I love mussels, sausage AND poblano peppers. The burger was good, and the pork sandwich was plentiful, though the cheese had congealed during the wait and became a negative.

When we left, they did knock the lost dish off the bill, but it just felt awkward, like we wanted to get away from them and they were probably happy to see us leave. I'm hoping my next trip is better.

We came here on halloween night at 8pm and it was great because there was nobody there except a few people so it felt like we had the place to ourselves and it was quiet.

The ambiance was great as it felt like we were in a europe type cottage with the soft french style music playing over the speakers. 

The hostess and waitress was very nice as well as the cook. The food was really good. The sauce in the French Pot Roast was delicious. The meat was cooked cooked vey tender. The Corn Chowder Soup was fantastic and the seasonal Pumpkin Pancakes were very good as well. 

Everything was very enjoyable and I am looking forward to returning and trying some other items. This establishment was way better then the one in Sacramento.

We came here in the middle of visiting the WWII museum (which was great, by the way). The people here were so kind and gracious, and the food was AMAZING. We got the mufaletta and boudin. The boudin was a new dish to me, and while the texture took a bit getting used to, I loved it after a couple of bites. It's great with the crunchy pickles and mustard! And even more delicious with the sweet potato hot sauce. The mufaletta sandwich was also super delicious. At first, I was a bit apprehensive about the sandwich, because I paid so much and it came on a hamburger bun? Rest assured, this was no hamburger bun. The bread was delicious and toasted perfectly so each bite into the sandwich had a resolute crunch to it. I would highly recommend this place - I can't wait to come here again!
Best Chinese food in all of St. Louis. Great for take out or dine in. Our favorites are the pork fried rice, wan fu garlic beef, and general tsing chicken. You can taste the quality!
Unless you're a hipster plugged into a laptop, I wouldn't bother. Coffee was not bad. Bread pudding was incredibly dry and somewhat bland. As my friend said, an "Epic(ally dull)" experience.

Love Dr Roberts and staff  highly recommend!  Easy and very affordable .   I have many friends who feel the same. The staff and Dr Roberts are friendly and very professional !   Very impressed with how easy the plan is.
Saw the prices and it freaked me out , kind of pricey but you get what you pay for, quality Mexican food , quality carne asada ! Will definitely be back on my next trip to Santa Barbara !!!

Wow, what an incredible and historic spot.  Rather than just being a venue to watch a music show, this is actually an experience!  We were here for about two hours and saw an incredible show, which showcased different kinds of country music, great presenters and even square dancing.  The place is huge and had the most incredible sound system...all music came out crystal clear!

This is such a unique and amazing experience and I recommend everyone to visit if you can...not a disappointment!
A great sports bar with excellent food. The hermanaki wings are our favorite . Pizza is great also!

This is one of the most disappointing meals I've had in Nashville to date.The server was an asshole. Told us that the chef was too "swamped" to be bothered to ask him if he could cook some eggs on the side of our breakfast order and at that, they would be scrambled, not how we requested them-which when you're paying $24 for an entree, I think it's fair to get eggs how you ask for them. Also, if you're overwhelmed as a chef, probably pick a different career...
The waiter then proceeded to mock us for being high maintenance for asking for eggs on the side and could not read the room that we were offended by his behavior. On top of this, It took me 30 min to get a Bloody Mary and a good 10 minutes before this terrible waiter even greeted us at our table. Do not waste your time with this pretentious over priced excuse for a restaurant. Definitely ruined our Easter brunch experience that our family paid through the nose for.

In a city where many restaurants serve po boys, this is the most famous.  It's also small, crowded, loud, overpriced, and mediocre.  The seafood in the sandwiches is over-breaded, the rolls are not particularly good or fresh, and there is no table service.  And they only accept cash.  Yes, it's an experience, but one you can easily avoid.

This company is so good, they compelled me to write my very first yelp review!

I cannot think of a single bad thing to say about this tour. Everyone was friendly, knowledgeable, and even extremely accomodating to us when we couldn't keep our original tour date.

My girlfriends and I were in NOLA for a bachelorette weekend and decided to do this tour on our first day here. Unfortunately, the bride started feeling faint within a few minutes of getting on the bikes and couldn't continue. Rudy, the tourguide, had called the manager Ford to come pick us up and escort us back to the bike office. Without even asking, Ford didn't even hestitate to let us switch our tour to that Sunday, how nice! Not only did they completely accomodate us, Ford also spend about half an hour giving us a complete rundown (map included!) of all of his favorite places in New Orleans we could go instead. We checked a few of them out on our trip, and they didn't disappoint! 

When we came back Sunday, Ford was super friendly and asked how my friend was feeling, while Rudy (the tourguide) gathered the rest of the group. Rudy too was very kind and make sure everyone was taken care of. The tour lasted about 2.5 hours, and you could tell Rudy was very knowledgeable and geniunly loved sharing his passion for New Orleans with the riders. 

Overall, just superb.

Approximately 15 minutes after being seated, we still had  not been approached by a server. Upon leaving, a server stated that she didn't see us there. She had to have passed us at least twice. It is her responsibility to be aware of her tables and their needs.

I had a relaxing time with my family. We didn't realize until we got there, that when we went to the same hotel 8 years ago around it was at the same time in  Fiesta time. It brought back great memories. I was pregnant when I was there 8 years ago so it was great being at the same place in time with out 7 year old. The lobby wait was great.. I had wine and had quick service. Beautiful room, room service, had fun on the roof in the pool. Every person that works there made us feel very welcome. We walked at our corner street State to walk around and enjoy the fiesta vibe. The valet guys were very polite. Will be coming back for sure. The only small thing is maybe have more toilet paper in the bathroom, there was only one roll. But I still love you guys. Lol

JJ's is awesome. From the outside, it's rather confusing as to what is within, but after browsing through the shelves of international chocolates, snacks, and beer, you stumble into the coffee shop area where they offer tea, specialty "house" coffee drinks, and the standard java options. 

Sure, the furniture is beaten up to the point of almost falling apart, but there's something  warm and homey about it. And I love the tall ceilings and open windows that let in the sun. I've stopped in with a group of friends and had game nights here, it's a great space to relax, study, conduct a business meeting, or catch up with a group of friends. One of Nashville's greatest treasures! 

My only complaint is they are a bit slowish with making your drinks, so stop in if you are looking for a leisurely visit!

The last 4 times I've been here 3 times they haven't cut the Quesadillas!!!
Like who doesn't cut the quesadillas? With that said super oily. My quesadilla was immersed in oil and soggy. That's just gross!
Met up with friends for lunch which some of them haven't been there and they loved it. Food was delish like always. I had a chicken pita with homemade lentil soup which was delicious.

Food was good. Ordered some pizza and flatbread and chips and salsa. 
Service - could be better. The girl at the desk could've lightened up the mood a hit but it seemed like she couldn't wait to get off work and go home.

Very unsafe store - I asked an employee, Pauline or Paulina was her name, why she was wearing her mask around her chin leaving her mouth and nose completely exposed.  She said "I need to breathe".  I asked her if it was store policy that she be in close proximity to customers without properly wearing a mask.  She told me "don't worry about it".
I saw other store employees and customers wearing masks over their mouths only with their noses completely exposed.  In the middle of a pandemic, this is wholly irresponsible and unacceptable.
I will NEVER step foot in this store again and suggest that anyone concerned about their health and safety also avoid this location at all costs.
The food here is good. The hot wings are a must. The calamari the best on the mainline and good chicken dishes. Good for all ages and a nice childrens menu

Beautiful beach, very cleans and full of food vibes. The sand is soft and white and the water is warm and clear. There are tons of restaurants to eat at nearby and also great hotels with amazing views.

I am amending my review. We had a bad experience in service recently (just service, food was delicious as always). Within the same day of posting the review, the manager contacted me, both through phone and email to follow up. He listened to the concerns and certainly maintained our business as the level of customer service the manager alone showed in response to our issues was above what you see these days.

I am not normally a fan of chicken on nachos, but the way they marinate the chicken is delicious, so definently recommend the chicken nachos (side note, you'll need to share, they are huge!) And the pot stickers are great appetizers. You can't leave without fulfilling that sweet tooth craving with the captain jacks. We will often go just for this!

The bar in the evening gets three stars, the coffee gets one star (I tried both an utterly undrinkable cup of drip...pause...cup of drip is a good way to describe it *and* and barely drinkable Americano. If they can't even get an Americano right, there's a problem), service gets three and a half stars, decor gets four stars. It all sort of evens out to three. Just avoid that coffee!

Let it be known that I didn't eat anything in the restaurant.

Three words.  SHRIMP AND GRITS.  Do it.  

This was by far, the best shrimp and grits I have ever had.  The shrimp are large and wrapped in bacon, and who doesn't like anything wrapped in bacon?!  The grits are amazing.  The service was so warm and welcoming, our server even snuck me extra grits.  While this was our most causal dinner we had in New Orleans, it still ranks among one of my favorites.

This place has become my SO and I's favorite breakfast spot in Saint Louis. The breakfast burritos are gigantic and sooo tasty (try them "Christmas style" with red and green chili!). The coffee is great and so is the service. 

Expect a wait so make sure you check in beforehand and poke your head into the little bus on the side of the building so you can sit down get some coffee to sip on while you wait.

I didn't have the pizza here, though they did look pretty good. Instead, we got the cast iron wings, which I highly recommend! The wings were so tasty and delicious. They were baked with caramelized onions. Best wings I've had in a while! 

This restaurant is right next to the Wilmington Brew Works. 

Plenty of parking.
David was an amazing server. He was very funny and completely on top of making our meal an enjoyable experience.
Good food, and a good atmosphere. Came here for my dad's birthday and he really enjoyed it. Also had a great beer selection!
A great little breakfast joint. Prices are reasonable and the service is fast & friendly.

Stopped here based on reviews. Food was delicious and came out quick. Prices are 1-2 dollars higher in the restaurant then online on most items. Restaurant lacks atmosphere... reminded me of a cafeteria... i wouldn't go here on a date but a quick in and out is a great hole in the wall to stop into for some yummy food.

Every time I come to TJ Wings, I am greeted with a smile and leave with a full belly! I have tried many good items over the year and I have never left hungry or disappointed! For a small owner to run this bar and have such a successful staff is outstanding! They have the best chicken salad club in stl! Wings are phenomenal! Burgers and sandwiches are wonderful and the atmosphere makes you feel right at home! Long love for TJ Wings!
A big thank you to Lily's Flowers for making my friend's birthday bright! The arrangement created was even more beautiful than depicted online. I couldn't be more pleased with their service. A++

The BEST FRIED CHICKEN!!! hands down like seriously. We did the buffet which was around $25 pp. Not sure if that is the normal but it was during Essence Fest, so that could have played the part in the price. Either way I would seriously pay that $25 everytime im in nawlins just to get some of that great soul food. I'm telling you don't pass it up. Your mouth will thank me later ;-)

Came here because we had a 10% off coupon. Arrived to find the place practically empty.  Ordered off the lunch menu.  Got the steak and shrimp along with some sushi.  I won't say it was bad, but I've had a lot better. I would look for another establishment unless this was the only choice.
Love this farmers market. Fruit and veggies are always large and much cheaper than the grocery store plus the strawberry milkshakes are delicious!

We knew we were in trouble when they asked if we would like to "opt out" of maid service. This hotel casino has finally hit rock bottom. From the Hash House to the ratty carpeting, there seems to be no effort put into upgrading the product.  
Time to start shopping for a new hotel when in Reno.

The store's customer service is very poor there was a line of about 6 to 7 people when I arrived I received my order sat at my table then only thing I have from there for view was but they were backed up and the butts were in my face and on my table I approached the manager ask him why do they only have one cashier and she said but we have one running orders but I said yes ma'am but what the about the line and she didn't seem to give a crap there you have it in and enter at your own risk

This has been my go to place for over 40 years, but with the recent change in ownership it has really gone down hill fast.  I have frequented El Cap almost once a month since forever, but the last three visits were extremely disappointing and will probably not go back.  Such a shame as this place used to be a local landmark.

Went on weekend around 3:30pm. They told us the wait for a table for two (inside or out) was going to be 45 minutes. Form the other reviews, it looks like this is a standard response from the hostess girls? The good news was that it wound up taking about 30 minutes to get our table. Somewhat acceptable for the time and day. But for two people?

The olive hummus spread was really good. It came with tasty pita bread slices and lemon slices.  But the perogies were just ok. They came with a small sausage button on top of the perogie. And it came with sour cream and some type of curry sauce. The curry sauce wasn't that good and didn't go well with the perogies at all.

I ordered the Mojo chicken and it was absolutely horrible. It tasted like they boiled a frozen chicken in tap water and then plopped it on the bun; then added lettuce and tomatoes. I didn't taste any mojo or seasoning at all. It was totally bland and tasteless. 

Guinness Burger was nothing to write home about as well. Average burger meat with just a lot of stuff jammed under the bun. Like eating a bunch of mush and left you not wanting more.

Didn't go inside the restaurant but the ambience outside was decent - somewhat near a park and the water.

Overall a decent place but they really need to liven up their menu and make tastier food. Pricing was not high but not low either. Don't be fooled by the catchy / swanky name - this place is just about average.

A wonderfully chill and tasty place to celebrate a birthday, etc. I'm typically not a huge fan of Mediterranean food, but every thing we offered was delicious. The "king of kings" humus and chicken meatball were amazing! Also, I'm a fan of egg salad, and this was the best I've ever had. 

*Only downside: They were not super attentive to keeping drinks full and plates from piling up. Maybe it's because we were on the patio or because it was super busy for a Monday night.

We stopped in on a busy Saturday evening. We did not have reservations but the host was happy to accommodate my sons and I. I have a fairly picky eater and one that is not so picky but is somewhat of a food critic in his own right. The meatballs and bruschetta were fantastic! The pizzas or even better. We got a Bambino and a pepperoni and they were delicious.

Tried this place for the first time today,  ordered Mongolian beef and it was salty beyond belief. Beef looks old too...Maybe it was because there wasn't a single diner there other than me. 

First and last time there.

Food was very good.  Maybe an off night but the waitress really messed up our orders.   The did comp a meal which was appreciated.  Timing was off as well.  Waitress was apologetic. Possible they are dealing with short staff like a lot of restaurants are.  Prices are as expected for a high end steakhouse.  Don't know why the cut up the tomahawk ribeye though.  Thought that was part of the presentation when ordering this cut.

This little restaurant is quite the Hyde Park Gem.

Definitely one I'd recommend for more of a special occasion than a casual, last minute where should we eat situation.  Reservations are strongly recommended, as the dining room has limited seating. They did have a small bar top area, which I assume is first come, first serve.

Their menu offers two options. A la carte or if your party can collectively vote YES! a 4 course option.

Our group unanimously agreed on the 4 course option. I chose: Beet & Quinoa Salad, Pork Belly App, Wagu Steak & Chocolate Cake.  There wasn't one thing I chose, I wouldn't consider ordering again. For $50 per person, I think it was the way to go.

Everything was presented beautifully and tasted very good. 

Our server was very attentive,  knowledgeable about the menu and friendly. 

Ambiance is reminiscent of a speakeasy, in my opinion. From the outside of the building you'd never guess what you would find on the inside.  Booth seating is very private.

Not a great place for a large group, unless you rented the whole restaurant.

First coffee stop in New Orleans and this place is amazing and friendly! Fresh coffee and pastries but also breakfast items as well. Decor is beautiful with outside seating to enjoy the view and people.

I went into this store after reading other reviews on Yelp. Unfortunately, Judy sold me a table for $125, but upon charging my card and printing the receipt, Amy walked over and changed her mind and requested that I pay $375 instead. I could not, but left me phone number so they could call if they ever got anything similar in stock. 

Instead Amy and the store's former owner Jane both used my phone number to harass me after I posted about my experience on another online forum. Amy cursed at me immediately after calling my number, calling me f***ing d**. I will never spend money at a place that treats their customers this way. 

Also, this place was not observing any masking protocol for covid.

Great SoBro Brunch spot!  The presentation is picture worthy and the taste is fresh.  There's definitely a variety to choose from on the menu.  The orange juice is a delicious fresh squeezed glass of goodness.  The display case of baked treats is irresistible from the hummingbird cake to the magic bars to the cheesecake.  Seeing they are open now on Wednesday and Thursday for dinner, I will make a point to return to try it out.

Salvo's was a nice treat for a group of us that don't make it to the West Bank very often. Several of us tried and were fans of the ribs, though the wet ribs definitely went over better than the spicier dry ribs. The sandwiches were quite good, and all of the employees were super friendly making our entire party feel right at home.  As Patty J. mentioned, the prices are indeed quite good.

I'm a New Orleans native, and I used to dine here religiously before I relocated after Katrina.

First off don't be frightened off by the exterior, it does LOOK like a dump on the outside.
Also long waits are very common, thus explaining the crowds of people you usually see hanging outside.

Its so worth it though. They have the best local food selection I've ever seen.
Simply put..........GO THERE

Dopo 4 anni sono ritornato qui e l'accoglienza è sempre la stessa.
Camere molto carine ed intime (sono 10).
Pulizia ottima.
Alcune hanno anche una piccola cucina.
Spazi comuni sempre ben curati.
Servizi top: biciclette, giochi da spiaggia, sedie... c'è di tutto ed è free.
Vicino a State St. ha cmq attorno locali dove poter fare colazione, cenare e pranzare.
Una certezza.

My wife is diabetic and it's hard to find sugar free so when we try this place the cheese cake was very good. We live in Philadelphia drove all the way to berlin farmer's market for the cheese cake. Only to find out they had no sugar free and we were not happy at all, we got there at 10:30 Sunday morning the hole place is open for business but the house of cheese cake they open at 12:30 so we waited 2 hours to find out we could not get what we wanted. Real good customer service we still got cheese cake but not sugar free. You knew you were out then some should of been brought some in sunday afternoon when you came in.

Just got off the phone with a rude employee with absolutely no customer service. Wish I got her name but I didn't. Here's the story of what just happened, and yes I'm one of those people whose biggest pet peeve is bad customer service, especially for a business that is supposed to be service-oriented.

I wanted to book a couple's massage for my husband's birthday. They were supposed to be open at 9am, so I called a couple of times around opening time (9:02am-9:03am) but nobody answered. I thought that since it was still near opening time, maybe they hadn't settled in, so I gave it some time and called again ten minutes later at 9:13am. Each time, the call would ring a few times and proceed to a long message telling the caller to leave a message. I didn't leave a message on my calls because I thought that someone would answer. Is that so unreasonable to expect from a business phone number? When I still couldn't reach anyone, I decided to leave a message since I was trying to make a same day appointment. I realized that maybe it's one of those businesses where they only listen to voicemail instead of answering the phone? I wouldn't know; I am/would have been a first time customer to their whole chain. So I called and left a message at 9:14am.

A minute later, I got a call back. She said hi, and   I said, "Hi, thank you for calling me back." Her immediate response was, "For future reference, you don't need to call FOUR TIMES. You just need to call once." Keep in mind, I have never tried to make an appointment with this business before. I was surprised that she felt the need to say it that way, so I apologized (now I know that I shouldn't have had to) and explained that I was trying to reach a person since I didn't know their phone system/process. She replied saying that she's running around (even two minutes after opening?) and can't always get to the phone. It's Tuesday. Maybe you are that busy; maybe you are not. Either way, does it excuse the unintuitive process with which you operate and then fault the customer for? Again, I think it's just unnecessary to be so defensive but that's a higher level of customer service I guess... I didn't say that and let it go. 

She responded to my voicemail about wanting to book a couple's massage later today. She told me that she only has 12:45pm. I asked if that was the only time and she said that there is also a 1pm. (Why didn't you tell me this at the start?) She then added how difficult it'd be to schedule therapists for two people at once because this and that, and it'd be different if we schedule separate sessions. All of this I already knew and understood, but I really did not appreciate the timing and condescending attitude with which she conveyed the information. I wouldn't be in the area until 2pm or later, so I asked if there was another available time around then. She then sneered and replied sternly but with this condescending chuckle, "I have 12:45pm, and 1pm." As if to emphasize in a "I already told you what's available, how stupid are you to ask again" kind of way...

So I simply said, "Okay, nevermind then. Thanks." By that point, I had no interest in continuing the conversation because I didn't feel respected and valued as a potential customer. Can't speak on the actual massage, because I didn't get the chance to even make my appointment. If you can't even make your customers feel welcome and comfortable on the phone, I have no confidence in coming into your business.

Took my son and his friend around 5 pm this evening and it was a bit rainy so they were the only kids there for a good bit of time. Used a Groupon (8 games for $20- check groupon out it'll save you a ton of $) and since they only had each other to play against, the staff took turns playing with them and it really made their night. Very nice staff and they had a blast, we had a great time.

I have been going to heads and tails off and on since they opened. I have never had a bad experience in this salon, and by far have had my best experiences. It is very clean, and stylish. You feel very comfortable from the time your walk in the door. I find the pricing very reasonable, (first time I got a Brazilian I paid 100 and the girl did a horrible job, she also explained that she hated doing brazilians which made me feel very uncomfortable.) I get waxed by Jenne and haven't gotten a blow out done yet, but am planning on it soon. If your new to waxing or are just looking for a new salon that does a great job this is the place to go. When you go in for your appointment you can go over everything you want done and they can tailor their services to your needs, like if you are nervous on doing a full Brazilian and want a custom bikini instead. Also I've never been to a place that shapes my eyebrows as well as heads and tails... And I have tricky eyebrows that are two different shapes, so getting them to look even and similar can be very difficult. As long as I'm getting waxed I'll be a customer of heads and tails. You will not be disappointed with their services.

Friendly staff. Took to-go couple of times. I liked their paneer butter masala and chicken 65 comparing to other items. Initially I thought everything is bit pricey but they are serving decent portion for the money money.

Came here for Mother's Day. My mom and stepdad really enjoyed the food here. I do think the menu did shrink but probably because of the pandemic. We were still able to find everything that we liked to eat. I got my non alcoholic Bahama mama. My parents just got water/soda. Since we got there at the beginning when it first opened that day we were able to get served quickly with drinks. Also we're able to order food in a timely manner and get it out to us. The food was super delicious. My parents loved their food. I took some of my food home due to getting so stuffed so quickly and ate the food later for a dinner meal. The server was super fast when getting the orders in. So we were probably in there a max an hour from being sat to leaving. Definitely would recommend to anyone. They are still a great place to eat even during the pandemic.

My colleague and I wanted a quick bite for lunch and we decided to stop at Marlow's Tavern. Upon entry I immediately realized the space was dimly lit, which put me in a relaxed mood. The service was excellent, the server was attentive and kind throughout the dining experience. I ordered the house made crafted black bean burger in a lettuce wrap with truffle fries. The fries were soft, thin, not crisp and overall okay but it became better after dipping in honey mustard sauce. Words like "HOUSE-MADE BLACK BEAN VEGGIE BURGER" get me excited, however the burger was a disappointment. The pattie was dry and bland. The lettuce tomatoes, carrots and onions added flavor to the meal. Perhaps, a redesign of the black bean burger is in order. I understand Marlow's specializes in meat burgers but us veggie lovers would like some love too :) Overall, okay experience.

This store really lives up to the chain's jingle, it is the place with friendly hardware folks! I've come in here several times and usually because my husband has sent me to grab something he needs to finish a project he's working on, like screws, caulking or nails.  And each time, just as I start to wander through the store with a clueless look on my face, Mike C has come to the rescue, offering his expertise in the most helpful and friendly manner, taking me to the correct aisle when necessary.  While some things may be cheaper elsewhere, I come here because I know I can get help if I need and when I do get help, it's always with a smile.  The ladies up front are friendly as well.

Absolutely a favorite! Have enjoyed Five since their days in the Grove and have always enjoyed an incredible meal. Adventuresome menu treats guests to unique, culinary delights. Love the atmosphere and the wonderful people. You gotta go here!

The place has good quality meat,but a tad on the expensive side. I would suggest buying a groupon or amazon coupon when going to this place and to also go during the week during lunch hours. That will make it cheaper. On holiday weekends like labor day,they jack the price up to 25 per head. They also do not give tap water. They did awhile back,but now they bring you bottled water. The funny thing is they do give you free refills on softdrinks. So I don't know what the deal is with that. They also have a little market in the back area where can buy various latin foods.
The best breakfast place hands down ! Every time we go we feel like family walking through the doors.
We found this cute cafe by accident while looking for something else . What a gem . The service was excellent . Had the pulled pork and black beans , delicious .

Really have not had issues with other CareNow locations until now. The doctor in my recent experience, Arie I believe, completely dismissed my wishes for an antibiotic for sinusitis. Unfriendly with lot of Hubris.

The provided photo (a lighted interior shot) threw me a little bit. The owners keep this old-school restaurant dark, presumably in an attempt to foster an intimate ambiance, but I found myself wanting a flashlight (or a headlight, maybe?) to navigate between the tables, especially when I first entered the restaurant. As my eyes acclimated, I took in the scene -- it looked like the kind of place the Rat Pack might have frequented in an old time movie: dark wood, candle light, 1970's decor. 

The restaurant actually has been there since the mid 70's, and it's not hard to see why: A focused menu, diligent service, and fantastic food make Sperry's a destination worth revisiting. 

Most, if not all, entrees at Sperry's come with a trip to the salad bar. I don't always love salad bars -- the worst are usually neglected relics of 1980's remodel jobs -- this one was worth visiting. The salad bar was small, but filled with fresh choices and all the essentials. (Real and varied lettuce types, fresh tomatoes, real bacon, lots of cheese.) 

I ordered the "Prince William" -- (not to be confused with a Prince Albert) -- a blue cheese-stuffed fillet, wrapped with bacon ($26). The blue cheese was mild, but the steak was very solid, over all, and I would recommend it again. My only criticism is that the fillet, a small steak, was served on a large plate, which made it look rather lonely without any side dishes to accompany it. I also ordered the creamed spinach, which was lovely, and tasted more of spinach than of cream, but added an extra $4 to an already expensive bill. 

My dinner companion ordered another steak (also excellent) with a twice-baked potato, which was ordinary, but acceptable. Worth noting: the 6 oz steak, the salad bar, and the baked potato is about enough food for even the hungriest. There's little need to order the larger cut.

Juanita did a wonderful job on my hair. I was nervous to try a new hair cut but she made me look fabulous :)
Thanks!!

My girls and I went to the cake bake shop for a "real life tea party."  We wore tiaras and white gloves with our dresses.  It was such an amazing memory.  The decor is absolutely beautiful.  The food was scrumptious.  We finished off with a few cake choices.  Each slice was amazing.  I would highly recommend taking your girls or your friends here to create some magical memories.  It's expensive, but completely worth going!  The staff treat you like royalty.  Everyone really should explore this experience!

Nice selection of supplements and vitamins. The customer service is friendly but I got disappointed with what I bought here. I got the nuts and more peanut butter but when I got home and open the peanut butter it was way too dry and old. So I went back for the 2nd time and I got another peanut butter of the same kind but this time it's way too watery as if someone just opened it and add oil or water on it and then resealed it. I know about the quality of  nuts and more peanut butter you know and also I do buy nuts and more peanut butter at GNC but it's not the quality of nuts and more like what I got in this shop. As well I do go to other Vitamin Shop in other town or other states but I don't get disappointed with what I buy. This shop doesn't seem to check the product first before putting it in their shelf where they should do that first.

Located inside Reading Terminal Market, DiNic's offers great service and amazing meat sandwiches! We ordered the ~$10 Roast Pork Sandwich and ~12 Brisket Sandwich with sharp provolone (MUST-ADD) and sweet roasted peppers as toppings. I had the brisket sandwich, and the juicy, tender meat contrasted with the truly sharp provolone created a delicious and unique flavor. I suggest adding ketchup if you want an even better range of delicious flavors in every bite!
The pizza is always on point, the restaurant is clean, and the service is fast. One of my favorites is the BBQ chicken pizza! They have a nice selection of boozy thangs, too, if you're into that.

Top Shelf.  I've been to zoos all over America and I have paid lots more and lots less for admission/parking/food.  The Nashville Zoo at Grassmere is the best balance I have ever found, and apparently they do it with NO PUBLIC FUNDING whatsoever.  It's all admissions and private donations!

Rock on.

Bought tires a year ago, one has been leaky ever since (yep, I waited a year to bring it in...) So I brought my giant truck in with the camper loaded and asked them to look. Well, it was a nail! Had to have picked that up within a week of having new tires installed. Anyway they patched it up for me on the spot! Awesome service! And the tires have been awesome too!

I've been to Windsong many times over the years and I always have an amazing time. Everything from booking a boat, to driving it, is a breeze because of the friendly and knowledgeable staff. The office staff helped me pick a boat that fits my needs and budget. While the dockhands always make sure we have everything we could possibly need: cooler, ice, chairs, waters and sodas, and even fishing poles and bait. When we plan on drinking like pirates, we have opted for a licensed captain to come along and make sure we are safe while we party. You can even have a beach BBQ where everything is set up for you and all you have to do is arrive and enjoy the beach, good food, and shaded covered area with chairs. If you do a BBQ you have to try the BBQ chicken and shrimp its amazing and Chef Bud will take great care of you

Windsong has something for everyone, Capt. Wendy, and the crew will make sure you have a great experience and are well taken care of.

It's byob!! Their app spreads are delish as well as salads and other hot apps. Entrees are big portions and very tasty. My lamb shank was amazing, as it fell right off the bone with a fork. My friends enjoyed their meals too from fresh fish to gyro. We were impressed and delighted. Unfortunately their desserts need work. None of it was any good or fresh. Too sad because bad dessert really does spoil an entire meal. And now I know not to order any next time. Service was great. The girls were attentive and we even had some special service by the chef and owner. Thank you!
They had closed 40 minutes prior but I called as I was in a pinch and they took me in no explanation necessary! Awesome friendly staff.

We stopped in for a late lunch.we ordered the mushroom cheese crepes. They come with a small cup of soup.we had the onion.  The crepes ate made to order in the manner they are made in France. The soup and crepes were delicious. The presentation was outstanding and delightful. The staff is friendly and efficient. Our only suggestion would be to park on the side of the building because it is difficult to back out onto Gulf Blvd. we will return and try the remaining menu.

When we got there, the line was out the door and down the street! But it went really quick, and we were sat in no-time flat. I had the spicy braised chicken, with jambalaya and that green veggie stuff lol. It was awesome. Can't wait to return.

Great service, reasonable prices, fun atmosphere.  

The jambalaya left something to be desired, but wasn't bad.  I think the seasoning was off just a tad, but I still enjoyed it.  My fiance ordered the surf and turf and while she loved the shrimp, her steak tasted like it had been left out.  Not left out under a heat lamp, but left out before it was cooked.  She didn't get sick though, so maybe it was something else.  (It almost tasted like it had been cooked over a gas flame instead of a nice smokiness you'd get from charcoal or wood-baked.)

The salad that came with the entree wasn't very good at all, to the point that I would just forgo it.  Nutrionless iceberg lettuce, no croutons or almonds or eggs or nuts, only came with onions and over-sized tomato slices.  Odd.  Also, for a "boat house" they didn't have many seafood options.  Based on other reviews, seems like we should have stayed in the "beef" zone and ordered burgers.

Also -- the food arrived fast.  Like scary, five minutes fast.  Makes me wonder what's going on in the kitchen...
