I've been to a lot of Chinese restaurant and most of the places taste like panda express or less. This place, I was really suprised that they can actually cook! The food is good compare to other places, but they do poor job for taking care of the ingridents. 

Overall: good

The wine and cheese place has an excellent selection of various wines and liquor. They also have a really nice variety of cheeses, sweets, and crackers. Additionally, they have a variety of excellent cocktail accessories (bitters, bourbon cherries, syrups, etc). There will usually ALWAYS be a vendor on site for sampling's; usually you can refer to the website for special events/vendors. The staff is helpful and consistent (there isn't a new person every time you go in). The environment is calm and relaxing, perfect for browsing and taking your time. Check it out!

Service is consistently slow. We waited around 10 minutes just for waters. The table next to us go 3 meals before we received our first. 
Food was pretty good though.

We were a party of five dining on a Tuesday night at about 8 PM.  The restaurant was about 1/4 full.  The interior of this place is beautiful- roomy and very well appointed.  The waiter appeared promptly and took drink orders.  When he brought the wrong drinks, he looked at us like we had mis-ordered.  (throughout the evening, he tried to project this "I'm a surly but accomplished waiter"  attitude),  We asked about ordering a sushi/sashimi boat, which we saw on an adjacent table and was "market" priced on the menu.  He left to "ask the chef" then said it would be $250 and take 45 minutes, as would any other order from the sushi chefs.  Unbelievable as the restaurant did not seem that busy.  We ended up ordering teriyaki beef, chicken, and salmon.  Mine was beef, which was passable but overpriced.  To add insult to injury, the waiter penciled in a 20% tip, which he said was restaurant policy for "large parties."  I'd stay away,

Not that bad. Not that good. Somewhat pretentious. Interesting cocktail ingredients that don't quite coalesce. Some good wines on the list but not properly chilled. Good octopus appetizer. Pasta doesn't taste homemade (as warranted by the server). Pizza lackluster. Not worth a return visit.

We had a leak under our sink and Tom came out right away to fix it. He was fast, professional, and honest. We have had this company out for a couple other things and will continue to use them in the future. Great customer service!

So the plane was delayed a bit and all I could think about was: We aren't going to make it to Crabby Jacks in time :( Luckily, the po-boy gods blessed us and we made it 15 minutes before closing. We had the duck po boy which is what kinda drew me here to try. It was awesome. I'm not a native so I won't even attempt to critique the po boy part of it but that was one damn tasty po boy. We also had the shrimp which was pretty damn tasty too. Very cute place. Get here 15 minutes before closing and no line! :) Great 1st stop off the plane.

So I was sitting on my couch and jumped up to grab my husbands phone, and dropped mine (an iPhone 5) from my lap straight on to the floor glass side down. I was so upset. I immediately started crying bc I realized that I had broken not only the glass but the LCD screen and needed an entire replacement. I called them they said 100 buck to replace it I got there, was greeted immediately. The guy told me 15 min. We spoke about some phones he had in store for sale, btw great prices for great products. Not even 20 min later a guy comes for the back hands me my phone and viola my phone is fixed looks brand new. It does have a glitch or two, or maybe its just the phone I don't know but its perfect. Going to sell my iPhone on Craigslist and purchase phones from them. I'd recommend them to anyone, I even took some of their cards and will be giving them out to my friends and family.
I don't know why the rating is so high. The rice for the sushi is horrible. It is soggy. This is more of a takeout with 5 tables than a restaurant. Not coming back.

We got cancelled out of an in shore fishing charter due to high winds so four of us decided to do a head boat knowing the winds would have an impact.
We did the 5 hour afternoon trip and caught some keepers and a ton of throwbacks. I had about an 18 inch mackerel up to the boat but lost it.
The mates worked very hard to keep everyone's line in the water and remove the fish that were caught.
We didn't expect much due to the weather and the trip exceeded our expectations.

chapterhouse has some wonderful coffee, and is housed in one of the most beautiful cafe spaces i've ever seen.  that is for sure.

however, like many other coffeeshops, it has become inundated with the spending-six-hours-on-my-laptop patrons.  which can be extremely annoying when you want to grab a latte and food with a friend.  though i dislike the places that cover up their outlets completely to solve this problem, i just wish some of the jefferson med students that study here would get that other people want to sit down.  but i digress....

my only other complaint is that some of the employees here are a bit standoffish.  ok, i get you think you're all intellectual and artsy - but that doesn't mean you can't give me a smile when you serve me, or i tip you.
Don't order the Baja tacos fish or shrimp - no bueno! Service not much better  you can do better Reno!!

This place is a tucked away little secret in Town n Country. We don't have any places like this anywhere around here. I only rate it two stars because I wouldn't have the faintest clue what to do with anything bought here. Tip to Japanese store owners: we love your food, but don't know how to make it on our own. Halp! (recipe cards would be helpful) Help us help you!

Let me start off with the food was very good.  The service on the other hand...NOT SO MUCH!  Greeted and seated by a very pleasant young man.  Bartender, Ashley waited on us and was not a pleasant individual.  No smile, bad vibe altogether.  Ordered and specifically said no tomatoes on a salad, there were tomatoes on the salad!  She took it away and when she brought it back about dumped it on the floor and just dropped it at the table with attitude!  Another server delivered our food, very pleasant and reassured us the order was correct and read it back to us as he set it on the table.  . Ashley checked on us once and my husband asked for ketchup and again threw it on the table as she walked by.  
When you work in the public, especially for tips, attitude is everything!  If your in a pissy mood before work, check it at the door on your arrival to work.  Fake it, whatever you need to do to not poison the atmosphere with your negativity!  I hope her manager shows her this review!

Chinese food on Christmas in the Tampa area just doesn't sound the same as Chinese food on Christmas in NYC. It doesn't taste the same either.

Locals rave about this place and while it may be good for Florida standards, it doesn't hold up to NY standards. (That sounds so food snobbish, but it's true!) 

Nothing was bad at all, it just seemed like everything tasted the same. Didn't matter the protein or veggie...the sauce was similar in every dish and made it all taste the same. 

I'll fulfill my Chinese cravings when I'm home, not visiting family in Fla.

The kids love this place! Wish they served all pieces of the chicken, but it's the sauce and chicken fingers that make this place. Always get the chicken strip sandwich and Texas toast. That's the go too! Extra sauce. If u want some good chicken with a great sauce, this is the restaurant to go too!!

I'm not quite sure what I was expecting, to be honest. It's an adult Chuck E. Cheese. With all the good and bad that comes with that (but no ball pit that some poor kid has left a present in).

So let's start off with the good. 
-There's a nice selection of deals for the budget-minded for food, drinks, and games. 
-It's a brand new building, so (almost) everything is nice and shiny and new.
-There's a nice selection of redemption games, arcade, light gun games, racing, even some 3D games
-The prices for the games are perfectly reasonable, some even far cheaper than you'd expect for higher level games. Refreshing, considering how many quarters got eaten in old arcades of my youth.

The Meh:
-I do wish that they'd setup some classic games (pinball, older fighting games, etc.), but that's more a personal gripe than anything else
-The reload stations for your play card (the card you use to play games) are sort of off in a corner and not easily visible. The area is near where you redeem tickets for prizes, but it's somehow tucked away a bit and hard to see.
-The music is SUPER loud, and doesn't help when combined with the din of a lot of people. Maybe I'm getting older but I couldn't even hear myself think.
-There's one bathroom area. It's enormous, well maintained, and I understand its placement (along the wall in the middle of the game area) but a smaller bathroom near the dining area would be nice just so you wouldn't have to push your way through a bunch of people clustered around a game to use the toilet.
-The food is merely OK. It wasn't awful (nothing undercooked or anything like that), but for the level of expense, I was expecting just a bit more than what I got, if that makes sense.
-Tried my hand at Guitar Hero, but found that even if you don't play the guitar at all, it won't give you a "Game Over" for some reason. Made no sense to me.

The Bad:
Here's where we get down to the brass tacks. Even taking into account the fact that the staff is new and all the baggage that comes with that, there were some serious missteps that just cannot be overlooked.
1. I came there with a somewhat small group from my church (about 10 people total). We were given our own table that was "ours until 8:30pm", which is OK except that while the place was fairly packed in the gaming area, the dining area was not, and accepting that I know nothing about restaurant/reservation management, it seemed that it wouldn't have been a problem to just let us sit there for however long we wanted.
2. The delays between visits from our server. She was perfectly nice, but the times we saw her could be counted on one hand.
3. The food itself was OK, as previously mentioned. But, there were a number of miscues with the food and related items, such as:
3a. When we received our food, we received no silverware or napkins. None had been provided when we were seated, and only after prompting and another, frankly unreasonable wait was it provided.
3b. One of the people in our group ordered chicken strips only to find out that they'd run out of them in the kitchen. This only after everyone else at the table had gotten their food (including a few others who had ordered chicken strips). It speaks of poor inventory management, and not checking to make sure for a large group order that they've got enough of everything.
4. Most importantly, a number of the more expensive games were in less than stellar shape. I know it's a public arcade, and that between drunk adults and hyper children (and seriously, too many really little kids with no supervision, felt like I really was in Chuck E. Cheese at times), there'll be some wear and tear on things. But for a basically brand new place, stuff that was completely off and uncalibrated, as well as broken, was a bit silly. As an example, on a lot of the light gun games (think Time Crisis, etc.), you'd have to aim the gun almost off the screen to land shots in the center of the screen. This resulted in a rather comical look of people playing those games with the guns pointed somewhere off in the distance. Part of an arcade being good is maintaining the equipment, and taking the time to make sure maintenance is getting done is part of ensuring the guests have a good time.

In closing, if you want to drink and play some games with friends, and you don't care about all of the games being perfect, you'll likely have a nice time. If you want to eat here, I'd only recommend if you have the patience of a saint.

Decided to watch the Lightning hockey game at Brick House. First off, if you are looking for a place to watch all the sports you want, this is it!!! They have TVs everywhere and a variety of seating options indoor and outdoor. The bar is really nice, being half indoors and half outdoors (with a roof over). To top off the great atmosphere, our server Kaitlyn was just phenomenal. 

We chose where we wanted to be seated and started off with the pretzel appetizer.  I am a huge sauce person, loving to try all and any different sauces. The photo of the pretzel shows the dips that come with it (queso, siracha ranch, and yellow mustard). Our server went above and beyond giving us a variety of the other sauces they have for other menu items. Our entrees came out in a timely manner and was exactly what we wanted. Being a picky eater myself, I ordered a salad and asked for a few additions which I received with no extra charge. The chicken sandwich was tender and juicy, and how can you go wrong with some bacon added?! Instead of the traditional sides, we chose the apple cider slaw for a little bit of health. Lastly we got a few Togo boxes for what we didn't finish and the server brought out little togo containers with all the different sauces. 

Service and food was excellent! Definitely will be going back soon! 


Had to go back and of course had to ask for Kaitlyn!! We watched the Lightning hockey game again and had a blast. Ordered some different items this time! 

Zucchini curls- AMAZING, will always have to order these now! 
Beef tips and a side salad with extra toppings- beef tips were so tender and flavorful.

So someone recommended me with her hair lady Chanelle. So I contacted her and she set me up with an appointment for Monday June 25th at 5pm. I got there a little early and I texted her that I had arrived. The front desk girl also called her twice and no answer. I waited for half an hour and I didn't hear back at all so I left. This is terrible service and it is not cool to set up someone for an appointment and then just not show up or respond to messages or phone calls. I went straight there after work I was already tired and I was looking forward to my haircut but instead I was disappointed. I could have been taking care of other things instead of wasting an hour or more of my time. very not cool!!!

Stopped by this weekend with family and we really enjoyed ourselves.  First, the staff was amazing; they were attentive and helpful.   The restaurant has a retro counter-diner feel and is sleekly decorated.  The burgers, fries, onion rings and black/white milkshake were all good.  The burgers tasted a little salty maybe overseasoned?  We ordered the LA Burger, Crunchburger and Children's Cheeseburger.  Would definitely return if in the Penn Campus area and this place is very good for a "burger place".

So this was sort of a split decision. First, the ice cream was absolutely delicious. I had a scoop of Strawberry Bliss and a scoop of Coconut Chocolate Fudge and wanted more before I even finished. It was cold and creamy and buttery and delicious. It tasted like they had just made it. The downside was that there is hardly any seating and the outdoor seating they have is really uncomfortable. The patio area could be a cool place to have your ice cream and chill out but it's very uneven and everyone I saw go out there tripped on the uneven pavement.  I'm pretty sure they are trying to be hip but I think you can be hip and comfortable. Bottom line is I'll probably go back but I'm driving my truck and tailgating along the street.

Update: I went back. I'll stick to my parking/seating comments and hope for better seating options someday but in the meantime this ice cream is ridiculously good. I want more please!
Cute little place with a nice atmosphere, people, decor and food. Got a pizza and it was amazing.

My wife and I visit Thai Thani every now and then for delicious Thai cuisine and are always left feeling satiated. In fact, we typically share an appetizer and an entree due to their portions being quite large. The quality of the food is very good and has a lot of TLC involved. I also like that it is never really that crowded which lends itself to romance and very quick service. We will definitely continue to return for years to come.
This place was great. Wine was awesome and Jessica knew a lot about the vineyard, the growth of grapes, and the family who owns the vineyard.
Fresh pasta, great sauce, tasty focaccia, delicious desserts, local and awesome.  The staff is also very friendly. We've eaten there multiple times and never been let down.

I went in for a last minute appointment with Stacy. Probably one of the nicest stylists I've ever met - friendly, approachable and courteous. She even gave me tips for straightening my unruly and wavy hair.

I was in New Orleans for the Saints home game against the Falcons. My fiancé is from there and had told me about his dad working at Mandina's a long time ago. So glad we had the chance to go there that Monday before the game. Portions are big! I ordered the 1/2 order Oyster Po Boy. So so good! Thank you for an enjoyable experience. Lots of love from Vegas!

When in town visiting family, decent resto choices are pretty slim in the New Port Richey area but driving almost an hour to Tampa all the time isn't exactly convenient. 

This is definitely a welcome addition to the neighborhood and it's not just a decent place, but a really good place. There's something for everyone on the menu and the burgers and flatbreads are standouts. Real good specials each night, not the best wine list but an excellent beer list. Cool rustic decor, late hours with a fun and vibrant atmosphere, which can get a little loud, but surprisingly my mom doesn't even mind it. Guess it makes her feel young. All in all, a very good spot for a local and causal night out.

Amazing!

 Amy's massages, facial's, and pedicures,are the best. Absolutely professional and friendly. 
And it is very convinient location to get to. 
Love it
This place has the best cocktails! Love the bread and butter with cinnamon flavor. Service is always friendly and quick.

This place is mad Kool. 
Atmosphere is great, music is great everyone is relaxed having fun and just no worries in the world.  
2 floors. Top floor has Pool tables, bar television and some couches. 
Main floor has foosball, shuffleboard, great traditional restaurant seats for eating, watching the game or fight or just drinking with a large group. 
What makes this place that much better is it's located in the heart of Philly, old city. Plenty of bars, clubs, lounges, and restaurants to choose from. 
Over all this place is a great place just to kick back enjoy the night and have some fun.

Anyone of their locations is going to be fantastic! Plan to wait a little before you eat because they always have a line! Definitely worth the wait and they hustle to get you seated. Service is always good. If you like eggs Benedict they have the best selection and hollandaise sauce! If you need breakfast this place will not disappoint

Over the last few years this place has become a family go to around the holidays.  Its an hour and a half drive to the airport so we always stop to grab food either coming or going.  This year the whole family, me, mom, dad, brother and soon to be sister in law, popped in here after grabbing the brother/fiancee from the airport.  It was the Saturday night before Xmas and the place was packed!!!  The hostess gave us the option of a 2 hour wait, or see if we could grab a table in the 'bar area'.  (Bar area is a huge area that can seat over 100)  Some how (christmas miracle) found a table for the 5 of us, and grabbed a seat immediately.
We'd been here before and knew what beers we liked.  Their brews are good, nothing too out there for an area that is famous for budweiser.  The brown ale is the go to for us.  We all ordered entrees and the food came out in a reasonable time for as crowded as it was.  Service was good, especially since we were getting 'bar service'.  Everyone enjoyed their meals, no complaints.  The food is a bit pricey, but it is a touristy area and it is consistently good.  
Like I said this place has kept us coming back on a semi-annual basis (since the closest one of us lives 100 miles away thats a pretty good return rate) for the past few years.  We'll more than likely be back the next time we all fly home for the holidays.

The last time we came here we said we wouldn't come back,  but as that was awhile ago, I went against that decision and decided to try it again.   MISTAKE. 

This has to be the loudest restaurant I've ever eaten in.   The last time,  we complained about the noise and were told "it's family style and people like to have a good time".  So it's perfectly acceptable to yell down the table to other people in your group and dance in the aisles, heck the staff will even laugh and clap along with you.  See they can laugh and clap along because they aren't using that time to actually provide you with good service.   Waitress disappeared so long we were asking other wait staff for things,  and those requests were mostly ignored.   This time we asked for a table in a quieter section of the restaurant,  the hostess smiled at us,  like YEAH RIGHT GOOD LUCK WITH THAT.   Once again we couldn't hear the people directly across the table from us, and my college aged kids went outside as soon as they were done their meal because of it.

On a plus side,  I noticed most people bringing like 12 packs of beer and lots of wine in.  it's byob even though they have a liquor license.  That probably accounts for some of the noise.  It's like an Eagles game with Italian food.  Except I didn't want to eat at an Eagles game,  I wanted a nice dinner with my family. 

And for all the people that complain about having reservations and still having to wait a long time,  I can confirm that's true and I know part of the reason.   As you wait for almost an hour past your reservation time you'll notice that the owner will seat everyone he knows before you, even though they don't have reservations.   See he's a great guy that way.   He'll also come around and socialize with those same people,  yet act like everyone else there is an annoyance to him. 

If you read thru the reviews you'll see these same things complained about over and over again.  And I can only guess that the people giving the good reviews are his friends that he takes care of,  and those individuals that love hitting the liquor store on the way to the restaurant so they can party it up "on the cheap"

Kind of a shame too, because the food is actually pretty good

This was recommended to me by a Greek friend of mine, and boy was she right! By far the best souvlaki in tarpon springs.  It's very casual, almost like a street food stand. Go early though. When he sells out he packs up for the day. I've seen him sold out by 3 pm.

After hearing great reviews about this restaurant, we decided to visit...and we were certainly pleased. Although they were pretty busy, we were seated within 20 minutes. The service was awesome and the food was awesome. It just doesn't get any more awesome than that! The portions were huge, so definitely go on a day when you're ready to dig in. Thanks Deanies! We will definitely be returning!

High prices, rotten produce (you can get fresher vegetables and fruit on ninth street for a fraction of the price and we all know that produce is on it's last leg but at least it's cheap), VERY miserable employees....They actually stand there with their arms crossed while you bag your own groceries. Also was in there tonight and three employees putting out produce were talking like they were on the corner of Broad Street using the F word loud and several times... where are the managers here? So unprofessional this place is a sorry excuse for a grocery store.
Most restaurants have 2 of 3 things, Atomosphere, great Food , amazing service. This is one of a million that's got all 3!!! Thank you for everything !!!!
We called in our order for pick up, and our order was prepared quickly and accurately. Everything tasted great, but I feel like it was a little overpriced. Overall it was a good experience.
The teas taste great but the sales clerk we had was pushy and I probably won't return to the store because of her.  Way to expensive.
Had another Wonderful dinner! Meatball appetizer was yummy! Gnocchi special with shrimp in pesto sauce was perfect!!! Can't wait to return

I'm going to out and tell you that my review will not be an accurate reflection of how good Tacconelli's is. Many reviewers less humble than I would purport to provide an authoritative opinion on their culinary experience in a given review, although in reality they ordered the crappy "experimental" dish like 10 minutes before closing time on a Saturday night. 

Being a man of truthfulness - an Esq., even! - I will make no such misrepresentations. Instead, I will inform you here and now that when I review a restaurant, I tend to abide by the Rule of One. Meaning, if there is one entree at a restaurant that I love, then the place is getting 4 or 5 stars, even if the place is located in the middle of a fallout zone and all the other dishes at the place are made out of cyanide and pure materialized misanthropy. Tacconelli's is such a place and their margherita (with sausage and basil, natch) is that One Entree. I'm not even going to justify my love on a public forum because that would kick-start my withdrawal symptoms.

If you told me that eating this stuff would turn me into a kangaroo, I'd start looking for a joey I could wear in my pouch. The End.

We are out of town visitors and we're excited to give the oldest Mexican restaurant in the United States a try. We were told there's going to be nearly an hour wait. However after some chips and salsa and a couple of over-priced margaritas we were in! By the way the house salsa was delicious. The restaurant itself is very quaint and feels quite historic. We were kind of just stuffed into a corner which was just fine by me. The most commendable thing about her experience was the service. The servers were friendly, checked on us frequently, were knowledgeable of the product, and and professional. We both ordered two different kinds of chimichangas. A bit overpriced in our opinion, and the flavor was just so so. However it was pretty much what I expected. Definitely gigantic and attractive! I ordered the Aged beef. Definitely an acquired taste but I knew what I was getting into. Whatever the case it was a great experience. I think I enjoyed it more than my wife did, which is pretty much goes for most things. If you are ever in Tucson, experience this place. I wouldn't say my chimichanga was mouth-watering or knee dropping, but I'm glad I got it and I'm glad I did it.

I've been going to Fridays for years they just recently got a promotion for all you can eat appetizers for $10 I think it's an awesome deal boneless wings potstickers and they just keep bringing a out it  is great my two favorite boneless wing sauces are Jack Daniels sauce and garlic Parmesan sauce

This location of Five Below is in the Independence Mellon Building where the Ross Department Store & Citizen Bank are located.

This Five Below has 2 Levels and offers cash registers on both floors.  Self checkouts are available as well.  The items available are similar to most Five Below stores (i.e. Candy; Games; Philly Sports Team Items; Educational Books; Blankets, etc).

The candy at 5 for $5 is the devil!

The staff are all around-helpful and attentive.  This Five Below is a nice addition to this building!

This is a pretty good diner for breakfast. While I have eaten breakfast 15-20 times here over the past couple of years, I have never tried it for lunch or dinner. So I can only tell you about the place when everyone else is rushing to work. The one standout item on my plate each time is the hash-brown potatoes that are cooked long enough to make the outside a little crispy but still soft inside. The corned beef hash and omelets have always been served fast and hot. Endless coffee and well sized portions round the place out. Overall a solid choice for breakfast. Being a southerner I tend toward grits and biscuits and gravy and other unhealthy breakfasts. If they had that, it would be a 4-star for me.
Funky atmosphere. Very nice waitress. $5 for 2 eggs, home fries & kielbasa. all good stuff. Can't beat that.

This store is amazing!  Not only for their outdoor furniture but all of the beautiful decor as well.  Sales people are friendly, helpful and professional.
Highly recommend shopping here for your patio/outdoor needs!

Great breakfast sandwich today! It was a spicy sausage, egg and cheese on a short roll. The sausage was really good, large portion, and the roll really made the sandwich... For six bucks or whatever it really works. There are a couple tables and chairs, but it's an ideal takeout joint. Will definitely be back here for a quick breakfast bite in the future.

Stephen the bartender was the shit. He got a mouth full off 151 and blew fire at a hooker. She caught fire a little but we got her put out and long story short she gave me a half price burn discount on a handy in the bathroom. Love that place.

Always good on a rainy day, or if you are feeling under the weather! Whenever my bf and I want something warm in our stomach, we turn to each other and ask, "Want to get some pho?" And we go to Pho Kien Giang. The staff are pretty speedy and the food comes quickly. I love to get the classic Pho Dac Biet. It has all different types of beef. I load up my pho with bean sprouts and Thai basil. Delicious!

I wish I could give this place more stars...I have been here probably 12 times since they opened (crazy I know). I am obsessed. I dream about the nashville hot buns. Everything I have had here is so amazing. The service is always great, even though the place is constantly packed and a bit loud. Things you must order: cheese curds, nashville hot buns, fried chicken, meatloaf. These have consistently been my favorites. But I have also enjoyed the chop cuey, all the salads, short rib strogonoff, lobster buns and tofu buns. Please try and save room for desert....the menu changes  often but if there is anything resembling a donut, GET IT. youll thank me later. During one visit I was at the bar looking into the kitchen and (the head chef and owner) Marcie Turney was standing next to me directing dishes and taking the time to make sure every dish was perfect, which I loved. I am counting the minutes until they start brunch service!!!
Best breakfast in all of New Orleans, to me. The Cochin ay lait is PHENOMENAL!!! I crave it while I'm away and get excited every year I'm in town to taste it again.

I went by myself and they treated me as if I had a party of 8--meaning they were attentive, informative and prompt. It was my first time ever there and Danielle was very helpful in her descriptions and recommendations. I had the Bowl Bluto Buster - great portion, tasty meal!

This place is amazing!  Great wine and great food!  Everyone is so nice and knowledgeable.   Great experiences with Jonathan, Shawn and talking to the manager Danny.  Great guys!   Second time here and will become a regular.   Awesome!!!!

I like beer. I don't particularly like refinement. I like Philadelphia. I don't mind some surly attitudes from staff. In fact, I expect it and prefer it to artificial niceness that is not so subtly asking for bigger tips. So the first time I went here, I was not surprised to find someone behind the bar taking pride in his surliness. In fact, he called the day Surly Sunday to commemorate himself. 

The beer was fine (mostly American micro). Not the most exciting tap selection out there, and certainly nowhere near the best in Philadelphia (Eulogy is a bit better, although it is lacking compared to some of the newer places like Memphis Taproom, Tria, and Local 44). On a Sunday, the service was fine and the surly bartender was a little talkative although I don't think he really liked us. Whatever. 

The second time we came in late. We ordered one beer (after waiting for quite a bit). It was late. We got accused of smoking pot inside and then were looked at suspiciously. Granted, I think someone inside may have been smoking pot, as we all smelled it, we certainly were not. In any case, when I cam back up to the counter to pay my tab, I was completely ignored for about 10 minutes. I left without paying. Thanks for the free beer. I doubt I'll come back.

This is a great place!  Since we recently moved, it's now very close.  It will be convenient to grab a creative gift or find something for our home.  The inside is much larger than one would think.  It is very clean and well organized.  Prices are reasonable.  Merchandise covers a wide variety of styles and eras.  They offer collectible items, as well as home decor.  Free coffee and popcorn are offered, as well as chips and beverages for sale.  The staff is so friendly and welcoming.  It's definitely not a group of artsy, antique snobs.  They appreciate the $20 purchase as much as the $200 one.  One of the benefits is a points club where you can receive discounts for purchases.  Overall, it's a fun place to spend an hour or two browsing.  You should definitely stop in.

Waste your time with this place only if you want a quick meal this has barely anything to do with empanadas. More like expensive hotpockets.

I really really really wanted to like this place. I've been eating empanadas since I was a kid and they are the ultimate comfort food. 1) The dough: really poor quality. Too flakey and too soggy. 2) Filling: way under seasoned and over mixed. The meat just becomes tough and looses its flavor. 3) Flavor Combinations: Very poor. I had most varieties available for the day and they were just unexciting. 4) Naming: Calling something brazilian doesn't make it brazilian. I asked how she went from chimichurri chicken to Colombian. She said, I don't know we just pick a name that we like. ARE YOU KIDDING! I don't put a sausage in a bun and call it a brat. Lame.

Home Depot has the worst customer care I've ever experienced. The basic move for their management staff (which I've experienced for 2 straight months trying to get them to properly complete a tile delivery) is to pass the buck and then retreat into a labyrinthine corporate structure. Please save yourself the heartache and find a different option than Time Hole Depot.

May not be the absolute best BBQ in St. Louis, but it is very good especially for the price. The beer selection is decent. I like that they have many local brew options. It has a very bar/divey atmosphere which is great. If you live in South City and want a good place to grab some BBQ, I definitely recommend Southtown pub.

My kids absolutely loves this place. Great atmosphere and staff.  A young gentleman named Will was very accommodating! This pass Sunday was my second visit . I am not from the area but when I come back to visit family this will definitely be our go to!

Honestly this isnt the best Mcdonalds to go to in town or even around the block from most places. Ordered a #4 large and that was simple enough youd think? The helpful cashier even asked everything on it? I said yes and got a hard old patty, and no tomatoes when the build is mayo, leaf lettuce and chicken patty. Thoroughly disappointed.
Update: after returning 2 minutes before close they shut off menus and closed store early and BLATANTLY IGNORED US. We will be returning early morning.

EDIT(2/13/15) Been back many times since the first review and tip I need to add - ask what the soup of the day is. I have had several different daily soups that are absolutely to die for, a spicy posole, a thai seafood chowder-type mixture that was just delicious with huge chunks of fresh seafood, and a great spicy pumpkin bisque. So Tip 1) bar bites menu & Tip 2) try the soups! & Tip 3) take a risk and try the wine of the month.
All good!

Haven't visited Yelp in a number of years - however, the meal I just consumed, forced me to write this review.  It was probably one of the worse restaurant takeaway meals I've ever had.  Sirloin and Crab Cake.  The steak was done just as ordered, no objection there - but it was so tough and full of fat, it was almost uneatable. The Crab Cake was so small, I almost missed it, plus, it was full of way too much filling, other than crab, and so spicy that the taste of the crab was lost.  The "whipped" potatoes had no taste at all, and appeared to have been just taken out of the fridge in a lump and heated.  Thankfully, I "upgraded" for an extra charge, the vegetable, from the "signature" broccoli to the "prime" asparagus - that at least was very good.  This is the second time I've visited this restaurant, both times to use gift cards.  Do not plan another visit - my gift giver has to be in formed of our objections - Oh, my wife also had a meal with me - shrimp and fries - which she said was way too salty.
Does it even need a review. Awesome, always has and always will be awesome.  Fresh food, great portions, easy on the wallet and the service is "diner-perfect"!!!

Nunzio's is a "Meal". 
I have been a Patron of Nunzio's food since the "Monte Carlo" years.  Now at Nunzio's the dining room is reminiscent of an outdoor Piazza with hand painted frescos and faux streetscapes. It is captivating.  I have had dinners for my fraternity alums, social gatherings, and business meetings.  Each time my companions and I have left satisfied with no complaints.  The wait staff is capable, courteous, and very attentive to our needs.  The food is excellent.  
The appetizers are delicious and sufficient for our needs. The entrée of my choosing was the Split Veal Chop stuff with Sautéed Spinach and Mozzarella.   The meat was sufficiently brazed and cooked to a mouth watering consistency that was complimented by the Spinach and Mozzarella and the Mushroom Demi-glace.  The freshness of ingredients and culinary skill is evident in presentation of the greens and homemade pasta.  I recommend this Special.
If you are lucky enough to see Nunzio in the dining room, a rare occasion, he is sure to come up to you and thank you for your patronage.  He is very approachable and willing to enjoy a glass of wine with you before returning to his extremely busy kitchen.  
I have read several of the reviews and completely agree with many of them that recognize the artistry of gourmet cooking, the simplicity of Italian/Mediterranean regional cuisine, and attentive service.   I have to laugh at those that quibble on price and complain about soda refills.  You my friends are "Olive Gardenesk "with a buffet priced palette to match.   
For those seeking an opportunity to enjoy a Meal try Nunzio's and agree with me that it is the BEST!  Buon Appetito!

I live close by and see this place almost everyday. After being able to make an appointment and reading all the great reviews I was really optimistic about the thought of maybe finding a good nail salon in Miami. I got a red gel manicure and regular pedicure. When I walked in I was promptly greeted and sent to a chair. The lady chitchated with me for a few minutes and continued doing my nails. I know red can be a little tricky but it was getting all over my cuticle and was a little too messy for my liking. The tables for the manicures are shared as in connected to each other. So when the lady was filling my nails the entire table was shaking and the lady working next to her had to tell her to file a bit softer as it was messing up her clients manicure and vice-versa. In conclusion; I'm still looking for a good nail salon that I can feel ok about spending $50 in... the search continues.

After seeing all the positive reviews of this place I decided to stop by for lunch. Ordered the half and half boneless with the olive oil/secret spicy. Very disappointing. The olive oil just tasted like any other cheap frozen chicken tender you'd buy at a supermarket. Was actually surprised at how plain and bland it was. The secret spicy was all sweet and zero spice. The sauce tastes exactly like gochujang and sugar. 

The order also took about 25 minutes and I was the only one there so be prepared to wait awhile. I might give them another chance and try one of the other flavors but for over $22 I expected way better. No idea why this place has so many positive reviews.

Founding Farmers is great! Their menu has a wide selection so I've been a repeat customer and still always try new things. My favorite is probably their fried chicken. Their cocktails are also very good and not too steep in price.
Typical In-N-Out Burger.  Lots of parking thanks to being in the El Con Mall area and across from Target.  Food is good, and service is quick.

Frosty Jakes has delicious custard and a surprising and creative selection of sundaes to choose from. I ordered a peanut butter, chocolate, and banana sundae and my hubby ordered the banana, chocolate and pecan option (called Jake's favorite).  The custard was creamy and cool, and although the portions are not huge, they satisfy.  There are some issues with customer service; for instance, they forgot the bananas in my hubby's sundae and rather than make a new one they splatted a handful of bananas on top of his melted ice cream.  Still, I recommend this dessert oasis in the desert.
Truffle fries, tuna tartar, caramelized onion cheese tart , short ribs, and the brined chicken were all amazing! Highly recommend!

So I did cheat a bit on my first review given it was from an elite event. I finally made my way back in here today and guess what I had, my sushi roll ($7), described as carrots and cucumbers julienned, sun seed pate, bell peppers, marinated mushrooms, sprouts and a dipping sauce. Today it was a peanut looking sauce with sesame seeds. I did ask for a side of their awesome gluten and sugar free and unicorn hair soy sauce which I enjoyed so much the first time. I also tried the creamsicle smoothie, after emphasizing I am immunocompromised and needed washed fruit skins. Made with juiced orange, pineapple, banana, vanilla and almond milk. As my friend Leone would say, "D-Lish!"

The thing that really makes you want to come back is the service, everyone is chill, polite and friendly. Not pretentious hipsters! 

I still love the mission behind this place, in sustainable, ethical food. You feel oh so good eating it.

If you like ice cream you have to get the orange and vanilla twist. A large portion will set you back $2.10 and a regular is $1.60. The vanilla side is regular vanilla soft serve, but the orange side is the best, its a unique orange flavor that I haven't had anywhere else. I disagree with the other two reviews the twist is awesome. The fresh oranges and juice at this place are also really good, better than what you get in the supermarket and the farmers market that recently opened up outside has some great reasonably priced fruits and veggies.

Great studio with friendly staff and wonderful instructors! The space is amazing and the post-class lavender towel always feels great when I'm a sweaty mess. Chrissy led a really fun, relaxing class the other day that was challenging at the same time. Gilbert makes every class unique and entertaining.
absolutely love shopping here, the product and service is consistently great!

Another visit to this Discount Tire, another great experience. 

Sage was super knowledgeable and she was very helpful.  

The rest of the team was great as well as they got my car in right away, got my new summer tires on, bagged my winter tires and put them in the trunk, and had me out of there in 25 minutes. Yes, 25 minutes! 

This place is clean and well run. 

I ordered my tires on the website which in and of itself was a good experience. The user interface is great as I easily found the best tires for my needs. Moreover, the website makes it super easy to tie the order in with an appointment time. Done and done. 

Highly recommend this place.

I never post reviews but after my recent experience at Kimmels, I wanted to warn others. I brought my leather purse in because the corners worn down the the plastic binding was coming out. They acted like it would be an easy fix, but the color might be slightly different. I paid my $43.82 and felt that I was leaving my purse in good hands. When I picked it up I was upset to see they mearly glued cheap leather patches on the corners. The color they chose clashes horribly and sticks out like a sore thumb. When I voiced my disappointment the repair man shrugged and said they don't have rolled binding. That would have been nice to know before they ruined the purse with gobs of glue. They didn't even clean the material before gluing the patches on and there is dirt and a hair! In the glue. I thought the price was very reasonable until I saw the result, now it will cost me a new purse plus the $40+ wasted on the repair :(  If they couldn't repair the purse in a professional looking way I wish they would have called me (or even waited until I came to pick it up) instead of doing this shoddy work. I can't believe they think this is an acceptable repair job for a professional shop.
IMG_1100.JPG

What initially caught my attention about this establishment is that it's African American owned...so you already KNOW you're in for a delectable treat!

But this place surpassed my wildest expectations! It's not often that you can say that everything that you consumed was not only scrumptious but also very filling! Portion sizes are more than adequate. Check my profile for pictures of my entrees! 

Do yourself a favor and stop by! Excellent for small groups! I can't think of any cons at this time. I want to thank the manager for a pleasuarble experience!
Disappointed on the lack of service from the staff every time we have a appt it's a night mare just seem like no one is held full

Pint Size Bakery. Sure they're "pint sized" alright. Their nonexistent "customer dining area" is certainly "pint sized" and the building itself is quite small.  You know what is NOT pint-sized about Pint Size Bakery? Their Cajones! They move in within a stones throw of 2 National established chains - one known for coffee (Starbucks)  the other for baked goods (Panera) and they hang a shingle and decide to sell? Well coffee and baked goods, OF COURSE.  Yeah, that's some GINORMOUSJUMBO cajones if you ask me.  And, in my opinion, they were very, very smart to do so.  Because from everything I can tell, they do BOTH of those things BETTER than those crap National chains anyway.  I seriously, love, Love, LOVE their cranberry potato chip cookies - truly something to write home about (IF people did that anymore) - the perfect balance of sweet and salty.  Do NOT make the mistake of thinking it will taste like potato chips in a cookie and be deterred away from this gem. That would be YOUR mistake.  Their Kaldis coffee is,of course, BETTER than any of the burnt, over-roasted, bitter brown water you will get down the road at the National chains and I love that the owner "tweaks" the Kaldis concoction to make it not overly strong like Kaldis can be.  Again, with those non-pint sized cajones, ladies - because OF COURSE you can even improve on something as fabulous as Kaldis.  With the amazement cranking out of your kitchen - nothing surprises me at Pint Size EXCEPT their hours.  I get it - you are up at the break of dawn making your deliciousness and YOU think 3pm is a PERFECT closing time. Well, as your crazy customer who is always frantically calling you as I'm barrelling down Watson to get there by 3p and begging you to hold "my favorite items for me because I swear I will slide in there just AT your closing time" - I personally would LOVE for you to be open until Midnight. But we don't always get what we want.

The one star deduction is (and please don't look at it as THAT - look at it as a 4 star addition please!!) is for the savory scones EVERYONE is cyberspeaking about both on this site and elsewhere - and saying they are life changing, etc.  I am CLEARLY missing something.  I seriously do NOT taste ANYTHING when I eat these things. It's like a really dense biscuit with a faint note of.....flour???? Maybe I need to take the advice given to another Yelper and HEAT them up for "desired results" but honestly they don't inspire me to do so.  I will stick with my favorites at Pint Size: the cranberry potato chip cookie, the pumpkin bread - in June - can you believe THAT?, and the quiches - all have SIGNIFICANT YUM factor. 

Oh and one of the BEST parts about Pint Size? No barely conscious teenager popping their gum and rolling their eyes in adolescent disdain when I place my order as is ALWAYS the case at Panera.  Nope. These ladies are as warm and welcoming to me, EVEN WHEN I CRASH THEIR PAD AT 2:58 pm, as any customer could ever hope to encounter ANYWHERE in the customer service world. Pint Size gets a HUGE high five from me and as anyone who reads my reviews will attest, that is a rare, RARE thing indeed.  And if they keep doing EVERYTHING so EXCEPTIONALLY well they are going to have to move to a bigger building just to have someplace to put those cajones of theirs!

Went into this restaurant to have a breakfast in the morning and I normally use plastic because the exchange of money of during this pandemic and COVID-19 the dumbasses didn't have a machine at work so I would not go there

It was ok, ambiance was very nice, but it was very loud and the service was TERRIBLE.  the Mat re d' or whatever you want to call him carried on a personal conversation with someone for at least 10 minutes before we were even acknowledged.  Our server was absolutely worthless and sloppy, he was incredibly distracted by who knows what!!!!!  We had to ask for bread and butter....the tuna was very tasty and the bread pudding was nice.  Very over priced for what we received. There are entirely to many options in New Orleans for me to return to this restaurant.

Like always it was incredible! I don't know if I was super hungry but the hash browns  had this flavor that had me wanting more! It was a busy morning but the food was out fast! Great good great service!

So we are huge fans of Bar Rescue and saw the episode and wanted to come check it out ourselves. First time we came was a Saturday night and it was pretty dead when we first came in. For starters I wanted to try their signature "Smores martini" the bartender looked at me like she didn't know what I was talking about so she went to look up the recipe then came back to tell me they didn't have all of the ingredients needed so she couldn't make it. I settled on a pomegranate gimlet instead. Well when I was handed it, there were no pomegranate seeds in it as it stated. Minor issue so I let it go and kept smiling anyways. Their beers on tap were having a lot of issues. Coming out with a glass full of head and 2 of them were completely out of order. Next we wanted to try their food! We decided on a tri tip sandwich and man oh man it was amazing! But first, let me tell you how amazing their cook is. He is so sweet and friendly! He came out to my side and discussed my like and dislike of horseradish since it came on the sandwich. I mentioned I've never had it so I assumed I didn't like it. He offered to dilute it some with some home made ranch. He went back to make the sauce and brought it out to me to try before he put it on my sandwich. When my food came up, it was perfect! Perfectly cooked, seasoned, and the horseradish was awesome. So over all it wasn't a bad experience, we enjoyed ourself regardless of the bar tending mishaps.

One week later we visit again. But on a Wednesday night. More of an old school rap ish feel and a new bartender. So I try again for the Smores martini but again, no ingredients. So I settle for the same as last time she says she doesn't have any pomegranate seeds so I ask if she can make something tropical with vodka and she offered Malibu and pineapple juice.. I settled for that but was a tad disappointed. Oh and the beers on tap were still down and being crazy but the cook told us someone was coming in to fix them after thanksgiving, so that's good!. The bartender was very sweet though and moved around the bar to converse with everyone so we just enjoyed our time there. They also were having problems with their carbonation drink well thing so that threw them off but she really made the best of it. She even made a cocktail we requested that she had never heard of before (and it didn't turn out too bad either!) She was definitely friendly so it made up for the missing ingredients. When the cook came out he recognized us and made us another amazing sandwich. Seriously this cook is pretty awesome. He kept coming out and helping the bartender and talking to the customers and everything, it was very refreshing. To be 100% honest we will definitely come back but it's mostly because of the cook. He's great, truly! It's a pretty good environment to be in. I'm a non smoker so that's a downfall for me but what do you expect in a bar? This is definitely a smoking bar so If that bothers you I wouldn't recommend it. If it doesn't,
I'd recommend you giving them a shot. We like coming in. :)

Dear God, man--how have I not reviewed PYT yet? I've been here a bunch of times and have always had a good time. 

PYT has a pretty extensive burger menu, with specials that are sometimes pure genius. I've had a plain 'ol cheeseburger, which I thought was very good, and the special Handy Nasty (a collaboration with Han Dynasty burger). The latter was made from marinated pork belly (probably blended with beef) with dan dan noodle sauce and served on a steamed bao bun. It was really pretty amazing. They're also notorious for coming up with wacky ideas like the taco shell made of bacon (they literally latticed bacon into a taco shell). So whether your taste is staid, adventurous, or legit insane, they have something for everyone. 

The beer selection is just OK. They only have 4 or 5 taps, and half of them pour domestic mass production stuff. You can find the occasional good craft brew on tap, and they have a decent bottle selection too.  

Though others seemed to have had bad service experiences, I never have. I should note that I only ever sit at the bar, but every time I've been here, the bartenders have been very nice and attentive. 

Insider tip: For the past two years, PYT has opened on Christmas Day around 6pm or so. The kitchen is closed and there are no servers. They just serve up some cold drinks to anyone who needs to recover from a long holiday season, let you bring your own vinyl to play, and order Chinese food from Sang Kee that they give away for free to anyone who's hungry. This is possibly my favorite restaurant event of the year. The Piazza (indeed the city) is deserted that night, except for this twinkling lighthouse on the horizon. Not sure if they will continue to do this, but I lobby them to do so every year on facebook. 

Definitely a good spot and worth checking out.

Great communication. Very professional staff that was very well organized. Took great care of our belongings. The move took a second day, but that wasnt a big deal. They were efficient and willing to help take furniture apart and put it back together again at the other end. They moved us in the pouring rain and never complained or stopped. Best movers we have ever had.
to whoever laughed at this or thought it was funny, aint shit funny about an angry hungry woman bitch.
Great barbecue and beer nice and cold. Having lunch and listening to good music. Nice clean place

We eat here now and then the food is good have not had a bad meal yet and have had several different items from the menu they have a nice section to choose from they are a little pricey and portion could be a little larger but all in all its not a bad place

My 5 star rating dropped to a 3.  The crab Rangoon used to be the best I ever had. Now it seemed like freezer quality. It was chewy and nothing like they used to have. Their chicken fried rice is still excellent!

I have been here 3 times and it's always the same. My appointment is scheduled at 9:50am and it's 10:40am and still have not been seen. I hear and see workers talking and mingling as if there's not patients waiting to be seen. This is ridiculous.

Its cheap and they deliver. Its tasty too. This is real good "garbage" food. I've enjoyed a burger, fries, chicken fingers, and a hoagie from this place and felt the way I do after eating most corner take out food. I'll hit them up again. 

If you use campusfoods.com they usually have some sort of coupon or web special.

Sixteen years ago I adopted the best dog in the whole world. Found in cage number 11, he barked and smiled and barked some more and it was love at first sight. But, the SPCA did not want to let me adopt him. I was young, I rented an apartment, I did not have a property deed.

It is understandable to want to ensure that a pet will have a good home. And perhaps promises of undying love and devotion are not enough to warrant the transfer of a dog from a shelter to a stranger. But they made me jump through many hoops: copies of my lease; wanting to talk to my landlord (before cell phones made this possible at the times they were open.) And, they were not very nice. Rude, dismissive, too busy to be bothered, annoyed. Three times I visited hoping to adopt him. And next to me were homeowners (this seemed to be the key) looking at a dog. They clearly stated, "If he doesn't work out we can just bring him back." 

It was unbelievable that these people, elderly but possessing a property deed, were able to be so brazen about their lack of commitment and still allowed to adopt the dog.

Well, the short side of the story is that I did what all young girls are tempted to do when they feel mistreated. I called my father. I am not sure what he did, or who he talked to, but on the fourth day and fourth attempt to adopt Kota, I was granted the privilege of taking him home. We have been together ever since. And I am very thankful to my father for his mysterious assistance.

Just recently, 16 years later, I found a dog running lose, trailing his leash behind him in Media. Of course, I grabbed him before he ran into traffic on State Street and proceeded to ask everyone I saw if they knew the dog. Then Sam and I spent several hours going from place to place, pet store, emergency vet, etc. to see if anyone knew where he lived, if he had a micro chip, etc.

The Del. Co. SPCA was our last choice. Funny, that ideally it should have been our first choice. But the sentiment was consistent at each place we visited. Perhaps better to keep the dog for a few days and post signs than to drop him off there...

In the end we had no choice. We walked into the SPCA and were completely ignored as the staff talked amongst themselves commenting on a recent client...negatively in front of other clients. They seemed disorganized and annoyed (still!) And there Sam and I stood wtih a little dog in our arms...waiting...waiting. Finally we had to be rude to get someone's attention. (What did they think we wanted standing there with this dog anyway?) 

There is a happy ending. Someone realized she had taken a "Lost Dog" call for the dog we had found. The owners were called and we volunteered to drive the dog home. He never had to be checked into or checked out of the SPCA. It would have been hard to leave him there.

If people love animals and want to work with them, I would hope that they would like people who also loved animals and are trying to help them. But it seemed there is no protocol to dealing with people, or communicating, or being helpful. A place to adopt animals should be much friendlier, perhaps cleaner, perhaps more organized.

Just tried their donuts last Sunday and omg so GOOD. Perfect density and texture. Their frosting doesn't taste fake. I assume it is made from scratch? I highly recommend this place especially the prices! Win win :)

This place is great! I work two blocks from here and I stumbled across it looking for a place to eat lunch one day. I have returned several times since and it never fails to satisfy. I recommend everything on the menu because they have something for everyone. Love burgers? Their "Big Sexy Burger." Is probably the best in the city especially for the price. Great selection of salads too, which is wonderful because you can't find too many salads around the area besides boring house salads. I recommend the spinach salad they have. A must for locals and people visiting the city looking for a not-so-touristy spot.

Well.. we came here in between dinner and the next stop with high hopes for a great cocktail. The smell is very odd. At first I wasn't sure if it was who I was sitting next to, the bar mats, or the entire space. It's the space. 

After waiting a good ten minutes for anyone to acknowledge us, the bartender was extremely short and unhelpful. I appreciate the fact there are not tons of printed menus laying around, however due to the bar being long and slim, not everyone can read the ONE drink board. When asking about a recommendation, I was promptly told to go read the board. Awkward AF standing at someone's table to get close enough to even read in a dark crowded bar. Anywho.

After all that, decided to go with an Old Fashioned. So much bitters, it was completely unpalatable. It's a rare day that I will leave an unfinished drink, and this was that day. Could not even choke it down. 

Based on the other reviews, I may try this spot again on the event this was a one off experience.

I love this place. It is just up the road from me, so it has become the preferred spot for dinner with my dad, lunch when I work from home, or drinks with friends. The bartenders are great, the food is good (great sandwiches, decent enough main entrees), the beer selection is very good (I love that they have Chimay), and the new outdoor area is great -- especially now that spring is here.

What a great area right outside of downtown Nashville. We found this area on our last day. The area has a great area of dining options. The staff here were super friendly and quick to greet you when you walked in. The food was outstanding! We shared the bonuts with other guests at our table and made friends.
Shari took good care of my hair. The staff is endearing and polite. I will be going back for sure. :)

This place sucks on foenem grave sum lil girl that looks like wendys girl cuz she has red hair her name tag said Jaime she was rude to me because I couldn't speak English cuz I speak Portuguese my friend help me type this. But I never returning here with my slatts  on gang.

With varieties like "Are you there, God? It's me, Margarita" and "I'm soy excited," East Nashville's Pied Piper Creamery proves you don't have to go to a major chain to get ice cream as cute as it is delicious.

Pied Piper, located next door to Beyond the Edge in East Nashville's Five Points district, offers several flavors of homemade ice cream ranging from the conventional to the creative.  They offer most of the cones, toppings, and flavors you'll find at Baskin Robbins (et al.) at a reasonable price.

But even more enticing than the ice cream (if you can believe it) is the atmosphere.  Pied Piper is located on the ground floor of what looks to the untrained eye like just another gentrified East Nashville home.  Outside you'll find a cozy and inviting porch perfect for Sunday afternoon lounging.  And inside, visitors are welcome to make themselves at home in a kid-friendly sitting area complete with a used book exchange.

With a friendly and talkative staff that is happy to make custom-order cakes, Pied Piper Creamery is just like one of those old fashioned ice cream parlors your grandpa always talks about...only more hip.

Their Chicken Rice soup literally nursed my Mom back to health. She was in the hospital for 7 days and all she wanted was the chicken soup from new china. They offer it with noodles or rice. It's delicious. Thank you New China for helping my Mom recover from her illness.

So cute! I stopped in to grab a little box of chocolates for a gift-sharing party, and I was not disappointed. They are beautifully crafted with some really awesome combinations, including of the spiked variety. Friendly peeps and some other really wonderful items that were a little outside of my price range, but would certainly make a nice gift. It helps that it's right next to Apo, which is another establishment that specializes in green stuff. 

The coolest part of the store has to be the large glass window in the back through which you can watch people making the chocolates.

This place is overall okay, but definitely not the best Asian restaurant. The dumpling soup broth was watered down kind off tasteless, but the dumplings were good. The chow fun was alright.The mints you can take when you walk out were good and not to minty (I like less minty mints). The place was relatively clean and the server was very nice. There was a crowd that was loud that I didn't like. (But I mean what can I do about that). So overall this place is okay. I wouldn't go out of my way to go to this place though.

I will start by saying that it was one of the worst service experiences I have EVER had.  The waitress seemed to not only try to rush us, but forgot about us. She seemed bothered that we had questions about the meals. The drinks and food were average for an airport. 
I know airport service is not exactly supposed to be the best service, but this was just down right wrong.
Tip- Go to Taco Bron instead better food and service.

What a disappointment. Poor service and lack of ingredients. One of the two employees was making salads while the other preened at the register. Only half of the ingredients for the Thai salad were available, but it was only after I paid that the salad-istas bothered to say that anything other than than chicken was missing. First off, how has the chicken run out?! No replenishment of chicken in sight. No cucumber. No avocado for another patron. I'm glad I paid over $10 for a spinach and carrot salad. When I asked to speak to the manager, they said he/she was in the other terminal. I asked if the manager was en route. They said "someone" could call the manager but didn't bother to do it themselves. They were completely uninterested in providing remotely acceptable customer service. Now I'm sitting on my plane with a sad, sad salad that I didn't have time to discuss with the mythical manager. Well done, City Greens - transporting your dissatisfied patrons to another state is an excellent business model.
I am not a fan of "regular" fried chicken but I will go to Southern every chance that I get.  Best chicken!  Medium is plenty spicy (and I  love spicy).  Try the gumbo - some of the best

You know...we stopped in because we saw a bottomless mimosas sign, and it was an excellent decision! B took excellent care of us keeping the champagne coming, and they even surprised my friend with a birthday dessert! It was a great spot to just chill and laugh and drink on a Saturday afternoon.

I stopped by this small bakery to get a Cuban sandwich and cortadito. They sell pastry items, cakes, breads, sandwiches, coffee, all to go. There's no place to sit and eat inside. 

Having said that, the Cuban sandwich ($5.95) was decent, the ham was no too salty however there was very little pork in the sandwich. They don't add salami which is great. They do slap a good amount of butter on the outer part of the bread before pressing it down. The best part though was the cortadito.  It was perfection, not too sweet and just dark/strong enough. 

Parking can be a bit tight in this small shopping plaza which has one way traffic only.
Did the tour with Elizabeth O today and it was great! She was amazing, super informative and extremely kind. Thank you for such a great experience

big bucks to cancel .. no notice regarding renewal..
 look for a gym with out a fee.  costs more to cancel watch out!  extra super friendly staff

I've become spoiled and will probably never get Thai food from any other restaurant. I've been to this place at least 5 times in the past year, and my girlfriend believes she may have put the entire staff through college. Yeah, we think it's that good. 

They make a really strong, dark thai iced tea that pairs so perfectly with our favorite curries. She's a fan of the panang, while I am obsessed with the pumpkin red curry (with chicken). If you go on a Saturday you'll get the chef who likes to make everything wicked spicy, which is exactly what we are into. The apps are good, if small for the price, but the peanut sauce for the satay is really delicious. The staff is really friendly and always ready to refill a drink or bus dishes when you're done so you have plenty of room on the table. 

Try it, you won't be disappointed!
Try the Red Goose Martini-- the ginger in it is unique and delightful.
Great place to get your phone repaired, these guys are honest reliable and do the job right the first time. Will be going back here whenever I need my phone fixed in the future

We went on Saturday night, just 2 of us, and was many parking spots outside but was very surprised to hear of over an hour wait.  We found 2 spots at the bar so we decided to eat there.  The bartender was excellent once we realized she was pretty much the ONLY one there serving the 12 or so bar spots along with all the waiters orders for their tables!  She suggested the Miso glazed salmon and it was AWESOME!  My husband loved his too.  Shame that this poor girl was alone but she worked  her butt off serving everyone.  I sure hope that they don't normally only have 1 bartender and maybe someone called in sick but it was a shame.  She was a trooper and worked very hard and that made it a great experience for us!

The vibe I get from Dominick's is very old neighborhood-friendly, relaxed, and intimate. I heard their pizza was good, so I wanted to try it out. My boyfriend insisted on waiting for a table in the dining room (a little more quiet and romantic than the bar area), but they had NCAA on the TVs in the bar, so he spent a good chunk of the evening staring out that way (eye roll). But that's neither here nor there!

I got the impression our server was overwhelmed, but she still made every effort to ensure that we were taken care of. Another server brought us drinks and bread. The service was very good, and all the staff were very friendly and warm. The little complimentary garlic knots were good. It was hard not to eat too many.

We ordered a Dominick's chopped salad to share, which was a good amount for an appetizer, but if that's all you're eating, you'd definitely want your own. We got a large Dominick's Special pizza, and we probably should've ordered a smaller pie. We ended up with a lot of leftovers. The pizza was good, but I would order a different kind or build my own with only a couple toppings next time. If you love a lot of toppings on your pizza, go for it, but it was too much for me. In my opinion, when you pile on too many toppings, the pie is too soggy. Overall, good experience. I would return.
Friendly staff, big cheesesteak selection, beer- word

CELIACS THIS IS A SAFE PLACE TO EAT ON CAMPUS. Gluten free friendly.
I sometimes get stuck on campus all day because of my weird class schedule and I found this place.
The food is pretty good and it comes out quick.
There are limited gluten free options directly on campus and the ones at the student store are normally not the best or overpriced. 
I eat here probably 1-2x a week with no complaints.
Typically order the wahoo chicken bowl. If you need a gluten free menu they have one behind the counter.

It is a hot dog stand with a simple menu.  You don't need a lot of items on a menu to be good.  You have few options and they do it well.  Try the different options and pick your favorite. I like their chili cheese hot dogs. My wife likes the sauerkraut.

The Logan is in the Curio group of the Hilton chain. It is somewhat of a stodgy big city hotel that has probably been around for many decades. As a NY kind of person it reminds me of the Waldorf Astoria. It is located in the heart of downtown Philly, close to UPenn and Drexel University and there is absolutely no on street parking or even a self park lot. 

The bathroom in my unit had a stone sink counter with large crack across it, almost seem like someone had sat on it. I also thought the floors was slippery, especially when wet, so I can imagine how the crack happened.

The place is expensive, but that's what you expect in a downtown hotel.They charged me $58 for a night to park my vehicle and my room rate was nearly $300. The bar was also pricey, the ten of us had a round of drinks for about $175

Spent three hours there yesterday with family.  Purchased the annual family pass, Mammoth pass. Kids loved the WWI exhibit and the Aboriginal exhibits. Us two adults found the exhibits to be nicely done. Perhaps they could have added a bit more text on the displays - perhaps build a smartphone app to go with the exhibits? Had hot dogs and chili for snacks. Recommend their cafe

Cat's Meow is the best place for karaoke in the Quarter.  They have an interactive host who encourages participation and performance from the crowd, the rotation moves pretty quickly, there are props (hats, boas, costumes, etc.) to help you "enhance" your performance, and they have 3-for-1 beers!  The 3-for-1 isn't really all that great a deal.  They're really forcing you to buy three (for like $12) when you really want just one.  The place smells like vomit, and there's usually lots of smoking going on.  If you can get over that, then you'll have a great time.  What I really like about this place is that there is always a variety of types there -- guys in suits who just got off work, cougars after prey, guys who really think they are Prince, naive 20-somethings... it's a place everybody can have fun.
Went here for my birthday and left the restaurant more than satisfied! Their boba drinks are tasty and the costumer service was exceptional! Great quality meats and a good time for sure!

This place used to be a lot better, but now the food is barely Asian. It's been under new management who tries too hard to cater to Tucson's non-Asian customer base. All their sushi rolls are either deep fried, stuffed with cream cheese, topped with jalapeno, or all of the above. They got rid of their AYCE Korean bbq and grills and now all their hot dishes taste flavorless and burnt. I understand that they are short-staffed and they have a lot of new people, but many times my server wouldn't check on my table because he or she would be too busy flirting up the hosts and hostesses. They don't answer their business phone line anymore. I called 40 times (I kid you not) on my way from work to place an order so that the food would be ready to pick up once I got there, with no answer each time. I finally got to the restaurant and walked in to see two hostesses chatting at the desk. I asked them if their phone was working and they told me they weren't answering anymore due to short staff. It would have been nice if they put that on their website or in a voicemail greeting or a sign. But I suppose they can just do what they want now.

My sister worked here for a while and they gave her no benefits nor perks. She would smuggle a bite to eat in the back every night because they wouldn't give her opportunity to eat or drink. The supervisor treated her decently, but the rest of the wait staff treated her badly, often making her clean up after their messes. She quit after only a few weeks. I used to love this place - they used to have fresh, affordable sushi, and this was the weekend hangout for Korean bbq. Now, I don't think I would come back.

How have I attended Butler University for five semesters and am just now visiting Illinois Food Emporium for the first time?! This place is incredible!

First of all, the service was impeccable.. I accidentally misread the very clearly presented menu, and ordered a breakfast sandwich containing meat. (It was before 8 AM, people, and I am not usually a morning person..) No problem! The wonderful lady behind the counter had a new sandwich prepared for me in a matter of minutes.

At first, I was skeptical of the price, but when they brought out my sandwich(es).. Well, a picture's worth a thousand words; it came with two biscuits, and the taste matched the service brought it to me! Well worth the money, to say the least.

I will 100% be returning to Illinois Food Emporium! (Maybe later in the day, when I've had enough time to wake up and read the menu..)

Prior to this past weekend I hadn't been to Coda since August 2015 when I took in a show by my forever fave, Rusted Root. The sound was incredible, the standing room only venue allowed even this short Mama to see from anywhere in the general admission floor plan, average brews were reasonably priced, and hanging with my friends in the band was super chill here as this is more laid back venue. 

This weekend we attended a family friendly yoga and instrumental ensemble retreat put on by the incomparable Daniel Cordua of Palo Santo right here in Philly, and sponsored Lululemon on also on Walnut. This put Coda back on my radar! 

The space is very versatile. It's wide open with city vibes thanks to the hand painted trippy, graffiti murals. It has a stunning chandelier above, and serves and a perfectly blended masculine/feminine urban, chic backdrop to anything...parties, concerts, clubbing, social gatherings, you name it. 

While Coda hosts many up and coming and indie artists, as well as many dj's, there unfortunately hasn't been many of my personal faves come through which is the sole reason for my infrequent visits, but I'll keep my eyes peeled because I really dig the venue, the location and overall vibes.

Coda is kind of hidden in plain sight on Walnut. You've probably walked passed while strolling the Rittenhouse area and never even noticed it! It's so easily accessible by public transportation, Uber and parking at off hours when events are usually held is a cinch right there on Walnut. Kiosk meter during posted hours. 

Ticket prices for concerts I feel are more reasonable here than many other venues in the city also. They do have a VIP section on the balcony which is more pricey. I don't find it necessary though. 

I wouldn't hesitate to return to a show here in the future, in fact, I look forward to it. I believe many of the negative reviews are for the club nights which I can't speak about. For me, it's been all positive. Maybe stick with concerts?

Was there a week ago on a Sunday night  with about 10 people.  When we arrived it was almost empty. Our drink orders were taken right away as we waited for everyone to arrive  drinks were delivered right away  the background music is so loud we had to go and stand beside the people at the other end of the table and then the lights were dimmed so low that in the seat I had I could  not even read the menu.  This isn't ambience. It's annoying. We had ordered 2 nachos to start and despite there being no crowd in the place they took forever  the nachos here are a kind of novelty but the portions are small and I found them greasy. Our meals came sporadically. Again in a mostly empty restaurant I'm not sure why the kitchen didn't have its act together  I had the perogy dish. The perogies were fine.
